clauses.head: 2. Purchase Price. The total purchase price for
clauses.name: 2. Purchase Price — Total Price

clauses.head: At Closing, the sum of $8,000,000 (Eight Million
clauses.name: 2. Purchase Price — Closing Payment
clauses.tail: inclusive of utility and real estate tax prorations).
clauses.text: At Closing, the sum of $8,000,000 (Eight Million Dollars) shall be due and payable to the Seller plus or minus any standard deductions and prorations (customary closing expenses incurred by the Seller inclusive of utility and real estate tax prorations).

clauses.head: The remaining balance less any deductions identified below
clauses.name: 2. Purchase Price — Outstanding Balance Payments
clauses.tail: setoffs as described below) are received (“Outstanding Balance”).
clauses.text: The remaining balance less any deductions identified below shall be paid to the Seller at a rate of 10% of the annual tax incremental financing reimbursement received by Buyer, For example, the anticipated annual Tax Incremental Financing [TIF] amount is approximately $2,000,000 of which an estimated $200,000 shall be paid to 1200 6"" Street, LLC, annually, and shall become due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt of same until the remaining $1,000,000 (One Million Dollars) (or less dependent upon setoffs as described below) are received (“Outstanding Balance”).

clauses.head: The Outstanding Balance shall accrue interest to the
clauses.name: 2. Purchase Price — Interest
clauses.tail: expenses and which shall be paid to Seller.
clauses.text: The Outstanding Balance shall accrue interest to the same extent, if any, that either or both the City of Detroit or the State of Michigan pay interest to the Buyer on the outstanding incurred eligible expenses and which shall be paid to Seller.

clauses.head: In the event the sale is consummated, and
clauses.name: 2. Purchase Price — Tax Incremental Reimbursement
clauses.tail: tax incremental reimbursement shall belong to the Buyer.
clauses.text: In the event the sale is consummated, and subject to repayment of the Outstanding Balance owed to 1200 6™ Street, LLC (less any deductions) the tax incremental reimbursement shall belong to the Buyer.

clauses.name: 3. Deed

clauses.text: 3. Deed. The Seller, at the time of closing of title, shall execute and deliver to the Buyer, a warranty deed containing the new legal descriptions which reflect the City of Detroit’s final approved plat of vacation and dedication of right of way necessary to affect the Buyer’s desired street closures, and the contiguous properties created as a result of vacating Sixth Street and Abbott Street, in customary form, consistent with statutory requirements, conveying good and marketable indefeasible fee simple title to the Property free from any and all liens or encumbrances, subject only to those items identified in the Real Estate Option Agreement dated between 1200 Sixth Street, LLC and GSA as permitted exceptions ("Permitted Exceptions").

clauses.head: 4. Title. No Later than thirty (30) days

clauses.head: If the Title Commitment discloses exceptions to title
clauses.name: 4. Title — Removal of Exceptions
clauses.tail: that may be caused by such unpermitted exceptions.
clauses.text: If the Title Commitment discloses exceptions to title other than those Permitted Exceptions attached hereto or otherwise approved by Buyer in writing, then Seller, at Seller's sole expense, shall have ten (10) business days prior to the date of Closing, to have such unpermitted exceptions removed from title or to cause the Title Company to commit to issue an endorsement insuring Buyer against loss or damage to Buyer that may be caused by such unpermitted exceptions.

clauses.head: If Seller is unable to have such unpermitted
clauses.name: 4. Title — Buyer's Election
clauses.tail: shall then be deemed to be Permitted Exceptions.
clauses.text: If Seller is unable to have such unpermitted exceptions removed from the Title Commitment or endorsed over, Buyer may elect, prior to the expiration of the period for Seller to remedy such unpermitted exceptions, to either (a) terminate this Agreement by written notice to Seller or (b) accept title to the Property subject to the Permitted Exceptions and such unpermitted exceptions which shall then be deemed to be Permitted Exceptions.

clauses.head: On the date of closing of title, the
clauses.name: 4. Title — Title Policy
clauses.tail: of title, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions.
clauses.text: On the date of closing of title, the Title Company shall issue an owner's title insurance policy or title commitment therefore, pursuant to and in accordance with the Title Commitment in the amount of the Purchase. Price insuring the fee simple title to the Property in the Buyer as of the date of closing of title, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions.

clauses.head: 5, Survey. Provided this agreement shall have been
clauses.name: 5, Survey

clauses.text: 5, Survey. Provided this agreement shall have been executed by Seller and Buyer, Seller will deliver to Buyer, an updated final plat of survey of the Property which shall reflect the City of Detroit’s final approved plat of vacation and dedication of right of way, describing the immediate contiguous properties created as a result of vacating Sixth Street and Abbott Street, as a prepared in accordance with the 2005 ALTA standards and certified as such to the Buyer, its lender, and the Title Company.

clauses.head: 6, Condition of Property. Buyer acknowledges that prior
clauses.name: 6, Condition of Property — Investigation and Acceptance
clauses.tail: orders, ordinances, regulations relating, in any manner, thereto.
clauses.text: 6, Condition of Property. Buyer acknowledges that prior to the date of this Agreement, Buyer has had the opportunity to make a complete and independent investigation of all facts and data which Buyer deems necessary in its decisions to acquire the Property, including, without limitation, all the facts and data pertaining to environmental conditions at, in, or, under, or affecting the Property and does hereby accept the Property subject to all federal, state, county, and municipal laws, requirements, rules, orders, ordinances, regulations relating, in any manner, thereto.

clauses.head: Buyer further acknowledges that it has inspected the
clauses.name: 6, Condition of Property — Inspection
clauses.tail: as expressly set forth elsewhere in the Agreement.
clauses.text: Buyer further acknowledges that it has inspected the Property or caused an inspection to be made thereof on Buyer's behalf and is familiar with the physical condition thereof except as expressly set forth elsewhere in the Agreement.

clauses.head: Buyer agrees to accept the Property in the
clauses.name: 6, Condition of Property — As-Is Acceptance
clauses.tail: or patent and whether now or hereafter existing.
clauses.text: Buyer agrees to accept the Property in the condition existing on the date of closing of title, including all faults of every kind and nature whatsoever whether latent or patent and whether now or hereafter existing.

clauses.head: 7. seller's Representations. Seller covenants and represents to
clauses.name: 7(a) seller's Representations — Ownership and Authority
clauses.tail: and the sale of the Property contemplated herein.
clauses.text: 7. seller's Representations. Seller covenants and represents to Buyer: (a) Seller is the record owner of the Property and has the requisite power and authority to enter into and fully carry out this Agreement and the sale of the Property contemplated herein.

clauses.head: (b) It has no knowledge of any teason
clauses.name: 7(b) Development and Title
clauses.tail: arise or be set up adverse to Seller.
clauses.text: (b) It has no knowledge of any teason why the local governmental authorities would not allow the Property to be developed for the Federal Office facilities contemplated herein; that possession of the land has been peaceable and undisturbed; that Seller's title to the Property has never been disputed or questioned to its knowledge; nor does Seller know of any facts by reason of which said possession or title might be disturbed or questioned, or by reason of which any claim to the Property, or any part thereof might arise or be set up adverse to Seller.

clauses.head: (c) Electricity, telephone, sewer, and water utilities have
clauses.name: 7(c) Utilities
clauses.tail: charge, assessment or apparatus for its current use.
clauses.text: (c) Electricity, telephone, sewer, and water utilities have been installed within the adjacent public right of ways and are of sufficient size, capacity and are available for immediate connection at the Property without any special charge, assessment or apparatus for its current use.

clauses.head: (d) Seller has disclosed that the property is
clauses.name: 7(d) Environmental Facility Disclosure
clauses.tail: in the environmental reports Seller provided to Buyer.
clauses.text: (d) Seller has disclosed that the property is a “facility” as defined by MCL 324.20101 et seq. due to the property's historic uses described in the environmental reports Seller provided to Buyer.

clauses.head: Seller also represents that it has provided all
clauses.name: 7(d) Environmental Information
clauses.tail: of asbestos containing materials located in existing structures.
clauses.text: Seller also represents that it has provided all environmental information that it has with respect to the environmental condition of the Property including the existence of asbestos containing materials located in existing structures.

clauses.head: (e) Except as otherwise indicated on Schedule A
clauses.name: 7(e) Environmental Representations
clauses.tail: exemption as defined and in CERCLA, as amended.
clauses.text: (e) Except as otherwise indicated on Schedule A attached, or as described in paragraph 7 (d) of this agreement, to the best of Seller’s actual knowledge: (1) — that since Seller acquired an interest in the property, Seller has been in compliance with all federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations, ordinances, codes and orders governing, establishing, limiting or otherwise affecting the discharge or disposal of hazardous substances or hazardous waste; (2) that the property has not been used since the time Seller acquired any interest in the property for storage, disposal, deposit, treatment, or recycling of toxic, dangerous or hazardous substances; (3) that in the event that any subsequent purchaser of the property avails itself of the available statutory exemptions from environmental liability, there are no activities on the property which would subject an owner thereof to damages, penalties, injunctive relief or clean-up costs under any federal, state or local law or under any civil action respecting hazardous substances on the property. The exemptions include that owner’s obligations to comply with its due care requirements as stated in MCL 324.20107a, its obtaining a Baseline Environmental Site Assessment under MCL 324.20101 et seq. and compliance with the All Appropriate Inquiry exemption as defined and in CERCLA, as amended.

clauses.head: Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer that
clauses.name: 7. Continuing Representations and Warranties
clauses.tail: be true and correct on each day hereafter.
clauses.text: Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer that the above representations are true and correct as of the date hereof and will continue to be true and correct on each day hereafter.

(a) Subject to any termination of this Agreement permitted hereunder by Buyer or Seller, closing ("Closing") shall take place at the office of the Title Company on a mutually agreeable date, but, in no event later than ninety (90) days after the execution of this Agreement.

clauses.head: Buyer shall cause the Purchase Price, plus or

clauses.head: Seller shall execute and deliver a recordable Warranty
clauses.name: 8(a)(ii) Delivery of Warranty Deed

clauses.text: Seller shall execute and deliver a recordable Warranty Deed as provided for in Section 3, conveying title to the Property to Buyer, subject to the Permitted Exceptions, and any exceptions created or suffered by Buyer.

clauses.head: Seller and Buyer shall] execute such other documentation

clauses.text: Seller and Buyer shall] execute such other documentation as is required by applicable law to effectuate the transaction contemplated hereby, and such other documentation as is reasonably required by the Title Company to issue the title policy(ies) in accordance with Section 4 hereof, including, without limitation, ALTA statements and GAP undertakings, if required the Title Company. This Section 8(a)(v) shall not require Buyer or Seller to incur any extraordinary obligations at the request of the Title Company.

clauses.text: (b) At the request of either party, the transaction contemplated hereby shall be closed in escrow, with the concurrent delivery of the documents of title, transfer of interests, delivery of the Title Policy and the payment of the Purchase Price.

clauses.head: Buyer and Seller shall each provide undertakings to
clauses.name: 8(b) Escrow Undertakings

clauses.text: Seller and Buyer shall each pay 50% of any Closing escrow fees and the charges of the Title Company for such closing.

clauses.head: 9, Prorations. All real estate taxes, expenses and
clauses.name: 9, Prorations — Closing Proration
clauses.tail: of the Property shall be prorated at Closing.
clauses.text: 9, Prorations. All real estate taxes, expenses and charges in connection with ownership and use of the Property shall be prorated at Closing.

clauses.head: To the extent that information for any such

clauses.head: 10. Default. If Seller fails or refuses to
clauses.name: 10. Default — Seller Default

clauses.text: 10. Default. If Seller fails or refuses to comply with the terms of this Agreement within five (5) days of receipt by Seller of written notice of such default, for any reason other than Buyer's default hereunder, Buyer may (a) sue Seller for the specific performance of this Agreement if such suit for specific performance is commenced within ninety (90) days after the date of Seller's failure or refusal to comply with the terms of this Agreement, or (b) may sue Seller for actual damages.

clauses.head: If Buyer fails or refuses to comply with
clauses.name: 10. Default — Buyer Default and Liquidated Damages
clauses.tail: Award and Assignment of the Option to Purchase.
clauses.text: If Buyer fails or refuses to comply with the terms of this Agreement within five (5) days of receipt by Buyer of written notice of such default for any reason other than Seller's default hereunder; Seller is entitled to, as liquidated damages not to exceed $50,000, either a $50,000 fetter of credit or cash equivalent (at Buyer’s option) which the Buyer is required to obtain or place in escrow, upon the execution of this Agreement and within ten (10) business days of Award and Assignment of the Option to Purchase.

clauses.head: In the event the Assignment to the Buyer
clauses.name: 10. Default — Revocation of Assignment
clauses.tail: the $50,000 letter of credit or cash equivalent.
clauses.text: In the event the Assignment to the Buyer is revoked by the United States of America, acting by and through the U.S. General Services Administration, the Buyer is entitled to the $50,000 letter of credit or cash equivalent.

clauses.head: Any subsequent Buyer is required to obtain, a
clauses.name: 10. Default — Subsequent Buyer Security
clauses.tail: Award and Assignment of the Option to Purchase.
clauses.text: Any subsequent Buyer is required to obtain, a $50,000 letter of credit or cash equivalent (at Buyer’s option) upon the execution of this Agreement and within ten (10) business days of Award and Assignment of the Option to Purchase.

clauses.head: In addition, the parties may seek any other remedy available at law or in equity.
clauses.name: 10. Default — Other Remedies
clauses.text: In addition, the parties may seek any other remedy available at law or in equity.

clauses.text: 11. Risk of Loss. The risk of loss or damage to the Property, if any, including but not limited to the buildings and other improvements; if any, by fire, the elements, or otherwise until the delivery of the deed hereunder is assumed by the Seller.

clauses.head: In case the property shall suffer injury beyond
clauses.name: 11. Risk of Loss — Repair or Deduction
clauses.tail: from the purchase price provided in Section 2.
clauses.text: In case the property shall suffer injury beyond the ordinary wear and tear, the Seller shall repair the damage before the date set for delivery of the deed or make an appropriate deduction from the purchase price provided in Section 2.

clauses.head: 12. Condemnation. In the event of any taking
clauses.name: 12. Condemnation — Substantial Taking
clauses.tail: Buyer of written notification of any such condemnation.
clauses.text: 12. Condemnation. In the event of any taking by the exercise of the power of eminent domain of a substantial portion of the Property prior to Closing (such portion as would impair or otherwise affect the intended use of the Real Property will be deemed substantial). Buyer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement by giving written notice to Seller within ten (10) days after receipt by Buyer of written notification of any such condemnation.

clauses.head: If Buyer elects to terminate this Agreement, all
clauses.name: 12. Condemnation — Termination Awards
clauses.tail: said condemnation shall be the property of Seller.
clauses.text: If Buyer elects to terminate this Agreement, all awards and compensation arising out of said condemnation shall be the property of Seller.

clauses.head: If Buyer fails to give Seller written notice
clauses.name: 12. Condemnation — Waiver and Assignment
clauses.tail: Property with no reduction in the Purchase Price.
clauses.text: If Buyer fails to give Seller written notice of termination within said ten (10) day period, said right to terminate shall be deemed waived and Buyer shall be credited with or assigned all of Seller's right, title and interest to all awards and compensation arising out of said condemnation, and Buyer shall remain obligated to purchase the Property with no reduction in the Purchase Price.

clauses.head: In the event of any taking of an
clauses.name: 12. Condemnation — Insubstantial Taking
clauses.tail: Property with no reduction in the Purchase Price.
clauses.text: In the event of any taking of an insubstantial portion of the Property prior to the Closing Date (such portion as would not impair or otherwise affect the intended use of the Property will be deemed insubstantial), Seller shall assign to Buyer all of Seller's right, title and interest to all awards and compensation therefore and Buyer shall remain obligated to purchase the Property with no reduction in the Purchase Price.

clauses.head: 13. Buyer's Right to Enter and Inspect the
clauses.name: 13. Buyer's Right to Enter and Inspect the Property
clauses.tail: the Property as a leasehold for Federal facilities.
clauses.text: 13. Buyer's Right to Enter and Inspect the Property The Buyer's authorized or ' designated representatives or agents, or offerors participating in the lease procurement process of the Buyer, shall have the right during the period of this Option including any extension periods subject to the rights, interests, and uses made of the Property by the Seller, to enter upon the Property for the purpose of inspecting same and making test borings, plans, topographical and boundary Surveys, environmental assessments, and any other due diligence matters deemed reasonably prudent in connection with the contemplated use of the Property as a leasehold for Federal facilities.

clauses.head: Optionee shall require any of said parties to

clauses.text: Optionee shall provide Optionor reasonable notice prior to entering the Property.

clauses.head: 15. Brokerage. Each party hereby represents and warrants
clauses.name: 15. Brokerage

clauses.head: 17. Time is of the Essence. Buyer and
clauses.name: 17. Time is of the Essence
clauses.tail: provision hereof in which time is an element.

clauses.head: No extension of time for performance of any
clauses.name: 17. No Implied Extension
clauses.tail: for performance of any other obligations or acts.

clauses.text: If any date for performance of any of the terms, conditions, or provisions hereof shall fall on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, then the time of such performance shall be extended to the next business day thereafter.

clauses.head: 18. Paragraph or Section Headings. The paragraph headings
clauses.name: 18. Paragraph or Section Headings
clauses.tail: meaning of the various and several paragraphs hereof.
clauses.text: 18. Paragraph or Section Headings. The paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall in no way enlarge or limit the scope or meaning of the various and several paragraphs hereof.

clauses.head: 19. Interpretation. Whenever used in this Agreement, the
clauses.name: 19. Interpretation
clauses.tail: use of any gender shall include all genders.
clauses.text: 19. Interpretation. Whenever used in this Agreement, the singular number shall include the plural, the plural the singular, and the use of any gender shall include all genders.

clauses.name: 20. Applicable Law and Parties Bound

This Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the state in which the Property is located and shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, legal representatives, successors and permitted assigns.

clauses.head: 21. Attorney's Fees. In the event either party
clauses.name: 21. Attorney's Fees
clauses.tail: as a result thereof from the losing party.

clauses.head: 22. Amendments. All amendments and/or supplements to this
clauses.name: 22. Amendments — Writing and Execution
clauses.tail: in writing and executed by each party hereto.
clauses.text: 22. Amendments. All amendments and/or supplements to this Agreement must be in writing and executed by each party hereto.

clauses.head: However, such amendments and/or supplements may be executed
clauses.name: 22. Amendments — Counterparts
clauses.tail: which shall be deemed to constitute one document.
clauses.text: However, such amendments and/or supplements may be executed in counterparts, all of which shall be deemed to constitute one document.

The parties agree that the obligations, representations and warranties herein contained shall not merge with transfer of title but shall survive the Closing and remain in effect until fulfilled, up to and including the time of completion of any improvements to be built thereon and the written acceptance of occupancy of such improvements by the United States of America General services Administration through its designated agent.

clauses.head: 24. Prior Agreements. The parties agree and acknowledge

The parties agree and acknowledge that this Agreement cancels and supersedes all prior agreements, whether written, oral, or both; is entire in itself; and that this Agreement, and that certain Real Estate Option Agreement dated , August, 2006, by and between the United States of America (“Government”) acting by the U.S. General Services Administration (“GSA”) and the Seller-which has been assigned to the Buyer hereunder ("Option ), are the only agreements between parties hereto respecting the Property and its terms of sale; that all agreements and undertakings between the parties are embodied in the Agreement and the Option.

clauses.name: 24. Prior Agreements — No Other Inducements
clauses.tail: any party hereto to enter into this Agreement.

clauses.text: 2.5 Compensation. (a) The initial Broker-Dealer Fee Rate shall equal .25 of 1% per annum as calculated below. The Broker-Dealer Fee for the Series 2004 Auction Bonds shall be paid by the Company to the Auction Agent for the benefit of the Broker-Dealer and represents compensation for the services of the Broker-Dealer in facilitating Auctions for the benefit of the beneficial owners of the Series 2004 Auction Bonds. The Broker-Dealer Fee Rate may be adjusted from time to time with the approval of the Company upon a written request of the Broker-Dealer delivered to the Company.

clauses.head: (b) While the Series 2004 Auction Bonds are
clauses.name: 2.5(b) Broker-Dealer Fee Calculation and Payment
clauses.tail: the Broker-Dealer for such Series 2004 Auction Bonds.
clauses.text: (b) While the Series 2004 Auction Bonds are in an Auction Period other than a daily Auction Period, on each Interest Payment Date following each Auction Date, each Broker- Dealer shall be entitled to receive an amount equal to the product of (x) the Broker-Dealer Fee Rate multiplied by (y)(A) if an Auction was held on such Auction Date, the sum of the aggregate principal amount of Series 2004 Auction Bonds that were (1) the subject of a valid Hold Order of an Existing Owner submitted by such Broker-Dealer, (2) the subject of a Submitted Bid of an Existing Owner submitted by such Broker-Dealer and continued to be held by such Existing Owner as a result of such Auction, (3) the subject of a Submitted Bid of a Potential Owner submitted by such Broker-Dealer and were purchased by such Potential Owner as a result of such Auction and (4) deemed to be the subject of a Hold Order by an Existing Owner that were acquired by such Existing Owner from such Broker-Dealer or (B) if an Auction was not held on such Auction Date, the aggregate principal amount of Outstanding Series 2004 Auction Bonds that were acquired by an Existing Owner through such Broker-Dealer, multiplied by (z) a fraction, the numerator of which is (i) if the Auction Period is seven days, 28 days, 35 days, three months or a Special Auction Period of 180 days or less, the actual number of days in the Auction Period next succeeding such Auction Date or (ii) if the Auction Period is six months or a Special Auction Period of more than 180 days, the number of days in the Auction Period next succeeding -6- such Auction Date calculated on the basis of twelve 30 day months in a year, and in either case the denominator of which is 360. If the Series 2004 Auction Bonds are in a daily Auction Period each Broker- Dealer shall be entitled to receive on each Interest Payment Date an amount equal to the sum calculated for each Auction Period in the preceding month of the product of (x) the Broker- Dealer Fee Rate multiplied by (y) the aggregate principal amount of Series 2004 Auction Bonds for each Auction Period that were (I) the subject of a valid Hold Order submitted by such Broker-Dealer, (2) the subject of a Submitted Bid of an Existing Owner submitted by such Broker-Dealer and continued to be held by such Existing Owner as a result of such Auction, (3) the subject of a Submitted Bid of a Potential Owner submitted by such Broker-Dealer and were purchased by such Potential Owner as a result of such Auction, (4) deemed to be the subject of a Hold Order by an Existing Owner that were acquired by such Existing Owner from such Broker- Dealer and (5) if an Auction was not held for any Auction Period, the aggregate principal amount of Outstanding Series 2004 Auction Bonds that were acquired by an Existing Owner through such Broker-Dealer, multiplied by (z) a fraction, the numerator of which is the number of days in the Auction Period and denominator of which is 360. The Broker-Dealer Fee shall be calculated by the Auction Agent, which shall be conclusive absent manifest error. Such amounts shall be communicated by the Auction Agent to the Company by 4:00 p.m. on the Business Day immediately preceding each Interest Payment Date. On or before 10:00 a.m. on each Interest Payment Date, the Company shall pay to the Auction Agent the amount due to the Broker-Dealer, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to such account as the Auction Agent may designate. The amount constituting the Broker-Dealer Fee shall be held by the Auction Agent on behalf of the Broker-Dealer and, immediately upon receipt of such Fee, the Auction Agent shall deliver such Fee to the Broker- Dealer pursuant to the written instructions of the Broker-Dealer. If any Existing Owner who acquired Series 2004 Auction Bonds through a Broker-Dealer transfers any such Series 2004 Auction Bonds to another Person other than through an Auction, the Broker-Dealer for the Series 2004 Auction Bonds so transferred shall continue to be the Broker-Dealer with respect to such Series 2004 Auction Bonds; provided, however, that if the transfer was effected by, or if the transferee is, another Person who has met the requirements specified in the defmition of"Broker- Dealer" contained in the Series 2004 Auction Bonds and executed a Broker-Dealer Agreement, such Person shall be the Broker-Dealer for such Series 2004 Auction Bonds.

clauses.text: 2.6 Settlement. (a) If any Potential Owner on whose behalf BD has submitted an Order fails to deliver funds with respect to any Auction, BD shall promptly deliver such funds to the party entitled to receive such funds. If any Existing Owner on whose behalf BD has submitted an Order fails to instruct its Agent Member to deliver Series 2004 Auction Bonds subject to such Order against payment therefor, BD shall instruct such Agent Member to deliver such Series 2004 Auction Bonds against payment therefor. The delivery of funds by BD for the purchase of Series 2004 Auction Bonds by a Potential Owner, as provided above, shall not relieve such - 7- Potential Owner of any liability to BD for payment for such Series 2004 Auction Bonds. Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of this Section 2.6(a), any delivery or nondelivery of Series 2004 Auction Bonds which represents any departure from the results of an Auction, as determined by the Auction Agent, shall be of no effect unless and until the Auction Agent shall have been notified of such delivery or non-delivery in accordance with the terms of Section 2.3(d) hereof. The Auction Agent shall have no duty or liability with respect to enforcement of this Section 2.6(a).

This Broker-Dealer Agreement shall be binding upon, inure to the benefit of, and be enforceable by, the respective successors and assigns of BD, the Bond Insurer and the Auction Agent. Nothing in this Broker-Dealer Agreement, express or implied, shall give to any Person, other than the Auction Agent, the Bond Insurer and BD and their respective successors and assigns, any benefit of any legal or equitable right, remedy or claim under this Broker-Dealer Agreement, other than the rights expressly granted to the Issuer herein. clauses.text: This Policy is issued by the stock insurance company identified in the Declarations (hereinafter the Insurer).

clauses.head: THIS POLICY PROVIDES LIABILITY COVERAGE ON A CLAIMS-MADE
clauses.name: Policy — Claims-made and reported coverage
clauses.tail: LIMITS OF LIABILITY AND ANY APPLICABLE SELF-INSURED RETENTION.
clauses.text: THIS POLICY PROVIDES LIABILITY COVERAGE ON A CLAIMS-MADE AND REPORTED BASIS, WHICH COVERS ONLY CLAIMS FIRST MADE AGAINST THE INSURED AND REPORTED TO THE INSURER, IN WRITING, DURING THE POLICY PERIOD. THIS POLICY PROVIDES COVERAGE FOR REMEDIATION COSTS ON A DISCOVERED AND REPORTED BASIS, WHICH COVERS ONLY POLLUTION CONDITIONS FIRST DISCOVERED AND REPORTED TO THE INSURER, IN WRITING, DURING THE POLICY PERIOD. PLEASE READ THIS POLICY CAREFULLY. SOME OF THE PROVISIONS CONTAINED IN THIS POLICY RESTRICT COVERAGE, SPECIFY WHAT 1S AND IS NOT COVERED AND DESIGNATE YOUR RIGHTS AND DUTIES. LEGAL DEFENSE EXPENSES ARE SUBJECT TO AND SHALL ERODE THE LIMITS OF LIABILITY AND ANY APPLICABLE SELF-INSURED RETENTION.

clauses.head: Throughout this Policy the words the Insurer shall
clauses.name: Policy — Defined-word convention
clauses.tail: meanings and are defined in Section V., DEFINITIONS.
clauses.text: Throughout this Policy the words the Insurer shall refer to the company providing this insurance. Other words and phrases that appear in quotation marks have special meanings and are defined in Section V., DEFINITIONS.

clauses.head: In consideration of the payment of the premium
clauses.name: Policy — General insuring agreement
clauses.tail: insurance coverage to the “insured” as described herein.
clauses.text: In consideration of the payment of the premium and in reliance upon all statements made in the Application to this Policy, including the information furnished in connection therewith, and subject to all terms, definitions, conditions, exclusions and limitations of this Policy, the Insurer agrees to provide insurance coverage to the “insured” as described herein.

clauses.head: I. INSURING AGREEMENTS Solely to the extent that
clauses.name: I.A. New Pollution Conditions
clauses.tail: commence, in their entirety, during the “policy period’.
clauses.text: I. INSURING AGREEMENTS Solely to the extent that the Coverages, below, are identified on the Declarations to this Policy as being underwritten by the Insurer, the Insurer agrees to pay on behalf of the “insured” for: A. NEW POLLUTION CONDITIONS (Coverage A.) “Claims”, “remediation costs”, and associated “legal defense expenses’, in excess of the “self-insured retention", arising out of a "pollution condition” on, at, under, or migrating from a “covered location’, provided the “claim” is first made, or the “insured” first discovers such "pollution condition”, during the “policy period”. Any such discovery of a “pollution condition” must be reported to the Insurer, in writing, during the “policy period”. Any such “claim” must be reported to the Insurer, in writing, during the “policy period” or any applicable “extended reporting period”. The coverage afforded pursuant to this Coverage A. only applies to “pollution conditions” that first commence, in their entirety, during the “policy period’.

clauses.head: B. PRE-EXISTING POLLUTION CONDITIONS (Coverage B.) “Claims”,
clauses.name: I.B. Pre-Existing Pollution Conditions
clauses.tail: whole or part, prior to the “policy period”.
clauses.text: B. PRE-EXISTING POLLUTION CONDITIONS (Coverage B.) “Claims”, "remediation costs”, and associated “legal defense expenses”, in excess of the “self-insured retention”, arising out of a “pollution condition” on, at, under, or migrating from a “covered location”, provided the “claim” is first made, or the “insured” first discovers such “pollution condition’, during the “nolicy period”. Any such discovery of a “pollution condition” must be reported to the Insurer, in writing, during the “policy period”. Any such “claim” must be reported to the Insurer, in writing, during the “policy period” or any applicable “extended reporting period”. The coverage afforded pursuant to this Coverage B. only applies to “pollution conditions” that first commenced, in whole or part, prior to the “policy period”.

clauses.head: LIMITS OF LIABILITY AND SELF-INSURED RETENTION A. It
clauses.name: II.A. Attachment of Insurer’s payment obligation
clauses.tail: with respect to coverage sought by any “insured”.
clauses.text: LIMITS OF LIABILITY AND SELF-INSURED RETENTION A. It is expressly agreed that the insurer's obligation to pay for any covered “claims”, “remediation costs” or “legal defense expense" pursuant to this Policy shall attach to the Insurer only after the “first named insured” has paid, or has provided evidence to the Insurer that another “named insured” has paid, the full amount of the “self-insured retention" with respect to any covered “pollution condition". Under no circumstances shall the Insurer be liable to pay any amount within the “self-insured retention”. In the event that the “first named insured” cannot provide satisfactory evidence that a “named insured” has paid the full amount of the “self-insured retention” with respect to any covered "pollution condition”, the “first named insured” shall remain responsible to pay the “self-insured retention” before the Insurer's payment obligation pursuant to this Policy shall attach with respect to coverage sought by any “insured”.

clauses.head: One “self-insured retention” shall apply to all “claims",
clauses.name: II.B. One self-insured retention
clauses.tail: the same, continuous, repeated, or related “pollution condition’.
clauses.text: One “self-insured retention” shall apply to all “claims", “remediation costs” and “legal defense expenses” arising out of the same, continuous, repeated, or related “pollution condition’.

clauses.head: With respect to Coverage A., and subject to
clauses.name: II.C. Coverage A per-condition limit
clauses.tail: identified in Item 2.b. of the Declarations to this Policy.
clauses.text: With respect to Coverage A., and subject to Subsections D., G. and H., below, the most the Insurer shall pay for all “claims”, “remediation costs” and “legal defense expense” arising out of the same, continuous, repeated, or related “poliution condition” is the Limit of Liability identified in Item 2.b. of the Declarations to this Policy.

clauses.head: With respect to Coverage A., and subject to
clauses.name: II.D. Coverage A aggregate limit
clauses.tail: expense” for all “pollution conditions”.
clauses.text: With respect to Coverage A., and subject to Subsection C., above, and Subsections G. and H., below, the Limit of Liability identified in Item 2.c. of the Declarations to this Policy shall be the maximum liability of the Insurer pursuant to this Policy with respect to all “claims”, “remediation costs” and “legal defense expense” for all “pollution conditions”.

clauses.head: With respect to Coverage B., and subject to
clauses.name: II.E. Coverage B per-condition limit
clauses.tail: identified in Item 3.b. of the Declarations to this Policy.
clauses.text: With respect to Coverage B., and subject to Subsections F., G. and H., below, the most the Insurer shall pay for all “claims”, “remediation costs” and “legal defense expense” arising out of the same, continuous, repeated, or related “pollution condition” is the Limit of Liability identified in Item 3.b. of the Declarations to this Policy.

clauses.head: With respect to Coverage B., and subject to
clauses.name: II.F. Coverage B aggregate limit
clauses.tail: expense” for all “pollution conditions”.
clauses.text: With respect to Coverage B., and subject to Subsection E., above, and Subsections G. and H., below, the Limit of Liability identified in Item 3.c. of the Declarations to this Policy shall be the maximum liability of the Insurer pursuant to this Policy with respect to all “claims”, “remediation costs” and “legal defense expense” for all “pollution conditions”.

clauses.head: Subject to Subsections C., D., E. and F.,
clauses.name: II.G. Total Policy Aggregate Limit
clauses.tail: Supplemental Coverages added by endorsement to this Policy, if any.
clauses.text: Subject to Subsections C., D., E. and F., above, the Total Policy Aggregate Limit of Liability identified in Item 4. of the Declarations to this Policy shall be the maximum liability of the Insurer pursuant to this Policy with respect to all “claims”, “remediation costs” and “legal defense expense” for all “pollution conditions” covered pursuant to Coverages A. and B., and any Supplemental Coverages added by endorsement to this Policy, if any.

clauses.head: If the Insurer or an affiliate has issued
clauses.name: II.H. Related pollution conditions and claims
clauses.tail: this “policy period” and no other policy shail respond.
clauses.text: If the Insurer or an affiliate has issued pollution liability coverage afforded on a discovered and reported basis or claims-made and reported basis consistent with Coverages A. or B., herein, in one or more policy periods, and a “pollution condition’ is first discovered and reported to the Insurer, or a “claim” is first made and reported to the Insurer with respect to a “pollution condition’, in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Policy, then: 1. Any continuous, repeated, or related "pollution condition” that is subsequently reported to the Insurer during later policy periods shall be deemed to be one “pollution condition” discovered during this “policy period”; and ny ft 2. All “claims” seeking “bodily injury”, “property damage” or “remediation costs" arising out of: a. That same, continuous, repeated, or related “pollution condition’ that was discovered during this “policy period”; or b. That same, continuous, repeated, or related “pollution condition” that was the subject of a “claim” first made and reported during this “policy period” or any applicable “extended reporting period’, shall be deemed to have been first made and reported during this “policy period” and no other policy shail respond.

clauses.head: lil. DEFENSE AND SETTLEMENT A. The Insurer shall
clauses.name: III.A. Defense duty
clauses.tail: settlement offer as provided in Subsection E., below.
clauses.text: lil. DEFENSE AND SETTLEMENT A. The Insurer shall have the right and, subject to the “self-insured retention” obligation, the duty to defend the “insured” against a “claim” to which this insurance applies. The Insurer shall have no duty to defend the “insured” against any “claim” to which this insurance does not apply. The Insurer’s duty to defend the “msured” ends once the Limits of Liability are exhausted or are tendered into a court of applicable jurisdiction, or once the “insured” refuses a settlement offer as provided in Subsection E., below.

clauses.head: B. The Insurer shall have the right to
clauses.name: III.B. Selection of legal counsel
clauses.tail: this Policy, or credited against the "self-insured retention”.
clauses.text: B. The Insurer shall have the right to select legal counsel to represent the “insured” for the investigation, adjustment, and defense of any “claims” covered pursuant to this Policy. Selection of legal counsel by the Insurer shall not be done without the consent of the “insured”; such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. “Legal defense expenses” incurred prior to the selection of legal counsel by the Insurer shall not be covered pursuant to this Policy, or credited against the "self-insured retention”.

clauses.head: In the event the “insured” is entitled by
clauses.name: III.B. Independent counsel
clauses.tail: freely and fully waive its right to select independent counsel.
clauses.text: In the event the “insured” is entitled by law to select independent counsel to defend itself at the Insurer's expense, the attorney fees and all other litigation expenses the insurer shall pay to that counsel are limited to the rates the Insurer actually pays to counsel that the Insurer normally retains in the ordinary course of business when defending “claims” or lawsuits of similar complexity in the jurisdiction where the “claim” arose or is being defended. In addition, the “insured” and the Insurer agree that the Insurer may exercise the right to require that such counsel: 1) have certain minimum qualifications with respect to their competency, inciuding experience in defending “claims” similar to those oeing asserted against the “insured”; 2) maintain suitable errors and omissions insurance coverage; 3) be located within a reasonable proximity to the jurisdiction of the “claim"; and 4) agree in writing to respond in a timely manner to the Insurer's requests for information regarding the “claim”. The “insured” may at anytime, by its signed consent, freely and fully waive its right to select independent counsel.

clauses.head: C. The “insured” shall have the right and
clauses.name: III.C. Environmental consultant
clauses.tail: “self-insured retention’, except in the event of an “emergency response”.
clauses.text: C. The “insured” shall have the right and the duty to retain a qualified environmental consultant to perform any investigation and/or remediation of any “pollution condition” covered pursuant to this Policy. The “insured” must receive the written consent of the Insurer prior to the selection and retention of such consultant, except in the event of an “emergency response”. Any costs incurred prior to such consent shall not be covered pursuant to this Policy, or credited against the “self-insured retention’, except in the event of an “emergency response”.

clauses.head: D. “Legal defense expenses” reduce the Limits of Liability
clauses.name: III.D. Legal defense expenses
clauses.tail: this Policy and shall be applied to the “self-insured retention’.
clauses.text: D. “Legal defense expenses” reduce the Limits of Liability identified in Items 2., 3. and 4. of the Declarations to this Policy and shall be applied to the “self-insured retention’.

clauses.head: E. The Insurer shall present all settlement offers
clauses.name: III.E. Settlement offers
clauses.tail: recommendation had been accepted, exclusive of the “self-insured retention’.
clauses.text: E. The Insurer shall present all settlement offers to the “insured”. If the Insurer recommends a settlement which is acceptable to a claimant, exceeds any applicable “self-insured retention”, is within the Limits of Liability, and does not impose any additional unreasonable burdens on the “insured”, and the “insured” refuses to consent to such settlement offer, then the insurer's duty to defend shall end. Thereafter, the “msured” shall defend such “claim” independently and at the “insured’s” own expense. The Insurer's liability shall not exceed the amount for which the “claim” could have been settled if the Insurer's recommendation had been accepted, exclusive of the “self-insured retention’.

clauses.head: IV. COVERAGE TERRITORY The coverage afforded pursuant to
clauses.name: IV. Coverage Territory
clauses.tail: “claims” made, within the United States of America.
clauses.text: IV. COVERAGE TERRITORY The coverage afforded pursuant to this Policy shall only apply to “pollution conditions" located, and “claims” made, within the United States of America.

clauses.head: V. DEFINITIONS A. “Additional insured” means any person
clauses.name: V.A. Additional insured
clauses.tail: that are specified by endorsement to this Policy.
clauses.text: V. DEFINITIONS A. “Additional insured” means any person or entity specifically endorsed onto this Policy as an “additional insured”, if any. Such ‘additional insured” shall maintain only those rights that are specified by endorsement to this Policy.

clauses.head: B. “Bodily injury” means physical injury, illness, disease,
clauses.name: V.B. Bodily injury
clauses.tail: confirm any such physical injury, illness or disease.
clauses.text: B. “Bodily injury” means physical injury, illness, disease, mental anguish, emotional distress, or shock, sustained by any person, including death resulting therefrom, and any prospective medical monitoring costs that are intended to confirm any such physical injury, illness or disease.

clauses.head: C. “Certified industrial hygienist” means a licensed professional,
clauses.name: V.C. Certified industrial hygienist
clauses.tail: including experience with similar “fungi” or legionella pneumophila remediation projects.
clauses.text: C. “Certified industrial hygienist” means a licensed professional, as established by the American Board of Industrial Hygiene, that is: 1. Mutually agreed upon by the Insurer and the "insured"; and 2. Qualified by knowledge, skill, education and training to perform an assessment of the fungal or bacterial ecology of a property, building systems and/or contents, prepare an investigation protocol, interpret the results and prepare a scope of work to remediate the site to an ordinary ambient indoor air ecology for similar indoor environments. The Insurer may also exercise the right to require that such “certified industrial hygienist” have certain minimum qualifications with respect to their competency, including experience with similar “fungi” or legionella pneumophila remediation projects.

clauses.head: D. “Claim” means the written assertion of a
clauses.name: V.D. Claim
clauses.tail: of “pollution conditions” to which this insurance applies.
clauses.text: D. “Claim” means the written assertion of a legal right received by the “insured” from a third-party, including, but not limited to, a “government action”, suits or other actions alleging responsibility or liability on the part of the “insured” for “bodily injury’, “property damage” or “remediation costs” arising out of “pollution conditions” to which this insurance applies.

clauses.head: E. “Contingent transportation” means the movement of the
clauses.name: V.E. Contingent transportation
clauses.tail: is unloaded from the automobile, aircraft, watercraft, railcar or other conveyance.
clauses.text: E. “Contingent transportation” means the movement of the “insured’s” waste or products by automobile, aircraft, watercraft, railcar or other conveyance beyond the boundaries of a “covered location" by a person or entity, other than an “insured”, engaged in the business of transporting property for hire, until such time as the waste or product is unloaded from the automobile, aircraft, watercraft, railcar or other conveyance.

clauses.head: F. “Covered location” means: Any location specifically identified
clauses.name: V.F. Covered location
clauses.tail: scheduled as a “covered location” by endorsement attached to this Policy, if any.
clauses.text: F. “Covered location” means: Any location specifically identified in Item 8. of the Declarations to this Policy; 2. Any location that meets the prerequisites to coverage identified in Automatic Acquisition and Due Diligence Endorsement attached to this Policy, if any; and 3. Any other location specifically scheduled as a “covered location” by endorsement attached to this Policy, if any.

clauses.head: G. “Emergency response” means actions taken and reasonable
clauses.name: V.G. Emergency response
clauses.tail: or the environment arising out of such “pollution condition”.
clauses.text: G. “Emergency response” means actions taken and reasonable “remediation costs” incurred within seventy-two (72) hours following the discovery of a "pollution condition" by an “insured” in order to abate or respond to an imminent and substantial threat to human health or the environment arising out of such “pollution condition”.

clauses.head: H. “Environmental indemnity obligations” means an "insured's” obligations
clauses.name: V.H. Environmental indemnity obligations
clauses.tail: Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement attached to this Policy, if any.
clauses.text: H. “Environmental indemnity obligations” means an "insured's” obligations to defend or indemnify a third-party with respect to a “pollution condition” to which this insurance otherwise applies, provided that such defense or indemnity obligation is explicitly included within a contract identified on the Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement attached to this Policy, if any.

clauses.head: |. “Environmental Jaw” means any federal, state, provincial,
clauses.name: V.I. Environmental Jaw
clauses.tail: the “insured” with respect to a “pollution condition’.
clauses.text: “Environmental Jaw” means any federal, state, provincial, municipal or other local law, statute, ordinance, rule, guidance document, regulation, and all amendments thereto, including state voluntary cleanup or risk-based corrective action guidance, governing the liability or responsibilities of the “insured” with respect to a “pollution condition’.

clauses.head: J. “Extended reporting period” means the additional period
clauses.name: V.J. Extended reporting period
clauses.tail: a “claim” first made against the “insured” during or subsequent to the end of the “policy period”.
clauses.text: J. “Extended reporting period” means the additional period of time in which to report a “claim” first made against the “insured” during or subsequent to the end of the “policy period”.

clauses.head: K. “First named insured” means the person or
clauses.name: V.K. First named insured
clauses.tail: unless any such responsibilities are otherwise designated by endorsement.
clauses.text: K. “First named insured” means the person or entity as identified in Item 1. of the Declarations to this Policy. The “first named insured” is the party responsible for the payment of any premiums and the payment of, or evidencing payment of, any applicable “self-insured retention” amounts. The “first named insured” shall also serve as the sole agent on behalf of all “insureds” with respect to the provision and receipt of notices, including notice of cancellation or non-renewal, receipt and acceptance of any endorsements or any other changes to this Policy, return of any premium, assignment of any interest pursuant to this Policy, as well as the exercise of any applicable “extended reporting period”, unless any such responsibilities are otherwise designated by endorsement.

clauses.head: L. “Fungi” means any type or form of
clauses.name: V.L. Fungi
clauses.tail: including mold or mildew, and any mycotoxins, spores, scents, or byproducts produced or released by “fungi”.
clauses.text: L. “Fungi” means any type or form of fungus, including mold or mildew, and any mycotoxins, spores, scents, or byproducts produced or released by “fungi”.

clauses.head: M. “Government action” means action taken or liability
clauses.name: V.M. Government action
clauses.tail: state, provincial, municipal or other local government agency or body acting pursuant to the authority of “environmental law”,
clauses.text: M. “Government action” means action taken or liability imposed by any federal, state, provincial, municipal or other local government agency or body acting pursuant to the authority of “environmental law”,

clauses.head: N. “Hlicit abandonment” means the intentional placement, abandonment
clauses.name: V.N. Hlicit abandonment
clauses.tail: an ownership or operational interest in the “covered location”.
clauses.text: N. “Hlicit abandonment” means the intentional placement, abandonment or disposal of any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant, including smoke, soot, vapors, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals, hazardous substances, hazardous materials, or waste materials, including “low-level radioactive waste”, “mixed waste” and medical, infectious and pathological wastes, on, at or into a “covered location” by a person or entity that: 1. Is not an “insured”; 2. is not affiliated by common ownership with an "insured", and 3. Does not maintain, or has not maintained, an ownership or operational interest in the “covered location”.

clauses.head: 0. “Insured” means the "first named insured”, any
clauses.name: V.O. Insured
clauses.tail: while acting within the scope of his or her duties as such,
clauses.text: 0. “Insured” means the "first named insured”, any “named insured”, any “additional insured”, and any past or present director or officer of, partner in, employee of, temporary or leased worker of, or, with respect to a limited liability company, a member of, any “insured” while acting within the scope of his or her duties as such,

clauses.head: P. “Legal defense expense” means reasonable legal costs,
clauses.name: V.P. Legal defense expense
clauses.tail: by the “insured” in the investigation, adjustment, or defense of “claims”.
clauses.text: P. “Legal defense expense” means reasonable legal costs, charges, and expenses, including expert charges, incurred by the “insured” in the investigation, adjustment, or defense of “claims”.

clauses.head: Q. “Low-level radioactive waste” means waste that is
clauses.name: V.Q. Low-level radioactive waste
clauses.tail: waste with greater than specified quantities of elements heavier than uranium.
clauses.text: Q. “Low-level radioactive waste” means waste that is radioactive but not classified as the following: highlevel waste (spent nuclear fuel or the highly radioactive waste produced if spent fuel is reprocessed), uranium milling residues, and waste with greater than specified quantities of elements heavier than uranium.

clauses.head: R. “Mixed waste” means waste containing both radioactive
clauses.name: V.R. Mixed waste
clauses.tail: Conservation and Recovery Act as either may be amended.
clauses.text: R. “Mixed waste” means waste containing both radioactive and hazardous components as defined pursuant to United States law within the Atomic Energy Act and the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act as either may be amended.

clauses.head: S. “Named insured” means any person or entity
clauses.name: V.S. Named insured
clauses.tail: the “first named insured” that are identified in Subsection K., above.
clauses.text: S. “Named insured” means any person or entity specifically endorsed onto this Policy as a “named insured”, if any. Such “named insured” shall maintain the same rights pursuant to this Policy as the “first named insured", except for those rights specifically reserved to the “first named insured” that are identified in Subsection K., above.

clauses.head: T. “Natural resource damage” means injury to, destruction
clauses.name: V.T. Natural resource damage
clauses.tail: reasonable costs of assessing such injury, destruction or loss resulting therefrom.
clauses.text: T. “Natural resource damage” means injury to, destruction of, or loss of, including the resulting loss of value of, fish, wildlife, biota, land, air, water, groundwater, drinking water supplies, and other such resources belonging to, managed by, held in trust by, appertaining to, or otherwise controlled by the United States of America (including the resources of the fishery conservation zone established by the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (16 U.S.C. § 1801 et. seq.)), any state or local government, or any Native American Tribe, or, if such resources are subject to a trust restriction on alienation, any members of any Native American Tribe, including the reasonable costs of assessing such injury, destruction or loss resulting therefrom.

clauses.head: U. “Non-owned disposal site” means any disposal site
clauses.name: V.U. Non-owned disposal site
clauses.tail: or operated by an “insured”, which receives, or has historically received, an “insured’s" waste.
clauses.text: U. “Non-owned disposal site” means any disposal site or recycling facility not owned or operated by an “insured”, which receives, or has historically received, an “insured’s" waste.

clauses.head: V. “Policy period” means: 1. The period of
clauses.name: V.V. Policy period
clauses.tail: 3. Any shorter period resulting from the cancellation of this Policy.
clauses.text: V. “Policy period” means: 1. The period of time specifically identified in Item 2.a. of the Declarations to this Policy for Coverage A. and/or Item 3.a. of the Declarations to this Policy for Coverage B.; 2. With respect to “covered locations” added pursuant to the Automatic Acquisition and Due Diligence Endorsement attached to this Policy, if any, the period of time following the closing date of the acquisition transaction or the effective date of the lease or, as applicable, through the applicable expiration date of the Policy identified in Item 2.a. or 3.a. of the Declarations to this Policy with respect to New Poilution Conditions Coverage and Pre-Existing Pollution Conditions Coverage, respectively; or 3. Any shorter period resulting from the cancellation of this Policy.

clauses.head: W. “Pollution condition” means: 1. The presence of
clauses.name: V.W. Pollution condition
clauses.tail: include, but are not limited to, “low-level radioactive waste” and “mixed waste”.
clauses.text: W. “Pollution condition” means: 1. The presence of “fungi” or /egionella pneumophila; 2. “Illicit abandonment”: or 3. The discharge, dispersal, release, escape, migration or seepage of any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant, including smoke, soot, vapors, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals, hazardous substances, hazardous materiais, or waste materials, on, in, into, or upon land and structures thereupon, the atmosphere, surface water, or groundwater. For the purpose of this definition, waste materials include, but are not limited to, “low-level radioactive waste” and “mixed waste”.

clauses.head: X. “Property damage” means: 1. Physical injury to,
clauses.name: V.X. Property damage
clauses.tail: 3. Diminished value of tangible property owned by a third-party; or 4. “Natural resource damages’.
clauses.text: X. “Property damage” means: 1. Physical injury to, or destruction of, tangible property of a third-party, including all resulting loss of use of that property; 2. Loss of use of tangible property of a third-party, that is not physically injured or destroyed; 3. Diminished value of tangible property owned by a third-party; or 4. “Natural resource damages’.

clauses.head: Y. “Remediation costs” means reasonable expenses incurred to
clauses.name: V.Y. Remediation costs
clauses.tail: prior to being damaged during the course of responding to a “pollution condition”.
clauses.text: Y. “Remediation costs” means reasonable expenses incurred to investigate, quantify, monitor, mitigate, abate, remove, dispose, treat, neutralize, or immobilize “pollution conditions” to the extent required by “environmental law". If no applicable laws exist that govern the remediation of “fungi” or /egionella pneumophila in the jurisdiction of the “covered location’, necessary “remediation costs” may be established by securing the written professional recommendations of a “certified industrial hygienist” retained with the prior approval of the Insurer. “Remediation costs” shall also include: 1. Reasonable legal cost, where such cost has been incurred by an “insured” with the written consent of the Insurer; and 2. Reasonable expenses required to restore, repair or replace real or personal property, to substantially the same condition it was in prior to being damaged during the course of responding to a “pollution condition”.

clauses.head: Z. “Responsible person” means any employee of an
clauses.name: V.Z. Responsible person
clauses.tail: at a “covered location”, and any officer or director of, or partner in, an “insured”.
clauses.text: Z. “Responsible person” means any employee of an “insured” responsible for environmental affairs, control, or compliance at a “covered location”, and any officer or director of, or partner in, an “insured”.

clauses.head: AA.“Self-insured retention” means the dollar amount identified in
clauses.name: V.AA. Self-insured retention
clauses.tail: Coverage B., or as otherwise designated by endorsement to this Policy, if any.
clauses.text: AA.“Self-insured retention” means the dollar amount identified in Item 2.d. of the Declarations to this Policy for Coverage A. and/or Item 3.d. of the Declarations to this Policy for Coverage B., or as otherwise designated by endorsement to this Policy, if any.

clauses.head: BB."“Terrorism” means activities against persons, organizations or property
clauses.name: V.BB. Terrorism
clauses.tail: to express (or express opposition to) a philosophy or ideology.
clauses.text: BB."“Terrorism” means activities against persons, organizations or property of any nature: 1. That involve the following or preparation for the following: a. If the Insurer and the “insured” disagree on the amount of “business income” or any other amount that is or may be covered pursuant to this Endorsement, either may make written demand for an appraisal of the loss. In this event, each party shall select a competent and impartial appraiser. If necessary, the two appraisers shall select an umpire. If they cannot agree, either may request that selection be made by a judge of a court having jurisdiction. The appraisers shall state separately the amount of “business income” or any other amount. If they fail to agree to a resolution, they shall submit their differences to the umpire. A decision agreed to by the appraisers, of the umpire, if necessary, shall be binding upon both parties. Each party shall: 1. Pay its chosen appraiser; and 2. Definition of Certified Act(s) of Terrorism For the purpose of this endorsement, the italicized phrase certified act(s) of terrorism means one (1) or more acts certified by the Secretary of the Treasury, in concurrence with the Secretary of State and the Attorney Gencral of the United States, to be terrorism pursuant to the federal Terrorism Risk Insurance Act, including all amendments (hereafter "[RLA"). The criteria contained in TRIA for certified act(s) of terrorism include the following: A. The act resulted in insured losses in excess of $5 million in the aggregate. attributable to all types of insurance subject to TRIA; and B. The act is a violent act or an act that is dangerous to human life, property or infrastructure, and is committed by an individual or individuals as part of an effort to coerce the civilian population of the United States or to influence the policy or affect the conduct of the United States Government by coercion.

clauses.head: Section 3. Sexual Responsibility – Seeking and Communicating
clauses.name: 3.0 Sexual Responsibility and Consent
clauses.tail: the outcome of any investigation or conduct process.
clauses.text: Section 3. Sexual Responsibility – Seeking and Communicating Consent 3.0. Brandeis University expects all members of the University community to treat one another with respect. Policies regarding sexual misconduct emphasize personal accountability as well as recognition of the impact of one’s behavior on others. Students are encouraged to examine their own values, communicate with one another clearly, and acknowledge the condition and requests of others. Incapacity to consent to sexual activity or compromised communication can result when individuals are under the inuence of intoxicants such as alcohol and other drugs. If both parties do not consent, or are unable to consent to a sexual act, then the interaction could be dened as sexual misconduct or sexual assault. Consent must be sought and clearly understood and communicated before engaging in any sexual activities. Due to the seriousness of sexual misconduct accusations and accompanying issues that may impact the Brandeis community, any student accused of sexual misconduct may be placed on campus restriction or emergency suspension pending the outcome of any investigation or conduct process.

clauses.head: 3.1. Students are prohibited from engaging in sexual
clauses.name: 3.1 Sexual Misconduct and Consent
clauses.tail: raise a presumption of physical and/or mental incapacity.
clauses.text: 3.1. Students are prohibited from engaging in sexual misconduct. Sexual contact that occurs without the explicit consent of each student involved may be considered sexual misconduct. Consent must be clearly communicated, mutual, non-coercive, and given free of force or threat of force. A student who is physically or mentally incapacitated by drugs, alcohol, or other circumstances is not capable of giving consent. Physical or mental incapacity means the lack of ability to appreciate the fact that the situation is sexual, and/or the inability to rationally and reasonably appreciate the nature and extent of that situation. Evidence of ingestion of drugs and/or alcohol may raise a presumption of physical and/or mental incapacity.

clauses.head: 3.2. Causing incapacitation or intoxication, or taking advantage
clauses.name: 3.2 Incapacitation or Intoxication
clauses.tail: engaging in sexual activity is considered sexual misconduct.
clauses.text: 3.2. Causing incapacitation or intoxication, or taking advantage of someone’s incapacitation or intoxication for the purpose of engaging in sexual activity is considered sexual misconduct.

clauses.head: 3.3. Consent or lack of consent may be
clauses.name: 3.3 Communication of Consent
clauses.tail: for the continuation or renewal of sexual activity.
clauses.text: 3.3. Consent or lack of consent may be communicated verbally or through actions but if a refusal to engage in sexual activity is communicated at any time then the activity must cease immediately. Lack of consent may also be inferred from the use of force, threat, physical intimidation, or advantage gained by the accuser’s mental or physical incapacity or impairment of which the accused was aware or should have been aware. Prior sexual activity or an existing acquaintance, friendship, or relationship that has been sexual in nature does not constitute consent for the continuation or renewal of sexual activity.

clauses.text: Section 4. Maintenance of Academic Integrity 4.0. Every member of the University community is expected to maintain the highest standards of academic integrity. A student shall not submit work that is falsied or is not the result of the student’s own effort. Infringement of academic honesty by a student subjects that student to serious penalties, which may include failure on the assignment, failure in the course, suspension from the University or other sanctions (see Section 21). A student who is in doubt regarding standards of academic honesty in a course or assignment should consult the faculty member responsible for that course or assignment before submitting the work. A student’s lack of understanding is not a valid defense to a charge of academic dishonesty.

clauses.head: 4.1. A student’s name on any written exercise
clauses.name: 4.1 Student Work and Examinations
clauses.tail: submitted also constitutes an infringement of academic honesty.
clauses.text: 4.1. A student’s name on any written exercise (e.g., examination, report, thesis, theme, notebook, laboratory report, computer program, etc.), or in association with an oral presentation constitutes a representation that the work is the result of that student’s own thought and study. Such work shall be stated in the student’s own words, and produced without the assistance of others, except for quotation marks, references, and footnotes that accurately acknowledge the use of other sources (including sources found on the Internet). Talking during an examination, or possession or use of unauthorized materials or equipment during an examination constitutes an infringement of academic honesty. Attempting to receive credit for work not originally submitted also constitutes an infringement of academic honesty.

clauses.text: 4.2. In some instances, a student may be authorized by a faculty member to work jointly with (an)other student(s) in solving problems or completing projects. However, students may not collaborate on assignments without explicit permission from the instructor. To provide, either knowingly or through negligence, one’s own work to assist another student in satisfying a course requirement constitutes an infringement of academic honesty. Aid from personnel associated with University-sanctioned tutoring services is acceptable.

A student who perceives the possibility of overlapping assignments in courses should consult with the appropriate faculty members before presuming that a single effort will fulll requirements of both courses.

clauses.head: Section 7. Equal Opportunity, Non-Discrimination, and Harassment 7.0.
clauses.name: 7.0 Non-Discrimination and Harassment Policy
clauses.tail: including dismissal from school or release from employment.
clauses.text: Section 7. Equal Opportunity, Non-Discrimination, and Harassment 7.0. Non-Discrimination and Harassment Policy: Brandeis University is committed to providing its students, faculty, and staff with an environment conducive to learning and working where all people are treated with respect and dignity. Toward that end, it is essential that Brandeis be free from discrimination and harassment on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religious creed, gender identity and expression, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, disability, Vietnam Era Veteran, qualied special, disabled veteran or other eligible veteran status or any other category protected by law. Rights and Responsibilities 2011 - 2012 9 It is the University’s responsibility to help prevent harassment and discrimination from occurring, to pursue concerns of which it is aware, to objectively investigate concerns, and to take immediate and appropriate action to remedy issues of harassment and discrimination. Brandeis takes this responsibility seriously. Therefore, violations of this policy will not be tolerated and may result in corrective actions up to and including dismissal from school or release from employment.

clauses.head: 7.1. Understanding Harassment: Harassment whether sexual or based
clauses.name: 7.1 Understanding Harassment
clauses.tail: faculty/student, within peer groups, or with third parties.
clauses.text: 7.1. Understanding Harassment: Harassment whether sexual or based on an individual’s protected class status (race, color, ancestry, religious creed, gender, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, disability, Vietnam Era Veteran, qualied special, disabled veteran or other eligible veteran status) is a form of discrimination and will not be tolerated. It is regarded as harassment when the conduct has the purpose or effect of unreasonably interfering with a person’s education or work performance by creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive environment in which to work, study or live; or otherwise adversely affects a person’s employment or educational opportunities. This may include but is not limited to, hiring, ring, salary increases, promotions, grades, recommendations, scholarly or teaching opportunities, participation in extracurricular activities and student organizations. Harassment may occur between supervisor/supervisee, faculty/student, within peer groups, or with third parties.

clauses.head: 7.2. Examples of Sexual Harassment: Depending on the
clauses.name: 7.2 Examples of Sexual Harassment
clauses.tail: is sexually involved, which adversely affects other students
clauses.text: 7.2. Examples of Sexual Harassment: Depending on the circumstances, conduct which may constitute sexual harassment includes, but is not limited to: • Unwelcome sexual conduct toward an individual, including offensive comments, touching or sexual propositions • Threats or insinuations that a person’s employment, academic standing, grade, assignments, or other conditions of employment or academic life may be adversely affected by not submitting to sexual advances. • Leering, making sexual gestures, touching, patting, pinching, rubbing, impeding or blocking movements, displaying of sexually suggestive objects, pictures, cartoons or posters, suggestive or obscene letters or e-mails, notes, invitations or gifts • Making or using derogatory comments, epithets, slurs or jokes with a sexual content • Persistent unsolicited and unwelcome invitations for dates, encounters, or pressure to engage in sexual activity of an implied or explicit nature • Persistent inappropriate and unwelcome questions asked about personal life • Comments to, or about, any individual or their appearance that is sexually graphic or would otherwise tend to be degrading • Displaying, sending, forwarding, downloading or otherwise distributing sexual materials via the Internet, computer, cellular data network, or e-mail • Consensual sexual relationships where such relationships lead to favoritism towards the student with whom the instructor is sexually involved, which adversely affects other students

clauses.head: 7.3. Examples of other Forms of Harassment/Discrimination: There
clauses.name: 7.3 Other Harassment and Discrimination
clauses.tail: to the level of a violation of law.
clauses.text: 7.3. Examples of other Forms of Harassment/Discrimination: There are other forms of harassment/discrimination as well that create a hostile educational or work environment on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religious creed, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression, age, genetic information, disability, Vietnam Era Veteran, qualied disabled veteran or other eligible veteran status or status in any group protected by federal or state law (together, ‘protected class status’). Depending on the circumstances, the following are examples of behaviors that may constitute harassment/discrimination under this policy. This is not an exhaustive list: • Jokes, comments or innuendoes that make fun of, denigrate, or are based on an individual’s or group’s protected class status • Epithets or slurs based on an individual’s or group’s protected class status • Objects, posters, cartoons, or pictures which make fun of, denigrate, or are based on an individual’s or group’s protected class status whether directed to an individual, placed on University premises or displayed or circulated on campus • Displaying, sending, forwarding, downloading or otherwise distributing materials via the Internet, cellular data network, computer, or e-mail that make fun of, denigrate, or are based on protected class status • Other verbal or physical conduct that denigrates or shows hostility or aversion toward an individual or group based on protected class status. Determination of whether particular conduct violates this policy is made on a case-by-case basis, in light of all the known facts and circumstances. The University may take action on conduct that it deems to be inappropriate, regardless of whether it rises to the level of a violation of law.

clauses.head: 7.4. Retaliation: Brandeis policy, as well as federal
clauses.name: 7.4 Retaliation
clauses.tail: including dismissal from school or termination of employment.
clauses.text: 7.4. Retaliation: Brandeis policy, as well as federal and state law, prohibits retaliation against any person who in good faith initiates a complaint of harassment or discrimination or cooperates in the investigation of a complaint of harassment or discrimination. Retaliation may result in corrective action up to and including dismissal from school or termination of employment.

clauses.head: 7.5. False Claims: If it is determined that
clauses.name: 7.5 False Claims
clauses.tail: including dismissal from school or release from employment.
clauses.text: 7.5. False Claims: If it is determined that an individual falsied a claim of harassment or discrimination, it may result in corrective actions up to and including dismissal from school or release from employment.

clauses.head: 7.6. Contact/Reporting Information, Concerning Staff or Faculty: Brandeis
clauses.name: 7.6 Contact and Reporting Information
clauses.tail: the Dean of Student Life at 781-736- 3600.
clauses.text: 7.6. Contact/Reporting Information, Concerning Staff or Faculty: Brandeis encourages the reporting of all perceived incidents of discrimination or harassment. Concerns about harassment or discrimination by a faculty or staff member (including visiting faculty, post-doctoral fellows, or graduate students acting in an instructional capacity) should be brought to the attention of the Vice President for Human Resources and Title IX Coordinator in the Ofce of Human Resources at 781-736-4464. Concerns about third parties, such as vendors, should also be directed to this individual. This individual, or a designee, is available to provide guidance in managing the concern, for help with informal resolution, for ling a complaint, and for reviewing complaints that require more in-depth fact-nding. For guidance and/or to le a complaint against any undergraduate or graduate student, contact the Ofce of the Dean of Student Life at 781-736- 3600.
