clauses.text: ARTICLE 7. CONFIDENTIALITY 7.1 Ownership of Confidential Information. Except as otherwise required by law, including without limitation Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 66 and Chapter 4, Section 7, Clause 26th, each of MTC and Network Operator is respectively the exclusive owner of any Confidential Information that it may furnish to the other from time to time pursuant to this Agreement, and the furnishing of such Confidential Information to, or access to such items by the other Party and/or its contractors, consultants or subcontractors will not grant any express or implied license to or interest in the other Parties and/or its contractors, consultants or subcontractors relating to such Confidential Information except as required to perform the #10069598_v13 66 Services or otherwise meet its obligations pursuant to the Agreement. Subject to the requirements of law, including without limitation Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 66 and Chapter 4, Section 7, Clause 26th, upon request by either Party at any time and from time to time and without regard to the default status of the Parties under the Agreement, the Parties and their respective contractors, consultants and subcontractors shall promptly deliver to the requesting party any and all Confidential Information.

clauses.head: 7.2 Treatment of Confidential Information. Network Operator and
clauses.name: 7.2 Treatment of Confidential Information
clauses.tail: set forth in the policy and procedure attached at Exhibit H-1.
clauses.text: 7.2 Treatment of Confidential Information. Network Operator and MTC acknowledge and agree that they shall follow the policies and procedure set forth in Exhibits H-1 and H-2, attached hereto. In addition to, and not in limitation of the foregoing, Network Operator acknowledge and agree that MTC (i) is subject to the provisions of the Massachusetts Public Records Act, M.G.L. Chapter 66 (the “Records Act”), which may require MTC to make certain information, including Confidential Information, available to the public, and (ii) may be compelled to disclose information in response to subpoenas or other compulsory legal processes, court or administrative orders or similar requests or demands for disclosure of information. MTC will use reasonable efforts to notify the Network Operator in the event that MTC receives any request for disclosure of information provided to MTC pursuant to this Agreement under the Records Act, or any subpoena or other compulsory legal process, court or administrative order, or similar request or demand, all as set forth in the policy and procedure attached at Exhibit H-1.

clauses.head: 7.3 Network Operator has read and agrees to
clauses.name: 7.3 Network Operator Confidentiality Obligations
clauses.tail: provisions of this Section and Exhibits H-1 and H-2.
clauses.text: 7.3 Network Operator has read and agrees to comply with, and will cause its agents, officers, directors, employees and subcontractors to comply with, the provisions of this Article 7 and MTC's written policies concerning confidentiality, as set forth in Exhibits H-1 and H-2 hereto and as communicated by MTC's Executive Director or General Counsel to Network #10069598_v13 67 Operator from time to time. Network Operator acknowledges that during the term of this Agreement it may receive, have access to or create Confidential Information (also referred to as Sensitive Information in Exhibits H-1 and H-2) which is not generally known by the public, nor as a matter of course disseminated by MTC, published on MTC's website or disclosed by MTC pursuant to the requirements of any Governmental Authority. Network Operator agrees, for itself and for its agents, officers, directors, employees and subcontractors, as follows: 7.3.1 not at any time, whether during or after the termination of this Agreement, to divulge, disclose or reveal to any Person any such Confidential Information, whether or not such information is produced by Network Operator's own efforts, except (A) as specifically required in connection with the fulfillment of Network Operator's obligations hereunder, or (B) as otherwise directed by the General Counsel in connection with a disclosure request under the Public Records Act, a request for discovery, subpoena, court or administrative order or other compulsory legal process, disclosure requirement or request relating to such Confidential Information; 7.3.2 not at any time, whether during or after the termination of this Agreement, use any Confidential Information for Network Operator's direct or indirect financial or other benefit or for the benefit of any Person related to or that is an Affiliate of with Network Operator or with whom Network Operator is now or hereafter associated, other than MTC, nor will Network Operator use or attempt to use any Confidential Information in any manner which could reasonably be expected to injure or cause loss, whether directly or indirectly, to MTC or any Applicable Third Party; 7.3.3 in the event that Network Operator (or any of its agents, officers, directors employees or subcontractors) is questioned about Confidential Information by anyone #10069598_v13 68 who is not known by Network Operator to be authorized to receive or have access to such Confidential Information, or is asked to provide Confidential Information to any such Person, Network Operator agrees to promptly notify the General Counsel and respond to the inquirer in accordance with the General Counsel's instructions; and 7.3.4 not at any time, whether during or after the termination of this Agreement, reproduce any written or electronic materials containing Confidential Information except to the extent necessary to perform Network Operator's obligations under this Agreement, nor make or use (or permit its employees or agents to use) any such written or electronic materials other than in connection with the performance of the Network Operators' obligations under this Agreement and for the benefit of MTC, it being understood and agreed that all such written or electronic materials are, shall be and shall remain the sole and exclusive property of MTC, and immediately upon the termination of the Agreement for any reason, Network Operator shall deliver all copies of MTC's Written Materials and all other property of MTC in its direct or indirect possession or control to MTC, at its main office. In addition, Network Operator shall, upon the termination of the Agreement, delete all Written Materials and Confidential Information, held by Network Operator as data stored on computers, floppy disks, c/d roms or other electronic media; provided that Network Operator shall not delete any customer information required by law to be maintained. Network Operator shall certify to MTC that it either has deleted all Confidential Information required to be deleted or despite diligent efforts has been unable to do so and will maintain such Information in confidence. To the maximum extent required by law, Network Operator shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless MTC from and against any and all claims, loss, cost, damage or expense, including but not limited to #10069598_v13 69 reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses, resulting from a failure to comply with the provisions of this Section and Exhibits H-1 and H-2.

clauses.text: ARTICLE 8. TERMINATION AND OTHER REMEDIES 8.1 Termination By MTC. MTC may terminate this Agreement for the following reasons: 8.1.1 A material breach of this Agreement by Network Operator that remains uncured for a period of thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice thereof or in the case of a breach under Section 10.3.3, remains uncured for a period of ten (10) days; or 8.1.2 There exists a series of non-material or persistent breaches by Network Operator that, in the aggregate, have a material and significant adverse impact on the services to or the support and operational management of the MTC Network or any Network Extension; or 8.1.3 Network Operator becomes insolvent or is unable to pay its debts or enters into or files (or has filed or commenced against it) a petition, arrangement, application, action or other proceeding seeking relief or protection under the bankruptcy laws of the United States or any similar laws of the United States or any state of the United States or any country in which the Network Operator has significant operations, or transfers all or substantially all of its assets to another person or entity; or

clauses.head: 8.1.4 In the event of a change of
clauses.name: 8.1.4 Change of Control
clauses.tail: otherwise faithfully fulfill its obligations under this Agreement.
clauses.text: 8.1.4 In the event of a change of control of Network Operator without MTC’s prior written consent, which consent shall not be withheld unreasonably, MTC, or its successor, may terminate the Agreement with one hundred eighty (180) days prior #10069598_v13 71 written notice to Network Operator given not later than fourteen (14) days after the notice of the occurrence of such change of control. For purposes of this Section, a change of control shall be deemed to have occurred if there occurs a change in the possession of the power to direct or control the management (at the board level) of the Network Operator, through the ownership of at least fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities. For purposes of this Subsection, reasonable grounds for MTC to withhold consent shall include, but are not limited to, if control is proposed to be transferred (y) to any person or entity that is, or as to which a direct or indirect owner of 10% or more of the beneficial interest is, on a list of debarred or suspended entities for either the Commonwealth of Massachusetts or the United States Government, or (z) to any person or entity that is, or as to which a direct or indirect owner of sufficient voting shares to elect or control election of the board of directors is, engaged in business in competition with the MTC Network and has not given MTC reasonable, credible assurances that it will cause the Network Operator to continue using its best efforts to maximize Network Revenue and otherwise faithfully fulfill its obligations under this Agreement.

clauses.head: 8.2 In the event grounds exist for MTC
clauses.name: 8.2 Termination Deferral Charge
clauses.tail: damages MTC may have due to the breach by Network Operator.
clauses.text: 8.2 In the event grounds exist for MTC to terminate this Agreement pursuant to Section 8.1, except for termination pursuant to Section 8.1.4, MTC may, in its sole discretion, following notice and an opportunity to cure pursuant to Section 8.1, elect to defer termination and instead impose a termination deferral charge for such breach. The amount of the termination deferral charge shall be calculated by increasing the percentage of Network Revenue owed by the Network Operator under Section 4.9.5 by one-half of a percent (.5%) for each additional thirty (30) day period, or part thereof, beyond the initial thirty (30) days that the breach remains uncured. Payment of such charges shall be due at the same time as regular #10069598_v13 72 revenue sharing payments under Section 4.9.5. The increase in revenue share shall remain in effect and shall continue to escalate by one-half of a percent (.50%) for each additional thirty (30) day period until the material breach is cured. Upon cure, the Network Operator’s revenue sharing percentage shall revert to the percentage in effect prior to the material breach. The incremental revenue share shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies and damages MTC may have due to the breach by Network Operator.

clauses.name: 8.3.1 Force Majeure Termination

clauses.text: 8.3 Force Majeure 8.3.1 If a Force Majeure Event occurs after the Commencement Date and results in a disruption to the basic functioning of more than fifty percent (50%) of the MTC Network for a period of more than 12 months despite compliance by both Parties with their obligations under this Agreement and commercially reasonable efforts by the Network Operator to restore such functioning, either Party may terminate this Agreement upon sixty (60) days notice to the other. In the event of termination under this Section, the Network Operator shall pay MTC all amounts owing through the date of termination, with amounts otherwise due on an annual basis being prorated for the portion of the then- current year that has elapsed prior to termination.

clauses.text: 8.3.2 If a Force Majeure Event occurs after the Commencement Date that is not within the scope of Section 8.3.1 and results in a disruption to the basic functioning of one or more elements of the MTC Network, the Network Operator shall take all commercially reasonable action to restore such functioning to levels and with the urgency established by this Agreement, but, provided the Network Operator has taken all commercially reasonable action, the lack of functioning so caused shall not create an instance of default under this Agreement, and Network Operator’s time to achieve levels #10069598_v13 73 of functioning established by this Agreement shall be extended by the period of time reasonably required to restore such functioning as soon as is reasonably practicable by one acting with urgency.

clauses.text: ARTICLE 9. INDEMNIFICATION 9.1 For purposes of this Article, Network Operator shall include each and all of its subcontractors, assignees, and any other third party acting at the direction of them. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the Network Operator shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless MTC, its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, successors and assigns, as Indemnified Parties, from and against all claims, liabilities, costs, or expenses arising out of: #10069598_v13 75 (a) bodily injury, death, personal injury or property damage resulting from the negligence or willful misconduct of Network Operator, (b) claims by third parties for breach by the Network Operator of, or default by the Network Operator under, any contract between Network Operator and such third party, (c) any loss, cost, damage or expense resulting from Network Operator's non-compliance with laws, orders, or rules of any governmental authority, (d) any loss, cost, damage or expense resulting from Network Operator's act or omission that causes, in whole or in part, MTC to breach any agreement between MTC and a pole owner, conduit owner, Wholesale Customer, MassDOT, or any other person relating to the MTC Network, or (e) any loss, cost, damage or expense resulting from Network Operator's infringement or misappropriation of, any patent, trade secret, copyright or other proprietary right of any third party. The foregoing indemnity shall not be deemed to apply to any of the foregoing claims, liabilities, costs or expenses to the extent attributable to the Indemnified Party’s own negligent acts or omissions or willful misconduct, or those of anyone acting by, through or under the Indemnified Party.

The foregoing indemnity shall not be deemed to apply to any of the foregoing claims, liabilities, costs or expenses to the extent attributable to the Indemnified Party’s own negligent acts or #10069598_v13 76 omissions or willful misconduct, or those of anyone acting by, through or under the Indemnified Party.

clauses.text: 9.3 Notice of Claims; Indemnification Procedures. The Indemnified Party shall provide written notice immediately to the Indemnifying Party, of any loss, event, happening or occurrence which would be the basis of an Indemnified Claim. So long as the Indemnifying Party is not in default in the performance of its obligations under the Agreement, as between the Indemnified Party and the Indemnifying Party, the Indemnifying Party shall retain primary responsibility for the conduct of an Indemnified Claim Proceeding and the defense (and any appropriate appeal) thereof. Legal counsel retained with respect to any Indemnified Claim proceeding shall be selected by the Indemnifying Party, but shall be subject to the reasonable prior approval of the Indemnified Party. As between the Indemnified Party and the Indemnifying Party, all costs incurred with respect to any Indemnified Claim Proceeding (including, but not limited to, reasonable costs and attorneys’fees) shall be borne by the Indemnifying Party, and the Indemnifying Party’s indemnification obligations set forth in this Article 9 shall extend to all such costs (but net of the amount of (x) any insurance proceeds realized by such Indemnified Party from insurance policies with respect to such matters or (y) any recoveries by any Indemnified Party from any third party, without duplication).

clauses.text: ARTICLE 10. INSURANCE AND RISK OF LOSS 10.1 Network Operator Liability Insurance. During the Term of the Agreement, Network Operator shall maintain and keep in force, at its own expense, the following minimum insurance coverages, and such other coverages as the Parties may determine are commercially reasonable: 10.1.1 Workers’Compensation Insurance in compliance with applicable federal and state laws with an "All States" endorsement, a "Voluntary Compensation" endorsement and United States Longshoreman and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act coverage, if required. Such Worker's Compensation Insurance policy(ies) shall include coverage for statutory workers' compensation benefits, voluntary compensation coverage and all appropriate state specific endorsements. Such policy(ies) shall also provide Employers Liability Insurance with not less than the following limits: 10.1.1.1 Bodily Injury with Accident - $1,000,000 (one million) per accident; 10.1.1.2 Bodily Injury with Disease - $1,000,000 (one million) policy limit; and 10.1.1.3 Bodily Injury with Disease - $1,000,000 (one million) per employee.

DISPUTE RESOLUTION 11.1 Dispute Resolution Procedures 11.1.1 Any dispute between the Parties either with respect to the interpretation of any provision of the Agreement or with respect to the performance by Network Operator or by MTC hereunder shall be resolved as specified in this ARTICLE 11, regardless of whether or not mention of this Article is made in any other Section.

clauses.text: 11.1.2 If the IPT does not resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after the date of receipt by the other Party of the Dispute Resolution Notice, then the dispute shall be escalated to an officer of MTC and an officer of Network Operator, neither of whom is then serving on the IPT, for their review and resolution within thirty (30) days after the receipt of the Dispute Resolution Notice.

clauses.head: 11.1.3 Except in the case of an emergency, exhaustion
clauses.name: 11.1.3 Arbitration
clauses.tail: vote of its members to take such action.
clauses.text: 11.1.3 Except in the case of an emergency, exhaustion of the foregoing procedures shall be a condition precedent to further Dispute Resolution proceedings. If the dispute is not resolved by the Parties’officers within forty-five (45) days after the receipt of the Dispute Resolution Notice, the dispute will be finally settled by binding arbitration conducted in accordance with the AAA Rules. Either Party may give the other Party notice, in accordance with the Rules, of its submission of such dispute to arbitration. Such notice shall also be given in accordance with the Rules, to the extent #10069598_v13 85 that the Rules are inconsistent with or supplement this notice requirement. Such arbitration shall take place in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, United States of America, before a single arbitrator. The Parties will agree upon the selection of a particular arbitrator as soon as reasonably practical after the notice described in this Section is given, but failing such agreement within thirty (30) days of such notices, the arbitrator will be selected in accordance with the Rules. All issues in the arbitration will be decided in accordance with Massachusetts law, without regard to its conflict of laws rules, and any applicable federal law. The determinations of the arbitrator will be final and binding upon the Parties to the arbitration, and judgment upon the award rendered by the arbitrator may be entered in any court having jurisdiction, or application may be made to such court for a judicial acceptance of the award and an order of enforcement, as the case may be. With the exception of applications to courts of competent jurisdiction for injunctive relief, the Parties stipulate that the submission of disputes to arbitration as provided in this Section, and arbitration pursuant thereto, shall be a condition precedent to any suit, action or proceeding instituted in any court or before any administrative tribunal with respect to such dispute. The arbitration provisions hereof shall, with respect to any dispute arising out of the Agreement, any SLA and any Wholesale Customer contract, survive the termination or expiration of the Agreement, any SLA and any Wholesale Customer contract. The Parties shall use their best commercial efforts to set the date of the arbitration within sixty (60) days after selection of the arbitrator but in no event shall the arbitration be set more than ninety (90) days after selection of the arbitrator. Discovery as permitted by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure then in effect will be allowed in connection with the arbitration to the extent consistent with the #10069598_v13 86 purpose of the arbitration and as allowed by the arbitrator. The decision or award of the arbitrator shall be rendered within fifteen (15) days after the conclusion of the presentation to and hearing by the arbitrator. The decision or award of the arbitrator shall be final, binding and non-appealable by the Parties. Each Party shall bear its own arbitration costs and expenses and all other costs and expenses of the arbitration shall be divided equally between the Parties; provided, however, the arbitrator may modify the allocation of fees, costs and expenses in the award in those cases where fairness dictates. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section, the IPT shall have the authority to stay the time periods set forth in this Section upon unanimous vote of its members to take such action.

clauses.text: 4. RESERVED OVERRIDING ROYALTY INTEREST A. Farmor shall except and reserve in each Agreement and Assignment of Operating Rights earned hereunder an overriding royalty-interest equal to twelve and one-half percent of eight eighth's (12.50% of 8/8) of the gross proceeds received from the sale of oil and/or gas produced from wells drilled hereunder without deductions of any kind. Upon the Payout of the first two (2) wells drilled and completed as a well capable of production in paying quantities Farmor reserves the right to escalate the reserved overriding royalty of twelve 5 Case: 5:16-cv-00150-JMH-REW Doc #: 1-1 Filed: 05/19/16 Page: 7 of 18 - Page ID#: 32 • � and one half percent (12.50%) to sixteen percent (16%). Upon Payout of all other wells drilled and completed as wells capable of production in paying quantities Farmor reserved the right to escalate the reserved overriding royalty of twelve and one half percent (12.50%) to eighteen and three fourth percent (18.75%). Should there be an outstanding twelve and one half percent (12.50%) non-participating royalty on oil in favor of a third party, then Farmor shall reserve in each Agreement and Assignment of Operating Rights earned hereunder an overriding royalty equal to one and one-half percent (1.5%) of the 5gross proceeds received from the sale of oil produced from wells drilled hereunder, without deductions of any kind, with the right to escalate said overriding royalty to three and one-half percent (3.5%) upon payout of the first two (2) wells drilled and completed as wells capable of production in paying quantities and the right to escalate said reserved one and one-half percent (1.5%) overriding royalty to six and one-half percent (6.5%) upon the Payout of all other wells drilled and completed as wells capable of production in paying quantities. However, if Farmor's interest in the acreage is less than one hundred percent (100%) or the working interest or if the Farmout acreage contributes less than one hundred percent (100%) of the total unit acreage, then said overriding royalty shall be reduced proportionately. Any reserved overriding royalty interest shall survive termination of this Agreement.

clauses.text: You are hereby notified that, under the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (the “Act”), effective December 26, 2007, this policy makes available to you insurance for losses arising out of certain acts of terrorism.

clauses.head: Terrorism is defined as any act certified by
clauses.name: Definition of Terrorism
clauses.tail: conduct of the United States Government by coercion.
clauses.text: Terrorism is defined as any act certified by the Secretary of the Treasury, in concurrence with the Secretary of State and the Attorney General of the United States, to be an act of terrorism; to be a violent act or an act that is dangerous to human life, property or infrastructure; to have resulted in damage within the United States, or outside the United States in the case of an air carrier or vessel or the premises of a United States Mission; and to have been committed by an individual or individuals as part of an effort to coerce the civilian population of the United States or to influence the policy or affect the conduct of the United States Government by coercion.

clauses.head: You should know that the insurance provided by
clauses.name: Federal terrorism reimbursement
clauses.tail: paid by the insurance company providing the coverage.
clauses.text: You should know that the insurance provided by your policy for losses caused by acts of terrorism is partially reimbursed by the United States under the formula set forth in the Act. Under this formula, the United States pays 85% of covered terrorism losses that exceed the statutorily established deductible to be paid by the insurance company providing the coverage.

clauses.head: However, if aggregate insured losses attributable to terrorist
clauses.name: Federal terrorism-loss cap
clauses.tail: amount of such losses that exceeds $100 billion.
clauses.text: However, if aggregate insured losses attributable to terrorist acts certified under the Act exceed $100 billion ina Program Year (January 1 through December 31), the Treasury shall not make any payment for any portion of the amount of such losses that exceeds $100 billion.

clauses.head: If aggregate insured losses attributable to terrorist acts
clauses.name: Insurer terrorism-loss cap
clauses.tail: accordance with procedures established by the Secretary of the Treasury.
clauses.text: If aggregate insured losses attributable to terrorist acts certified under the Act exceed $100 billion in a Program Year (January 1 through December 31) and we have met our insurer deductible under the Act, we shall not be liable for the payment of any portion of the amount of such losses that exceeds $100 billion, and in such case insured losses up to that amount are subject to pro rata allocation in accordance with procedures established by the Secretary of the Treasury.

In the event of loss sustained prior to the inception date of this coverage section, prior to the effective date of coverage for any additional insureds or prior to the effective date of any coverage added by endorsement, which would otherwise be covered under this coverage section, such prior loss shall be afforded coverage subject to the following: (a) an Insured or some predecessor in interest of such Insured carried a prior bond or policy, which at the time such prior loss was sustained, afforded some or all of the coverage of an Insuring Clause under this coverage section applicable to such prior loss; (b) such coverage continued without interruption from the time such prior loss was sustained until the inception date or effective date(s) as described above: (c) such prior loss was first Discovered by an Insured after the time allowed for discovery under the last such policy; and (d) some or all of the coverage of an Insuring Clause under this coverage section would be applicable to such prior loss.

clauses.text: B. INSURER CANCELLATION OR NONRENEWAL (1) The Insurer shall not be required to renew this Policy or any Insuring Agreement upon expiration of the Policy Period. This Policy or any Insuring Agreement may be cancelled or nonrenewed by the Insurer by giving to the Named Insured written notice stating when such action shall become effective and the reason(s) therefore. Notice will be mailed to the Named Insured by certified mail at the address set forth in Item 1 of the Declarations. The mailing of such notice as aforesaid shall be sufficient proof of notice, and this Policy shall terminate at the date and hour specified in such notice. The Insurer shall provide not less than: (a) twenty (20) days notice of its intent to cancel for nonpayment of premium; or (b) sixty (60) days notice of its intent to nonrenew; or (c) sixty (60) days notice of its intent to cancel for any of the following reasons: i. 1. iil. iv. fraud or material misrepresentation made by or with the knowledge of any Insured Person in obtaining the Policy, continuing the Policy or in presenting a Claim under the Policy; activities or omissions on the part of an Insured Person which increase any hazard insured against, including a failure to comply with loss control recommendations; change in the risk which materially increases the risk of Loss after coverage has been issued or renewed including, but not limited to, an increase in exposure due to regulation, legislation or court decision; loss or decrease of the Insurer's reinsurance covering all or part of the risk exposure by the Policy; determination by the Director that the continuation of the Policy would jeopardize the Insurer's solvency or would place the Insurer in violation of the insurance laws of this state or any other state; or violation or breach by the Insured of any Policy terms or conditions other than nonpayment of premium.

clauses.text: 4. Lease of fiber optic facilities. The Parties acknowledge that Texhoma leases from its affiliate Medicine Park Telephone Company ("Medicine Park") certain of the fibers used by Texhoma to provide service to PEG Bandwidth as described on Exhibit B, referred to herein as the "Burkburnett Fibers." Texhoma agrees to sublease to Comcell, for the term of the PEG Bandwidth Contract, the six Burkburnett Fibers described on Exhibit B at no monthly charge, to be used by Comcell to provide service to PEG Bandwidth pursuant to the PEG Bandwidth Contract. Texhoma warrants that as of the date of execution of this Assignment and Assumption Agreement, these fibers meet the Lease Fiber Optic Specifications in Exhibit B to the PEG Bandwidth Contract. Texhoma further agrees that during the term of this Sublease, Texhoma shall (i) maintain and repair the Burkburnett Fibers in accordance with the performance and maintenance standards provided in Exhibit B to the Maintenance Agreement between the Parties and (ii) promptly restore service in the event of a service disruption or Outage (as that term is defined in the Maintenance Agreement between the parties) at no charge to Comcell. In the event that Texhoma fails or refuses to maintain or restore the Burkburnett Fibers in accordance with the foregoing sentence, Comcell shall have the right to make the necessary repairs to the Burkburnett Fibers and shall be entitled to reimbursement for its reasonable costs incurred in making such 2 CONFIDENTIAL TEXHOMA_000935 Subject to Protective Order | U.S.D.C. E.D. Tex. Case No. 4:16-CV-815-ALM repairs. At the termination of the PEG Bandwidth Contract, this lease and the right of possession in these fibers shall revert to Texhoma and all obligations of this sublease shall terminate.

clauses.text: The term "Gross Sales” means the gross amount received by Tenant from all orders taken, placed or filled, and all sales and services made or rendered, and all rental fees, in or from the 3 Premises, whether for cash or credit, provided, however, that Gross Sales shall not include: (a) receipts from vending machines, coin-operated amusement devices and pay telephones; (d) any sales tax or other payment required by governmental law or regulation; (e) receipts from orders placed at the Premises, but filled elsewhere (provided that such exclusion shall apply only if such receipts are included in a percentage rent calculation at such other location); clauses.text: 5.1 Condition on Delivery. Landlord agrees to deliver possession of the Premises to Tenant upon the execution and delivery of this lease by Landlord and Tenant and upon delivery of required insurance evidence by Tenant. The date of delivery shall be referred to herein as the “Delivery Date.” Landlord and Tenant agree to confirm the Delivery Date in writing. Tenant shall accept the Building in its “as is” condition, with all faults and defects, on the Delivery Date, without representation or warranty.

Tenant may, atifs own cost and expense, equip and build out the Premises as Tenant deems necessary to operate its business ("Tenant's Work") in a manner consistent with a Gander Mountain prototype building. Tenant's Work shall be deemed Improvements under Section 14 of this Lease. Tenant agrees fo submit plans and specifications for Tenant's Work (“Tenant's Work Plans”) to Landlord. Landlord shall only have the right to approve, which approval shail not be unreasonably conditioned, withheld or delayed and which shail be deemed given if Landlord has not objected thereto within fifteen (15) days of such submission, any component of the Tenant's Work Plans which adversely affects the structural integrity of the Building. if Landtord does object thereto, Tenant shall be given fifteen (15) days in which to address such objection and resubmit revised Tenant's Work Plans to Landlord, whose approval shail be deemed given if Landlord has not objected thereto within fifteen (15) days of such submission. If Landlord still objects thereto, Tenant may terminate this Lease within fifteen (15) days following such objection.

Tenant shall pay all charges for gas, electricity, water, sewer, heat or other fuel or power or any other utility or service used on the Premises on or after the Delivery Dale 5 and during this Lease, All utilities to the Premises will be separately metered and the branch utility lines serving the Premises will not serve any other property,

Tenant may change its signs, at its cost, af any time during this Lease. Any sign installed must comply with all laws, ordinances, rules and regulations of any governmental authority, including any permitting requirements. Landlord shall not permit any other signs, billboards or posters to be displayed on any portion of the Building, the pylon or the Land, other than with the prior written approval of Tenant, which approval Tenant may withhold in its sole and absolute discretion. All signs shall be removed at the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

Tenant shall be responsible for the repair and maintenance of any such equipment during the term of this Lease.

clauses.text: 6.4 Definition. "Tax(es}” means all real estate taxes and assessments from time to time jevied or assessed against the Land (including without limitation against buildings, structures, lands, equipment and improvements therein) by municipal or other governmental authorities having jurisdiction together with all reasonable costs and expenses (including legal and other professional fees) incurred by the Landlord in good faith in contesting or appealing any such real estate taxes and assessments and all real estate taxes and assessments which may at any time be imposed in lieu of, in addition to or in substitution of same,

clauses.name: 6.2.1 Taxes
clauses.tail: Taxes shall survive the termination of this Lease.
clauses.text: 6.2.1 Taxes. Except as may be otherwise provided herein, commencing on the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant agrees to pay, as Additional Rent, Taxes which are due and payable on or after the Rent Commencement Date and during the Lease term {regardless of whether such Taxes are attributable to or on account of a prior year). Taxes for the initial and final years of the term shall be prorated on a per diem basis with Tenant only responsible for its portion of Taxes allocable to the Lease term. The parties’ obligations hereunder to prorate the last year’s Taxes shall survive the termination of this Lease.

clauses.tail: other proof of payment reasonably satisfactory to Tenant,
clauses.text: 6.2.2 Billing. Upon receipt of each tax bill from the taxing authority, Landlord shall furnish Tenant with a copy. A copy of a tax bill or assessment bill submitted by Landlord to Tenant shall at all times be conclusive evidence of the amount of Taxes assessed or fevied against the property to which such bill relates. Tenant shall have no abligation to make monthly escrow deposits for Taxes unless required by a fee mortgagee. Tenant shall pay to Landlord such Taxes at least fifteen (15) days prior to Landlord's due date; provided, however, that in the event that Landlord does not provide the applicable tax bill before at least twenty-one (21) days prior to Landlord’s due date, then Tenant shail not have to pay to Landlord such Taxes until five (5) days after receipt of such bill. Landlord agrees to timely pay all Taxes before the same become delinquent and to promptly forward to Tenant a copy of the "paid" tax bill or other proof of payment reasonably satisfactory to Tenant,

clauses.head: 6.2.3 Installments. If bylaw, any such Tax Is

clauses.text: 6.2.3 Installments. If bylaw, any such Tax Is payable or may at the option of the taxpayer be paid in installments (whether or not interest shail accrue on the unpaid balance of such Tax), Landlord shall pay the same (and any accrued interest on the unpaid balance of such Tax) in installments as the same respectively become due and only those installments coming due within the applicable year shail be included in Taxes for that year. Any Tax relating to a fiscal period of the taxing authority, a part of which period is included within the Lease term (after the Rent Commencement Date) and a part of which is included in a period of time before the Rent Commencement Date or after the Lease term, shall be adjusted so that Taxes shall only include that proportion of such Tax which falls after the Reni Commencement Date and within the Lease term. With respect to any Tax for public improvements or benefits which by law is payable, or at the option of the taxpayer may be paid in installments, Taxes shall include only those installments which become due and payable during the Lease term.

clauses.text: 6.3 Tenant Not to Pay Certain Taxes. Nothing in this Lease shall require Tenant to pay any giff, franchise, estate, inheritance, succession, capital levy or transfer tax of Landlord, or any income, excess profits, or revenue tax or any other tax, assessment, charge or levy upon the Rent payable by Tenant under this Lease, and all such taxes shall be paid or discharged by Landlord. Notwithstanding the foregaing, Tenant shall pay any tax assessment, charge or impost, which is a specific substitute in whole or in part for Taxes whether such tax, assessment, charge or impost is based upon real estate, gross receipts from real estate, transfer of real estate or any other source of determination or measurement; provided, however, that if fhe amount or rate of any such tax so levied against the income of Landlord as a specific substitute in whote or in part for such Taxes shall be increased by reason of any other income, receipts or property owned by Landlord, then and in that event, Tenant shall not be obligated to pay such increased amount, but only such tax as Landlord would be obligated {o pay in case it derived no income from any source other than the Premises nor owned any property other than the Premises.

Tenant shall have the right to request that the Landlord contest the amount or validity of any Tax upon the Premises and the right to inifiate such contest directly (whereupon Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant at Tenant's expense), in each case by appropriate legal proceedings and at Tenant's cost and expense. If any such contest results in a refund of Taxes, Tenant shall be entitled to any refund of any Tax and penalties or interest thereon. if any such contest results in additional Taxes, Tenant shall pay such Taxes if such contest was initiated by Landlord solely at Tenant's request or initiated by Tenant independently.

Tenant shall pay before delinquency all state, county and municipal taxes assessed during the term against Tenant's leasehold interest and personal property of any kind, owned by or placed in, upon or about the Premises by Tenant. clauses.text: 7. NET LEASE. After the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall have no right to cancel this Lease, seek a diminution of Rent, sue for damages, or assert any other contractual, legal or equitable remedy based either on (a) a claim that Landlord failed to deliver possession in accordance with the terms of this Lease; or (b) a claim that the size, location, layout, dimensions or construction of the Building, service areas (if any), sidewalks, parking or other common areas {if any), or any other facilities to be furnished by Landlord, were not completed or furnished in accordance with the terms of this Lease. Tenant understands, acknowledges and agrees that the Rent (including Base Rent, Percentage Rent and Additional Rent) reserved to Landiard in this Lease is net of all expenses, and that Landlord shail not be required to perform any work for or provide any services to Tenant or the Premises, except as may be specifically set out herein. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if during the term hereof Landlord is in default under any of its Lease obligations, Tenant shall have such rights al aw or equity to which it may be entitled, except that Tenant hereby waives any right to cancel or terminate this Lease or seek a diminution of Rent unless such right is explicitly reserved to Tenant under the terms of this Lease. Upon the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall be deemed ta have certified to Landford and the holder of any mortgage to which this Lease is, or shall thereafter be, subject and subordinate, that the Premises have been delivered fo it in accordance with the terms of this Lease and that possession thereof has been fully and completely accepted by Tenant who is then in possession of same, and that the term of this Lease and the opening for business to the public and the date for the payment of Rent hereunder have all theretofore commenced and that the Premises, the parking area, and all other portions of fhe Premises have been completed in accordance with the requirements and terms of this Lease and that there is not any offset of any Rent nor any violation of any of the Lease terms on the part of Landiord, except as may be specifically set out herein, in each case as of the Rent Commencement Date. The foregoing provisions shall be self-operative and no further instrument, letter or certificate shall be required by Landlord or any such mortgagee unless either said Landlord or mortgagee shall deem same appropriate in which event, in confirmation of the foregoing, Tenant shall, without cost to Landlord promptly execute, in writing, any instrument, letter and/or certificate containing the foregoing and such other like provisions in regard to the condition of the Premises, the Building, the Premises {and/or any portions thereof); the Rent, ferm and date of the opening of the Premises for business to the public as shall be requested by Landlord and/or said rnortgagee.

Subjectto all federal, state and local laws, rules, orders and regulations which are now existing or hereinafter enacted with respect to the Land and Premises, Tenant may use the Premises for any lawful purpose, including without limitation the following: retail sales and rental of hunting (including without limitation firearms and ammunition), fishing, camping and outdoor apparel, products, equipment and related accessories {and related retail sales and rental of videotapes, cassette tapes, compact discs or any other visual or audio products}, sale of other casual apparel, operation of a snack or food service, retail sales, rental and service of (and outside storage of) all-terrain vehicles and related sports vehicles, retail sales and rental of canoes, Kayaks and other similar vessels and other uses incidental therete (“Specific Permitted Use"), Tenant’s use of the Premises, the Building and the Land for parking, access and otherwise for operation of Tenant’s business thereon is exclusive to Tenant and, without limitation of the foregoing, Landlord may not do anything which interferes with the use of, or access or visibility to, the Premises and may not construct any additional buildings in, or modify the design or layout of, the Premises, without Tenant's prior written consent, which consent may be withheld by Tenant in its sole and absolute discretion. Thereafter, however, the duration and manner of Tenant's business operations, if any, shall be determined by Tenant in its sole discretion and nothing in this Lease may be deemed to impose any obligation upon Tenant to operate in the Premises or any portion thereof during the remainder of the Lease term. clauses.text: In the event Tenant elects to cease its business operations at the Premises after its opening, such cessation shall not be deemed to be an event of default hereunder, however, if business operations from the Premises cease for a periad in excess of nine (9) consecutive months (excluding cessations due to (a) damage or destruction of the Premises, redecoration, remodeling and/or refurbishing of the Premises or other causes described in Section 15 regarding damage, destruction and restoration, (b) events described in Section 16 regarding eminent domain or Section 25.9 regarding force majeure, (c} Landlord's default in the performance of its obligations hereunder or {d) events related to the inaccuracy of any representation or warranty made hereunder by Landlord), Landlord shail thereafter have the option of recapturing the Premises by terminating this Lease. Any such right of termination must be exercised, if at all, by providing Tenant with written notice following the expiration of such nine (9) month period. Said notice from Landlord shall provide for a date of termination of this Lease which shail be at least sixty (60) days but not more than ninety (90) days after the date of Landlord's notice and, upon such termination, Tenant and Landlord shall be relieved of and from any and ail further future liability or obligation to the other under this Lease. Upon such cessation of business operations, Tenant shall comply with all federal, state and local laws, rules, orders and regulations which are now existing or hereinafter enacted with respect to the Land and Premises. No provision of this Section or otherwise in this Lease may be deemed to extend a recapture right to Landlord in the event of an assignment or subleasing hereof, but the terms of this Section shall apply to the operation of any such assignee or sublessee.

Any breach of Landlord's representations or warranties in this Lease.

clauses.head: 13.2.3 Survival. This indemnity shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.
clauses.name: 13.2.3 Survival
clauses.text: 13.2.3 Survival. This indemnity shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

clauses.head: 14. IMPROVEMENTS AND ALTERATIONS. Alterations, installations, additions, and

clauses.tail: by Tenant in accordance with the terms of this Section.
clauses.text: 14. IMPROVEMENTS AND ALTERATIONS. Alterations, installations, additions, and improvements (collectively, “Improvements") to the Premises may be made by Tenant in accordance with the terms of this Section.

clauses.head: 14.1 Improvements: Plans. Tenant agrees to submit plans
clauses.name: 14.1 Improvements: Plans
clauses.tail: Lease, without the prior written consent of Landlord.
clauses.text: 14.1 Improvements: Plans. Tenant agrees to submit plans and specifications for any Improvements (“Improvement Plans”) to Landlord, Landlord shall only have the right to approve, which approval shall not be unreasonably conditioned, withheld or delayed and which shall be deemed given if Landlord has not objected thereto within fifteen (15) days of such submission, any component of the Improvement Plans which adversely affects the structural integrity of the Building. Otherwise, Tenant may make any other Improvements to the Premises, except as provided for in this Lease, without the prior written consent of Landlord.

clauses.head: 14.2 NoLiens. All such Improvements shall be performed
clauses.name: 14.2 No Liens
clauses.tail: to provide copies of such permits to Landlord).
clauses.text: 14.2 NoLiens. All such Improvements shall be performed at the expense of Tenantin a first class, workmanlike manner employing new materials of good quality. Tenant covenants and agrees nof to create, or suffer others to create, any lien or abligation against the Premises by reason of the Improvements, and to promptly pay for any such work and promptly cause any claim for such lien to be discharged or bond over such liens within thirty (30) days after Tenant becomes aware of such lien, at its sole cost, in accordance with applicable law, or to otherwise secure the Landiord to its satisfaction promptly upon request therefor by Landlord; to comply with all federal, state, and local governmental requirements; and to secure all necessary permits (and to provide copies of such permits to Landlord).

clauses.head: 45.1 Repair and Restoration. Ifthe Premises (including, without
clauses.name: 15.1 Repair and Restoration
clauses.tail: requirements of law and duly constituted governmental authority.
clauses.text: 45.1 Repair and Restoration. Ifthe Premises (including, without limitation, the Building) shail be damaged or destroyed in whole or in part by fire or other casualty during the Lease term, Tenant shall promptly repair and restore the Premises to a condition equal to its condition immediately prior to such damage or destruction and in conformity with and pursuant to all applicable requirements of law and duly constituted governmental authority.

clauses.head: 15.2 Insurance Proceeds. Insurance proceeds received on account
clauses.name: 15.2 Insurance Proceeds
clauses.tail: available by Tenant) shall be paid to Tenant.
clauses.text: 15.2 Insurance Proceeds. Insurance proceeds received on account of any damage to or destruction of the Premises (and any deductible carried with respect thereto by Tenant) shall be paid into an escrow mutually satisfactary to Landlord and Tenant, which escrow shall provide, among other terms, that such amounts be paid to Tenant, or as Tenant may direct, from time to time as the restoration of the Premises progresses, to pay or reimburse Tenant for the cost of such restoration upon written request of Tenant accompanied by evidence reasonably satisfactory to Landtord that an amount equal to the amount requested is then due and payable or has been paid and is properly a part of such cost. Upon receipt by Landlord of evidence reasonably satisfactory to it that such restoration has been completed and the cost thereof paid in full, and that there are ne mechanic's or similar fiens for labor or materials supplied in connection therewith, the balance, if any, of such insurance proceeds (and any amount otherwise made available by Tenant) shall be paid to Tenant.

clauses.head: 15.3. No Rent Abatement. No destruction of or
clauses.name: 15.3 No Rent Abatement
clauses.tail: Tenant on account of any such destruction or damage.
clauses.text: 15.3. No Rent Abatement. No destruction of or damage to the Premises, or any part thereof, whether such damage or destruction be partial or fotal or otherwise, shall entitle or permit Tenant to surrender or terminate this Lease or shall relieve Tenant from its liability to pay in full the Base Rent and all payments required to be paid by Tenant under this Lease, and Tenant hereby waives any rights now or hereafter conferred upon it by statute or otherwise to surrender this Lease or quif or surrender the Premises or any part thereof, or to receive any suspension, diminution, abatement or reduction of the Base Rent and all payments required to be paid by Tenant on account of any such destruction or damage.

clauses.head: 15.4 Lease Term. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary
clauses.name: 15.4 Lease Term
clauses.tail: paid, as is applicable, by Tenant to Landlord.
clauses.text: 15.4 Lease Term. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, if the Building shall be partially or totally damaged or destroyed within twenty-four (24) months of the expiration date of the then-current term and either (a) the time necessary to repair or rebuild the Building exceeds sixty (60) days or (b) the cost of restoration is reasonably estimated by Tenant fo exceed fifty percent (50%) of the replacement cost of the entire Premises and Improvernents, then Tenant may terminate this Lease by giving written notice to the other within thirty (30) days after the date of the damage. in the event of any such termination, Tenant shall not have any obligation to repair or restore the Premises and all insurance proceeds with respect to such casualty (and any deductible carried with respect thereto by Tenant} shall be assigned or paid, as is applicable, by Tenant to Landlord.

clauses.head: 16.1. Taking. tfall ofthe Premises shall be taken
clauses.name: 16.1 Taking
clauses.tail: Rent as may have been paid in advance.
clauses.text: 16.1. Taking. tfall ofthe Premises shall be taken by any public authority under the power of eminent domain or solid or conveyed in fieu of condemnation, this Lease shall terminate as of the day possession is taken by the public authority, and Tenant shall pay Rent up to that date with an appropriate refund by Landlord of such Rent as may have been paid in advance.

clauses.head: 16.2 Partial Taking. lfless than all of the
clauses.name: 16.2 Partial Taking
clauses.tail: to and including the date of such taking.
clauses.text: 16.2 Partial Taking. lfless than all of the Premises is taken and either (a) the taking would materially interfere with Tenant's business in the Premises in Tenant's reasonable judgment; (b) any portion of the Building, or any access to the interior of the Building or to any loading dock, is taken; (c) a portion of the Land is taken such that the parking ratio for the Premises falls below three and three-quarters (3,75) spaces per one thousand (1,000) square feet of Rentable Area (after taking into account all exclusions from the Rentable Area of the Premises) of the Premises remaining after any such taking; or (d) access to the Land or the Premises is taken, then Tenant shall have the option to terminate this Lease on the date the public authority takes possession, upon written notice to Landlord given within ninety (90) days after the date of such taking. In the event that this Lease shail terminate or be terminated under the provisions of this Section, the Rent and other charges hereunder shall be equitably adjusted. If any part of the Premises shall be so taken and this Lease shail not terminate or be terminated under the provisions of this Section (and Tenant closes all or a portion of its business to the public), then the Rent shall abate during the period of 13 restoration and if a portion of the Building is taken, the Rent all other charges hereunder shail be equitably apportioned according to the floor space so taken; and the Landlord, at its sole cost and expense, shail promptly make all repairs to the Premises to the extent necessary fo constitute the Building a complete architectural unit in accordance with plans approved by Landlord and Tenant, and restore the remaining portion of the Premises, including any permanent betterment and improvements thereto installed by Landlord, !o a condition equal to the condition immediately prior to such taking and in conformity with and pursuant to all applicable requirements of law and duly constituied governmental authority. In the event that this Lease shall be terminated, as herein provided, the parties hereto shall be released from their respective obligations hereunder accruing subsequent to the date on which this Lease is so terminated, but Tenant shall remain liable for the payment of Rent and the performance of all of the terms and provisions of this Lease due and owing or accrued up to and including the date of such taking.

clauses.head: 16.3 Condemnation Proceeds. All damages awarded for such
clauses.name: 16.3 Condemnation Proceeds
clauses.tail: or any other damages allowed Tenant by law.
clauses.text: 16.3 Condemnation Proceeds. All damages awarded for such taking, whether for the whole or a part of the Premises, shall belong to and be the property of Landlord whether such damages shall be awarded as compensation for diminution in value to the leasehold or to the fee of the Premises; provided, however, that Landlord shalt not be entitled to the award made to Tenant for loss of business, depreciation to and cost of removal of stock and fixtures, relocation expenses or any other damages allowed Tenant by law.

clauses.head: 17.1 By Tenant. if Tenant shall fail to
clauses.name: 17.1 Default by Tenant
clauses.tail: recovery of possession through any action or proceeding.
clauses.text: 17.1 By Tenant. if Tenant shall fail to (a) pay the Base Rent, Percentage Rent or ‘ Adgitional Rent within ten (10) days after written notice of such default has been given to Tenant by Landiord; (b) diligently proceed, after Tenant is aware of same (including by telephonic notice thereof to a designated emergency contact of Tenant or to the store manager), to cure any failure to perform any of the terms, conditions or covenants of this Lease to be performed or observed by Tenant with respect to the mainienance of the structural integrity of the Building; or (c) perform any of the other terms, conditions or covenants of this Lease to be performed or cbserved by Tenant for more than thirty (30) days after written notice of such default has been given to Tenant by Landlord (provided, however, that if any such default shall occur which cannot, with due diligence, be cured within a period of thirty (30) days from and after the giving of notice as aforesaid, then Tenant shall be deemed to be complying with such notice if Tenant promptly commences to take reasonable steps to cure such default during such time period and proceeds diligently thereafter to in fact cure such default), then in any such case, Landlord may, upon notice fo Tenant, terminate this Lease and recover possession of and re-enter the Premises without affecting Tenant's liability for past Rent and other charges due or future rent and other charges fo accrue hereunder. In the event of any such default, Landlord shail be entitled to recover from Tenant all other damages reasonably sustained by Landlord on account of the breach of this Lease. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Lease, Landlord shall not have any right to accelerate the Base Rent, Percentage Rent or Additional Rent hereunder. Any rents collected by Landlord from reletting the Premises shail be credited to the fulfillment of the agreements of Tenant under this Lease and to damages sustained by Landlord on account of Tenant's breach of this Lease; provided, however, in no event shall Tenant have any right to any payment from Landiord of any sums received by Landlord as a result of any reletting of the Premises in excess of the Rent payable by Tenant hereunder. The provisions herein shall be in addition and without prejudice to any other rights and remedies Landlord may have. Tenant waives any and all rights of redemption conferred by statute or otherwise, to the extent legally authorized, upon the expiration or sooner termination of the term hereof, or upon the entry of final unappealable judgment for recovery of possession through any action or proceeding.

clauses.head: 17.2 By Landiord. Should Landlord default in the
clauses.name: 17.2 Default by Landlord
clauses.tail: by telephone call to Landlord's Real Estate Department.
clauses.text: 17.2 By Landiord. Should Landlord default in the performance of the covenants required to be performed by Landiord under this Lease, Tenant may serve upon Landlord a notice 14 specifying the default and requiring performance by the Landlord within a period of time set forth in such notice, which shall not be fess than thirty (30) days after receipt of said written notice; provided, however, that if any such default shail occur which cannot, with due diligence, be cured within a period of thirty (30) days from and after the giving of notice as aforesaid, then Landlord shall be deemed to be complying with such notice if Landlord promptly commences to take reasonable steps to cure such default during such time period and proceeds diligently thereafter to in fact cure such default; or (b) Landlord defaults in the performance of the covenant of quiet possession set forth in Section 21 and Tenant does not have the quiet and undisturbed possession of the Premises, Tenant may serve upon Landiord a notice and requiring performance by the Landiord within five (5) days after receipt of said written notice. If Landlord fails to cure any such default within the applicable time period, Tenant may (a) cure Landiord's default and Landlord, on demand, shall reimburse Tenant the reasonable costs incurred by Tenant in curing Landlord’s default as aforesaid together with interest thereon at the Prime Rate pius two (2) percent per annum within thirly (30) days after demand therefor from Tenant to Landlord; and (b) if Tenant is denied possession of the Premises or if Tenant secures a2 final monetary judgment against Landlord with respect to such default, Tenant may, in addition to any other right or remedy Tenant may have at iaw or equity, abate the Base Rent, Percentage Rent and Additional Rent until such tlme as Tenant has possession of fhe Premises or such monetary judgment is salisfied, as is applicable. Notwithstanding any of the foregoing, Tenant shail have the right to remedy any defauit withaut notice in the event of emergency. Tenant shall notify Landlord orally prior to undertaking any emergency remedies by telephone call to Landlord's Real Estate Department.

clauses.head: 17.3 Remedies Cumulative. The rights and remedies of
clauses.name: 17.3 Remedies Cumulative
clauses.tail: provided by this Lease or allowed by law.
clauses.text: 17.3 Remedies Cumulative. The rights and remedies of Landlord and Tenant under this Lease shall be cumulative and the exercise of any of them shall not be exclusive of any other right or remedy provided by this Lease or allowed by law.

clauses.head: 17.4 Non-waiver. The waiver by Landlord or Tenant
clauses.name: 17.4 Non-waiver
clauses.tail: or as an estoppel against Landlord or Tenant.
clauses.text: 17.4 Non-waiver. The waiver by Landlord or Tenant of any breach of any covenant of this Lease shall be fimited to the particular instance and shall nat aperate or be deemed to waive any future breach of the same or any other covenant on the same or any other occasion, nor operate as a waiver of Landlord's right to enforce the payment of subsequent installments of Rent or any of Landiord’s or Tenant's rights under this Lease by such remedies as may be appropriate. No extension of time, forbearance, neglect or waiver on the part of Landlord or Tenant with respect to any one or more of the covenants, terms or conditions of this Lease, shail be construed as @ waiver of any of the other covenants, terms or conditions of this Lease, or as an estoppel against Landlord or Tenant.

clauses.head: 17.5 Landlord's Right to Cure. Landlord shall have
clauses.name: 17.5 Landlord's Right to Cure
clauses.tail: law in the case of nonpayment of Rent.
clauses.text: 17.5 Landlord's Right to Cure. Landlord shall have the right at any time after notice and expiration of any applicable cure period (or without notice in case of emergency) to make any payment or perform any act required of Tenant under any provision of this Lease. Nothing herein shall imply any obligation on the part of Landlord to make any payment or perform any act required of Tenant, and this exercise of the right to so do shall not constitute a release of any obligation or a waiver of any default. All payments made and all costs and expenses incurred in connection with any exercise of such right, from the respective dates of the making of such payments or the incurring of such costs and expenses shall be reimbursed to Landlord by Tenant within fifteen (15) days after notice from Landlord to Tenant of the amount of such payment tagether with interest thereon at the Prime Rate. in the event of nonpayment thereof, Landlord shail have the rights and remedies it would have hereunder or by law in the case of nonpayment of Rent.

clauses.head: 47.6 Prime Rate. "Prime Rate" means the base
clauses.name: 17.6 Prime Rate
clauses.tail: the Wall Street Journal {or any successor thereto).
clauses.text: 47.6 Prime Rate. "Prime Rate" means the base rate of interest (ar any successor to the base rate) from time to time established in the Wall Street Journal {or any successor thereto).

clauses.head: 17.7 Interest on Past Due Obligations. Any arnount
clauses.name: 17.7 Interest on Past Due Obligations
clauses.tail: cure any default by Tenant under this Lease,
clauses.text: 17.7 Interest on Past Due Obligations. Any arnount due from Tenant to Landiord hereunder which is not paid when due shall bear interest at the Prime Rate plus two (2) percent per 15 annum, but the payment of such interest shall not excuse or cure any default by Tenant under this Lease,

The commencement and termination dates hereof. 18.1.2 Lease. That this Lease is in full force and effect and has not been modified or amended {except as stated); 18.1.3 Conditions. The date to which rental has been paid; 18.1.6 Square Footage. The final calculation of the square footage of the Premises, and 18.1.7 Other. Any other information reasonably requested.

clauses.name: 18.2 Subordination

clauses.text: 18.2 Subordination. Upon written request of Landiord, Tenant shall subordinate its right hereunder to the interest of any ground fessor of the Premises and to the lien of any mortgage or other security interest now or hereafter in force covering the Premises; provided however, such subordination shall be upon the express condition that the validity of this Lease shail be recognized, and that, notwithstanding any default by the mortgagor, security party, beneficiary or ground lessee, as applicable, or any foreclosure or other proceedings, this Lease shall remain in full force and effect and Tenant's possession and right of use under this Lease shall not be disturbed as long as Tenant shail not be in default under any of the terms of this Lease afler notice and expiration of any applicable cure period. To evidence any such subordination, Tenant agrees to execute the Subordination, Nondisturbance and Attornment Agreement attached as Exhibit E ("Subordination Agreement"), but otherwise shall not be required to execute an agreement that differs materially from the attached form of Subordination Agreement; provided, however, that Tenant agrees tomake reasonable revisions fo the Subordination Agreement as may be requested by a mortgagee with respect to the application of insurance proceeds to the restoration of the Premises as set out in Section 15.

Landlord shall have the right at any time to sell or transfer its interest in the Land or Premises to any person, firm or corporation whatsoever; provided, however, that any such sale or transfer shail be subject to this Lease and that all of Landford's covenants and obligations contained herein shall be binding upon the subsequent owner or owners thereof and that such transferee from Landlord shall in writing assume the obligations of Landlord hereunder; further, provided, however, Landiord shall remain fully tiable on this Lease for any claims or other matiers arising out of the default, negligence or action of Landlord prior to such transfer. if Tenant executes an estoppel certificate in connection with a transfer of Landlord's interest herein, Landlord's ilabllity following the transfer of its interest herein shall be limited fo those matters set out by Tenant in such estoppel certificate.

His specifically understood and agreed that each successor landiord hereunder shall be deemed to have expressly assumed ail obligations hereunder of its predecessors with respect to this Lease. There shall be no personal (or entity) liability of Landlord (nor Landlord's agents, if any) in respect of any of the covenants, conditions or provisions of this Lease. in the event of a breach or default by Landlord of any of its obligations under this Lease beyond the applicable grace and/or cure period, or if Landlord shall otherwise be liable to Tenant for any reason whatsoever Tenant shail look solely to the interest, if any, of the applicable Landtord-in the Premises for the satisfaction of Tenant's remedies.

Tenant shail have the absolute right from time to time during the term hereof and without Landlord's further approval, written or otherwise, to collaterally assign or to grant and assign a mortgage or other security interest in Tenant's interest in this Lease and all of Tenant's property to Tenant's lenders in connection with Tenant's financing arrangements. Landiord agrees to execute such confirmation, certificates and other documents (except amendmenis to this Lease unless Landlord hereafter consents) as Tenant's lenders may reasonably request and in a form acceptable to Landlord and Landlord's counsel in connection with any such financing. Landlord may condition its acceptance thereof on the conditions that the applicable secured party unconditionally agree to restore the Premises to the condition required by this Lease on the removal of the secured property, and that the payment of Rent and Additional Rent, including any arrears, until lhe last day of the month in which the secured party is in possession of Tenant's property in the Premises be set forth.

clauses.name: 20.2 Corporate Action

clauses.name: 20.3 Valid

clauses.name: 20.4 Survival
clauses.text: 20.4 Survival. The foregoing representations and warranties shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

clauses.head: 21. COVENANT OF QUIET POSSESSION. Landlord covenants that

Tenant shall remove ifs trade fixtures and personal property prior to such surrender, If Tenant does not remove its trade fixtures and personal property prior to such surrender, Landlord may remove and dispose of the same for the account of and at the expense af Tenant.

clauses.text: 23. HAZARDOUS MATERIALS. 23.1 Definitions. As used in this Section, the following terms shall have the following meanings: 23.1.1 Environmental Laws. "Environmental Laws" means all federal, state and locallaws, including statutes, regulations, ordinances, codes, rules and other governmental restrictions and requirements relating fo the discharge of air poflutants, water pollutants or process waste water or otherwise relating fo the environment or solid, liquid or hazardous substances, materials or wastes, including, but not limited to, the Federal Solid Waste Disposal Act, the Federal Clean Air Act, the Federal Clean Water Act, the Federal Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976, the Federal Comprehensive Environmental Responsibility Cleanup and Liability Act of 1980, the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act of 1986, regulations of the Environmental Protection Agency, regulations of the Nuclear Regulatory Agency and regulations of any state department of natural resources or any other state environmental protection agency now or at any time hereafter in effect.

Such terms includes, without fimitation, [a] asbestos, [b] any material, substance or waste defined as a “hazardous waste” pursuant to section 1004 of the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (42 U.S.C. § 6901, ef seq.), [c] any material, substance or waste defined as a “hazardous substance” pursuant to Section 101 of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (42 U.S.C. § 9601, et seq.), [d] any material, substance or waste defined as a "regulated substance” pursuant to Subchapter IX of the 18 Solid Waste Disposal Act (42 U.S.C. § 6991, et seq.), or fe] petroleum and petroleum products.
