clauses.name: 23.1.4 Landlord Indemnified Person
clauses.tail: any director, officer, employee, contractor or agent of Landlord.
clauses.text: 23.4.4 Landlord indemnified Person. "Landiord Indemnified Person” means the Landlord and any director, officer, employee, contractor or agent of Landlord.

clauses.head: 23.2 Landlord Representations and Warranties. Landiord represents to
clauses.name: 23.2 Landlord Representations and Warranties
clauses.tail: tanks located in, on or about the Premises.
clauses.text: 23.2 Landlord Representations and Warranties. Landiord represents to Tenant that it has heretofore provided to Tenant full, accurate and complete copies of any and all reports, studies, and other information in its possession relating to the issue of the presence or suspected presence of any Hazardous Material in, on or about the Premises. Landlord represents and warrants to Tenant that, to Landiord's knowledge and belief without any independent inquiry or investigation: any handling, transportation, storage, treatment or usage of Hazardous Material that has heretofore occurred in, on or about the Premises has been in compliance with ail Environmental Laws: it has no knowledge that any leak, spill, release, discharge, emission or disposal of any Hazardous Materials has occurred in, on or about the Premises except in compliance with all Environmental Laws; to its knowledge, without any independent inquiry or investigation, the Premises {including the Building) is free of any Hazardous Material (including asbestos); and there are no underground storage tanks located in, on or about the Premises.

clauses.head: 23.3 Mutual Covenants. Landlord covenants and agrees that
clauses.name: 23.3 Mutual Covenants
clauses.tail: enacted with respect to the Land and Premises.
clauses.text: 23.3 Mutual Covenants. Landlord covenants and agrees that no Landlord indemnified Person shall use, generate, place, store, release, or otherwise dispose of, nor permit the use, generation, placing, storage, release or disposal of any Hazardous Material in, on or about the Premises except in strict accordance with ail Environmental Laws, whether in connection with the construction of the Premises or otherwise. Tenant covenants and agrees that no Tenant indemnified Person shall use, nor permit or suffer the use of, generate, place, store, release, or otherwise dispose of any Hazardous Material in, on or about the Premises except in strict accordance with all Environmental Laws. Without limitation of the foregoing, Landlord acknowledges and agrees that (a) the use of the Premises contemplated by Tenant involves the display, sale and demonstration of firearms, smokeless powder, black powder, ammunition and related materials, as well as camping fuel and other flammable, and certain petroleum products, and (b) such display, sale and demonstration does not violate any of the provisions of this Section to the extent Tenant conducts such display, sale and demonstration in strict accordance with ail Environmental Laws and other federal, state and local laws, rules, orders and regulations which are now existing or hereinafter enacted with respect to the Land and Premises.

clauses.head: 23.4 Landlord Indemnity. Landlord agrees to indemnify, defend
clauses.name: 23.4 Landlord Indemnity
clauses.tail: the expiration or earfler termination of this Lease.
clauses.text: 23.4 Landlord Indemnity. Landlord agrees to indemnify, defend and hold each Tenant Indemnified Person harmless from any and ail loss, cost, damage and expense that arises during or after the Lease term as a result of the inaccuracy or breach of any of the representations, warranties or covenants by Landlord contained in this Section 23. The costs covered by the Landlord’s Indemnification include, without limitation, costs incurred in the investigation of site conditions, reasonable attomeys' fees, engineers and other consultants, costs and expenses incurred by Tenant in exercising any of its rights hereunder and any damages suffered as a result of any termination of this Lease in accordance with this Section 23. Landlord has the right to ‘ provide the defense or, at Landlord's option upon request from Tenant, permit Tenant to conduct its own defense at Landlord's expense. Excluded from the Landlord's indemnification shall be any loss, cost, damage or expense resulting from the presence of any Hazardous Material introduced onto the Premises by any Tenant Indemnified Person, or placed inside fhe four walls of the Building or on, in or under the Premises by an invitee or customer of Tenant during the term of this Lease. This indemnity shall survive the expiration or earfler termination of this Lease.

clauses.head: 23.5 Tenant indemnity. Tenant hereby agrees to indemnify,
clauses.name: 23.5 Tenant Indemnity
clauses.tail: the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.
clauses.text: 23.5 Tenant indemnity. Tenant hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold each Landlord indemnified Person harmless from any and all loss, cost, damage and expense that arises during ar after the Lease term as a result of the introduction onto the Premises of any Hazardous Material by a Tenant Indemnified Person, or any invitee or customer of Tenant, or any breach by Tenant of any covenant contained in this Section 23. The costs covered by Tenant's indemnification include, without limitation, costs incurred in the investigation of site conditions, reasonable fees of attorneys, engineers and other consultants and costs and expenses incurred by Landlord exercising any of its rights hereunder. Tenant has the right to provide the defense or, at Tenant's option upon request from Landlord, permit Landlord to conduct its own defense at Tenant's expense. This indemnity shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

clauses.head: 23.6 Remedial Action, Landlord and Tenant agree to
clauses.name: 23.6 Remedial Action
clauses.tail: any interference with Tenant's use of the Premises.
clauses.text: 23.6 Remedial Action, Landlord and Tenant agree to promptly notify the other in the event such party becomes aware of the presence of any Hazardous Material other than any Hazardous Material which Tenant sells in the ordinary course of business, such as black powder, or any underground storage tank in, on or about the Premises. If any Landlord indemnified Person contaminates the Premises with any Hazardous Material, Landlord shall, at ifs sole cost, promptly commence and diligently pursue actions to clean up and/or remediate such Hazardous Material in accordance with all relevant Environmentat Laws. If any Tenant indemnified Person, or any invitee or customer of Tenant, contaminates the Premises with any Hazardous Material, Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense and after Landlord approval, promptly commence and diligently pursue actions {o clean up and/or remediate such Hazardous Material in accordance with all relevant Environmental Laws. lf any person or entity other than a Landlord Indemnified Person or a Tenant Indemnified Person, or any invitee or customer of Tenant, contaminates the Premises with any Hazardous Material, Landlord shall, if required by any governmental agency or if the presence of the contamination materially interferes with Tenant's use of the Premises, clean up and/or remediate such contamination in accordance with all relevant Environmental Laws. Any clean up or rededication of the Premises shail be done in such a manner as to minimize any interference with Tenant's use of the Premises.

clauses.head: 24.1 ‘Landlord's Compliance. The Premises are in compliance
clauses.name: 24.1 Landlord's Compliance
clauses.tail: the Premises with the Americans with Disabilities Act.
clauses.text: 24.1 ‘Landlord's Compliance. The Premises are in compliance with all federal, state and local laws, rules, orders and regulations which are now existing with respect to the Land and Premises as of the Commencement Date, provided that Landlord makes no representation with respect to the compliance of the Premises with the Americans with Disabilities Act.

clauses.head: 24.2 Tenant's Compliance. Tenant shall observe and comply
clauses.name: 24.2 Tenant's Compliance
clauses.tail: obtain any needed permit, license, approval or authorization.
clauses.text: 24.2 Tenant's Compliance. Tenant shall observe and comply with all federal, stale and local laws, rules, orders and regulations which are now existing or hereinafter enacted with respect to the Premises, including but not limited to the making of nonstructural alterations, insofar as they are due to Tenant's occupancy; provided, however, in | t such laws, rules, orders and regulations shall require structural changes; ind ubnot fo, the erection of a fire escape or exit, the same shall be complied with by L ole cost, unless such structural changes are required as a result of Tenant's Work, in which event, Tenant shail pay the costs. Tenant shall cause all construction work ta be done in a workmantike manner and in compliance with ail applicable faws, ordinances, rules, regulations and all lawful requirements of the nationat fire protection code. At no expense to Landiord, Landlord will cooperate with Tenant to obtain any needed permit, license, approval or authorization.

clauses.head: 25.1 Headings. The titles fo sections of this
clauses.name: 25.1 Headings
clauses.tail: any way limit or amplify the terms. ;
clauses.text: 25.1 Headings. The titles fo sections of this Lease are solely for convenience of reference and shall not in any way limit or amplify the terms.

clauses.head: 252 Successors and Assigns. All of the terms
clauses.name: 25.2 Successors and Assigns
clauses.tail: their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors and assigns.
clauses.text: 252 Successors and Assigns. All of the terms and conditions contained in this Lease shall Inure to and be binding upon Landlord and Tenant and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors and assigns.

clauses.head: 25.3 Exhibits. In the event of any conflicts
clauses.name: 25.3 Exhibits
clauses.tail: exhibit, the terms of this Lease will prevail.
clauses.text: 25.3 Exhibits. In the event of any conflicts between the terms of this Lease and any exhibit, the terms of this Lease will prevail.

clauses.head: 25.4 Access to Premises. Upon reasonable prior notice,
clauses.name: 25.4 Access to Premises
clauses.tail: to unreasonably interfere with Tenant's business by such entry.
clauses.text: 25.4 Access to Premises. Upon reasonable prior notice, but in no event less than twenty-four (24) hours (except in the case of an emergency), Landlord may enter the Premises during Tenant's business hours for purposes of inspection, to show the Premises to prospective purchasers and lenders, or to perform maintenance and repair obligations imposed upon Landiord by this Lease. Landlord agrees not to unreasonably interfere with Tenant's business by such entry.

clauses.head: 25.5 Entire Agreement. This Lease contains all covenants
clauses.name: 25.5 Entire Agreement
clauses.tail: except in writing signed by Landiord and Tenant.
clauses.text: 25.5 Entire Agreement. This Lease contains all covenants and agreements between Landlord and Tenant. No prior agreements or understandings pertaining thereto shall be valid or of any force or effect and the covenants and agreements of this Lease shall not be altered, modified or amended except in writing signed by Landiord and Tenant.

clauses.head: 25.6 Severability. Any provision of this Lease which
clauses.name: 25.6 Severability
clauses.tail: shall nevertheless remain in full farce and effect.
clauses.text: 25.6 Severability. Any provision of this Lease which shall prove to be invalid, void or iNegal shall in no way affect, impair or invalidate any other provision hereof and the remaining provisions hereof shall nevertheless remain in full farce and effect.

clauses.head: 25.7 Governing Law. This Lease shall be governed
clauses.name: 25.7 Governing Law
clauses.tail: the state in which the Premises are located.
clauses.text: 25.7 Governing Law. This Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the state in which the Premises are located.

clauses.head: 25.8 Naftices. All notices to be given by
clauses.name: 25.8 Notices
clauses.tail: Department 4567 American Boulevard West Minneapolis, MN 55437
clauses.text: 25.8 Naftices. All notices to be given by Landlord or Tenant shall be in writing and shall be personally delivered, sent registered or certified mail, postage prepaid, or sent by a nationally recognized courier service that issues a receipt, to the other party af the address in this Section (or fo such other address as may be designated by notice to the other party) and shail be deemed given upon the earfier of personal delivery, the date postmarked, delivery fo such courier or the refusal to accept such service: If to Landlord: Pathmark Stores, Inc. Attn: Senior Vice President of Retail Development 200 Milik Street Carteret, New Jersey 07008 With a copy to: Pathmark Stores, Inc. Attn: Vice President and Real Estate Counsel 200 Milik Street Carteret, New Jersey 07008 if fo Tenant: Gander Mountain Company Attn: Real Estate Department 4567 American Boulevard West Minneapolis, MN 55437 With a capy to: Gander Mountain Company Attn: Legal Department 4567 American Boulevard West Minneapolis, MN 55437

clauses.head: 25.9 Force Majeure. Time periods or deadlines for
clauses.name: 25.9 Force Majeure
clauses.tail: (10) days of the event causing the delay.
clauses.text: 25.9 Force Majeure. Time periods or deadlines for Landlord's performance under any provisions of this Lease shall be extended for periods of time during which performance is prevented due to circumstances beyond the Landlord's control, including, without limitation, labor disputes, embargoes, governmental restrictions or regulations, inclement weather and other acts of God, acts of Tenant, war or other strife, Time periods or deadlines for Tenant's performance under any provisions of this Lease (other than the payment of money) shall be extended for periods of time during which performance is prevented due to circumstances beyond Tenant's control, including, without limitation, labor disputes, embargoes, governmental restrictions or regulations, inclement weather and other acts of God, acts of Landlord, war or other strife. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any extension of time hereunder shall be conditioned upon the party seeking an extension of time delivering written notice of such delay to the other party within ten (10) days of the event causing the delay.

clauses.head: 25.10 No Partnership. Nothing contained in this Lease
clauses.name: 25.10 No Partnership
clauses.tail: or any other association between Landiord and Tenant.
clauses.text: 25.10 No Partnership. Nothing contained in this Lease shall be deemed or construed by the parties hereto or by any third person to create a principal and agent relationship, a partnership, a joint venture, or any other association between Landiord and Tenant.

clauses.head: 25.11 Memorandum of Lease. The parties agree not
clauses.name: 25.11 Memorandum of Lease
clauses.tail: Tenant may, at its cost, record the Memorandum.
clauses.text: 25.11 Memorandum of Lease. The parties agree not to record this Lease. Landlord and Tenant agree to execute, acknowledge and deliver, at the time of execution hereof, a Memorandum of Lease in the form attached as Exhibit G. Tenant may, at its cost, record the Memorandum.

clauses.head: 25.42 Consent. Exceptas expressly provided otherwise, wherever in
clauses.name: 25.12 Consent
clauses.tail: shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.
clauses.text: 25.42 Consent. Exceptas expressly provided otherwise, wherever in this Lease Landlord or Tenant is required to give its consent or approval, such consent or approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

clauses.head: 25.13 Waiver of Landlord's Lien. Landiord hereby waives
clauses.name: 25.13 Waiver of Landlord's Lien
clauses.tail: Tenant's furniture, fixtures, supplies, equipment and inventory.
clauses.text: 25.13 Waiver of Landlord's Lien. Landiord hereby waives any contractual, statutory, or other Landlord's lien on Tenant's furniture, fixtures, supplies, equipment and inventory.

clauses.head: 25.14 Brokers. Landlord and Tenant represent and warrant
clauses.name: 25.14 Brokers
clauses.tail: related to a broker hired by such party.
clauses.text: 25.14 Brokers. Landlord and Tenant represent and warrant to the other that, except for any commission or fee owed to Levin Realty Services, LLC, which amountis to be paid by Landlord by separate agreement, there are no other claims for brokerage commissions or finder's fees in connection with the execution of this Lease and each party agrees to indemnify the other against and hold them harmless from ail liabilities arising from any such claim related to a broker hired by such party.

clauses.head: 25.15 Counterparts/Facsimile Copies. This Lease may be executed in
clauses.name: 25.15 Counterparts/Facsimile Copies
clauses.tail: executed copies of this Lease shall be binding.
clauses.text: 25.15 Counterparts/Facsimile Copies. This Lease may be executed in counterparts, all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Landlord and Tenant agree that facsimile executed copies of this Lease shall be binding.

clauses.head: 25.16 Holding Over. If Tenant shall retain possession
clauses.name: 25.16 Holding Over
clauses.tail: to be any period longer than month to month.
clauses.text: 25.16 Holding Over. If Tenant shall retain possession of the Premises after fermination or expiration of this Lease without Landlord's consent, such holding over shall be deemed to constitute a tenancy from month ta month, upon the same terms and conditions as herein provided except that the monthly Base Rent shall be increased to two hundred percent (200%) of the monthly Base Rent in effect immediately prior fo such holdover. in no event shall the tenancy created by such holdover be deemed to be any period longer than month to month.

clauses.head: 25.17 Time of the Essence. Time shall be of
clauses.name: 25.17 Time of the Essence
clauses.tail: essence in interpreting the provisions of this Lease.
clauses.text: 25.17 Time of the Essence. Time shall be of the essence in interpreting the provisions of this Lease.

clauses.head: 25.18 Acceptance. The offer to lease set forth
clauses.name: 25.18 Acceptance
clauses.tail: and be of no further force or effect.
clauses.text: 25.18 Acceptance. The offer to lease set forth in this Lease must be accepted by Landlord by the delivery of fully executed facsimile copies hereof (with originals to follow) to Tenant - by April 16, 2004; otherwise, this offer may, at Tenant's sole option, be terminated and be of no further force or effect.

clauses.head: 25.19 Lease Provisions. All provisions of this Lease
clauses.name: 25.19 Lease Provisions
clauses.tail: authorship or alleged authorship of any provision hereof,
clauses.text: 25.19 Lease Provisions. All provisions of this Lease have been negotiated by both parties at arm's length and neither party shall be deemed the scrivener of this Lease. This Lease shail not be construed for or against either party by reason of the authorship or alleged authorship of any provision hereof,

clauses.head: 26. CONDITIONS TO TENANT'S OBLIGATIONS. In addition to
clauses.name: 26. Conditions to Tenant's Obligations
clauses.tail: terminate this Lease by written notice to Landiord:
clauses.text: 26. CONDITIONS TO TENANT'S OBLIGATIONS. In addition to any other rights of termination in this Lease, Tenant's obligations under this Lease are subject to the satisfaction, in Tenant's sole and absolute discretion, of the following conditions ("Tenant Conditions"), and if any of such conditions are nat satisfied on or before the Contingency Date, then Tenant only may, in its sole election, terminate this Lease by written notice to Landiord:

clauses.head: 26.1 Affidavit: Subordination Agreement. On or before the
clauses.name: 26.1 Affidavit; Subordination Agreement
clauses.tail: Landlord has executed an owner's or lessor’s affidavit.
clauses.text: 26.1 Affidavit: Subordination Agreement. On or before the later of forty-five (45) days following the date of execution of this lease or the Commencement Date (“Contingency Date’), (a) any party holding a mortgage or other similar interest in the Land has executed a Subordination Agreement; and (b) Landlord has executed an owner's or lessor’s affidavit.

clauses.head: 26.2 Survey. On or before the Contingency Date,
clauses.name: 26.2 Survey
clauses.tail: a survey of the Land and the Premises.
clauses.text: 26.2 Survey. On or before the Contingency Date, Tenant shall be satisfied in its sole discretion with a survey of the Land and the Premises.

clauses.head: 26.3 Phase | Environmental Audit. On or before
clauses.name: 26.3 Phase I Environmental Audit
clauses.tail: discretion with the environmental condition of the Premises.
clauses.text: 26.3 Phase | Environmental Audit. On or before the Contingency Date, Tenant shall be satisfied in its sole discretion with the environmental condition of the Premises.

clauses.head: 26.4 Completion of Documents. On or before the
clauses.name: 26.4 Completion of Documents
clauses.tail: of this Lease with all such provided information.
clauses.text: 26.4 Completion of Documents. On or before the Contingency Date, this Lease and all exhibits hereto shall be completed to the full satisfaction of Tenant, including the completion of all blanks, bracketed references and incomplete exhibits. Upon satisfaction of such, Landlord and Tenant agree to execute a conformed copy of this Lease with all such provided information.

clauses.head: 26.5 Access: Parking. On or before the Contingency
clauses.name: 26.5 Access: Parking
clauses.tail: exclusions from the Rentable Area of the Premises).
clauses.text: 26.5 Access: Parking. On or before the Contingency Date, Tenant shall be satisfied with the access to the Premises and the availability of adequate parking for the Premises. Such satisfaction shall require at a minimum, but shall not be limited fo, (a) the conversion of the right-in right-out access from Harry “L” Drive to full access (“Access Conversion’); and (b) demonstration of a parking ratio at least equal to four and two-tenths (4.2) parking spaces for each one thousand (1,000) square feet of Rentable Area of the Premises (after taking into account all exclusions from the Rentable Area of the Premises).

clauses.head: 26.6 No Change. On or before the Contingency
clauses.name: 26.6 No Change
clauses.tail: satisfying any of the conditions set out herein.
clauses.text: 26.6 No Change. On or before the Contingency Date, there has been no material adverse change in the marketability of the Premises, the access to the Premises, the availability of utilities to the Premises, the environmental condition of the Premises or the Premises, the condition of the Building and the Premises or the facts and circumstances satisfying any of the conditions set out herein.

clauses.head: 2i. EASEMENT OR OPERATION AGREEMENTS: GOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENTS. Landiord
clauses.name: 27. Easement or Operation Agreements; Governmental Agreements
clauses.tail: accruing to Landlord with respect fo the Premises.
clauses.text: 2i. EASEMENT OR OPERATION AGREEMENTS: GOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENTS. Landiord agrees that it will not (a) enter into any agreements with respect to the Premises, including without limitation any easement and/or operation agreements and any development, restrictions or other agreement with a governmental authority; or (b) amend any existing such agreements (including without limitation those set forth on Exhibit G), in each case without the prior written consent of Tenant, which consent Tenant may not unreasonably withhold. With respect to all such agreements, Landlord agrees (1} to perform and observe all of the terms, conditions and covenants imposed upon a party thereunder as applicable to the Land and the Premises; (2) to use reasonable efforts and diligence to enforce ail of the provisions thereof against all of the parties thereunder; (3) not to modify or amend any such agreement in any manner without Tenant's prior written consent, which consent Tenant may not unreasonably withhold; and (4) that the Premises shall include the easements and other appurtenant rights derived therefrom and any other any rights or benefits accruing to Landlord with respect fo the Premises.

clauses.head: 28. WAIVER OF TRIAL BY JURY. Landlord and
clauses.name: 28. Waiver of Trial by Jury
clauses.tail: Premises, and/or any claim of injury or damage.
clauses.text: 28. WAIVER OF TRIAL BY JURY. Landlord and Tenant do hereby waive trial by jury in any action, proceeding or counterclaim brought by either against the other upon any matters whatsoever arising oul of or in any way connected with this Lease, Tenant's use or occupancy of the Premises, and/or any claim of injury or damage.

clauses.text: 1. Subordination. Tenant agrees that the Lease and all of the terms, covenants and provisions thereof are, and shall al aif times continue to be, subordinate in all respects to the lien of the Mortgage and to all renewals, modifications, supplements, replacements and extensions thereof with the same force and effect as if the Mortgage had been executed, delivered and recorded prior to the execution and delivery of the Lease.

clauses.head: 2. Nondisturbance. So long as neither the Lease
clauses.name: Exhibit E 2. Nondisturbance
clauses.tail: the terms of the Mortgage shall be resolved in favor of the Lease.
clauses.text: 2. Nondisturbance. So long as neither the Lease nor Tenant's right of possession of the Premises pursuant thereto shall have been terminated by reason of a default by Tenant under the Lease (beyond any period provided Tenant in the Lease fo cure such default), Lender agrees that Tenant's possession of the Property and Tenant's other rights and privileges under the Lease or any extensions or renewals thereof, shall not be diminished, disturbed or interfered with by Lender and if any action or proceeding is commenced by Lender for the foreclosure of the Mortgage and/or the sale of the Property, Tenant shall not be named as a party defendant therein unless required by law but only provided the terms of this Section are complied with. Should Lender become the owner of the Property, or should the Property be sold by reason of foreclosure, or other proceedings brought to enforce the Mortgage, or should the Property be transferred by deed in tieu of foreclosure, or should any portion of the Property be sold under a trustee's sale, the Lease will continue in full force and effect as a direct lease between the Lender and/or the succeeding owner of the Premises, as he case may be, and the Tenant, upon and subject to all of the ferms, covenants and conditions of the Lease for the balance of its term as it may be extended, and Lender, or any successor owner of the Premises, will be bound by all of the terms of the Lease, Lender agrees that so jong as the Lease ts in full force and effect, no proper exercise by Tenant of its rights under the Lease shall constitute a default under the Mortgage or require Lender's consent, and that any conflict between the terms of the Lease and the terms of the Mortgage shall be resolved in favor of the Lease.

clauses.head: 3. Attornment. Tenant agrees that the institution of
clauses.name: Exhibit E 3. Attornment
clauses.tail: personally against Landlord for any defaults or acts of Landiord.
clauses.text: 3. Attornment. Tenant agrees that the institution of any action or other proceedings by Lender under the Mortgage in order to realize upon Landlord's interest in the Property shall not result in the cancellation or termination of the Lease or Tenant's obligations thereunder. If Lender shall become the owner of the Property by reason of the foreclosure of the Mortgage or the acceptance of a deed in lieu of foreclosure or otherwise: (a) the Lease shall not be terminated or affected thereby; (b} Tenant shail attorn to Lender and recognize Lender as its fandiord under the Lease for the unexpired term of the Lease, subject to all of the terms and conditians of the Lease and such attornment shall be effective and self-operative without the execution of any further instrument on the part of Lender or Tenant; (c) if, by operation of law, or otherwise, the commencement of any action or other proceedings by Lender under the Mortgage or the entry into and taking possession of the Premises shall result in the cancellation or termination of the Lease or Tenant's obligations thereunder, Tenant shall, upon request, execute and deliver a new lease of the Premises containing the same terms and conditions as contained in the Lease (Including all right of renewal and extension), for the remaining term thereof, and (d) Lender shall not be: (i) responsible or liable for any monetary damages as a result of, or obligated to cure, any defaults by Landlord under the Lease provided ihat the foregoing shal! not be deemed to relieye Lender or any other party from the obligation to perform any obligation of the Landlord under the Lease which remains unperformed at the time that Lender or any other party succeeds to the interest of Landlord under the Lease; (il) subject to claims, defenses or offsets under the Lease or against Landlord which arose or existed prior to the time Lender obtains possession of the Property provided that the foregoing shall not be deemed to (A) relieve Lender or any other party from the obligation to perform any obligation of the Landlord under the Lease which remains unperformed at the time that Lender or any other party succeeds to the interest of Landlord under the Lease, or (B) modify or waive any rights of self-help, set-off, abatement or termination expressly provided in the Lease; (iii) bound by any rent paid more than thirty (30) days in advance; {iv} liable for the return of any security deposit paid to any prior fandiord, including Landlord, unless Lender has actually received the same; or (v) bound by any amendment or modification of the Lease made without its prior written consent (Lender agrees not to unreasonably withhold or delay its consent to any proposed amendment or modification which does not materially and adversely affect Lender's security). Nothing in this Section shail be deemed a waiver of any rights or remedies that Tenant may possess or claim personally against Landlord for any defaults or acts of Landiord.

clauses.head: 4. Right To Cure Landiord’s Default. Notwithstanding any
clauses.name: Exhibit E 4. Right To Cure Landlord's Default
clauses.tail: was given or made to Landlord.
clauses.text: 4. Right To Cure Landiord’s Default. Notwithstanding any provisions of the Lease to the contrary, no notice of cancellation of the Lease by Tenant shall be effective unless Lender shall have first received notice of the default giving rise to such cancellation and shail have failed, for a period of thirty (30) days after receipt thereof, to cure such default. Tenant will forward to Lender coples of any statement, notice, claim or demand given or made by Tenant to Landlord, in all cases by the same method as the statement, notice, claim or demand was given or made to Landlord.

clauses.text: 5. Assignment of Lease. Tenant acknowledges that Landlord is assigning the Lease and rents thereunder to Lender as security for the note given by Landlord to Lender. Tenant agrees that upon receipt of a written notice from Lender, it wilt thereafter pay to Lender directly all rent and other amounts due or to become due from time to time under the Lease. Lender acknowledges it agrees that Tenant shall have the right to rely upon any such notice from Lender and that Tenant may pay such rents and other amounts to Lender without any obligation or right to determine the actual existence of the right of Lender to receive such rents and other amounts, notwithstanding any notice from or claim of Landlord to the contrary. Landlord shall have no right or claim against Tenant for any such rents and other amounts so paid by Tenant to Lender and Landlord waives and releases any such claims. Landlord and Lender agree that Tenant shall be credited under the Lease for any payments sent to Lender pursuant to such written notice. in addition, Lender agrees to indemnify and hold harmless Tenant from and against any and all claims by Landlord in any way related to Tenant's compliance with this Section.

clauses.text: 6. Casualty and Gondemnation. Such situation holders shall fill the situation within seven (7) days from the date of the above notification to the Chapel Chairman. In the event the situation is not filled by bid, the most junior qualified situation holder will be permanently assigned to the vacancy and the volunteer shall return to his regular situation.

clauses.text: 5.10 Bonding. Any person required to be bonded under the provisions of ERISA, including without limitation the Trustees, Administrator, Investment Managers, Custodians (and any other employees, agents or other representatives of the Trust handling monies, Securities and negotiable paper on behalf of the Trust or otherwise entrusted with any portion of the Trust Fund), shall be bonded under a fidelity bond issued by a reputable insurance carrier in the amount required by Section 412 of ERISA. The Board shall, in its sole discretion, have the authority to require the bonding of any other employee of the Trust and to require bonds above the minimum amount. The cost of premiums for such bonds shall be paid out of the Trust Fund.

clauses.text: 9.4 Failure to Make Employer Contributions. (a) The failure of any Employer to make Employer contributions to the Trust Fund when due shall not relieve any other Employer of its obligation to make Employer contributions. The costs and expenses incurred in the collection of Employer contributions shall be paid from the Fund. Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, upon the failure of any Employer to make Employer contributions to the Trust Fund required by the Plan, the Trust Fund or a Collective Bargaining Agreement, within ten (10) days after such payments are due and payable, the Board (or its counsel or other duly authorized designee) may compel and enforce payment in any manner it deems proper (including, without limitation, the assessment of interest, at a rate calculated in accordance with Section 9.5, from the date such payments first became due and payable).

clauses.head: (b) In addition, the Board may require a delin-

clauses.text: (b) In addition, the Board may require a delinquent Employer to pay a liquidated damage penalty equal to the greater of interest on, or twenty percent of, the unpaid contributions, plus all costs and expenses incurred by the Trustees arising out of the collection of such delinquent Employer contributions (including, without limitation, court costs and attor- neys’ fees).

(a) In addition to any other enforcement remedies that may exist under applicable law or any Collective Bargaining Agreement or any other agreement requiring Employer contributions to the Trust Fund, the Board is authorized and empowered to initiate whatever action or proceedings may be proper and necessary in its sole and absolute discretion for the enforcement of an Employer’s contribution obligations to the Trust Fund (including, but not limited to, proceedings at law or in equity, arbitration and any other remedies that generally would be available for the enforcement of said obligation to contribute to the Trust Fund).

clauses.head: (b) A delinquent Employer shall be liable for any

In addition to any other remedies to which the Board or any duly authorized Committee may be entitled hereunder, in the event that an Employer fails to make required contributions to the Trust Fund, in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, or any Collective _ Bargaining Agreement or other agreement, and any rules or gquide- lines promulgated by the Board pursuant hereto (hereinafter collectively referred to as "unpaid contributions"), the Board may bring an action on behalf of the Trust Fund pursuant to Sections 502(g) 2) and 515 of ERISA to enforce the Emplioyer’s obligation to contribute to the Trust Fund.

clauses.tail: under Section 4221(b)(1) of ERISA for any amount demanded.
clauses.text: “9,10 Arbitration of Withdrawal Liability Disputes. . Any and all claims by third parties (including Employers) against the Trust Fund concerning the assessment by the Trust Fund of withdrawal liability under Sections 4201 through 4219 of ERISA .. which cannot. be resolved between the claimant and the Trust Fund shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts (either State or Federal), but shall be subject to determination only by arbitration before an arbitrator designated by the American Arbitration Association (the "AAA") in accordance with its Multi- Employer Pension Plan Arbitration Rules for Withdrawal Liability Disputes. Any decision or award by such arbitrator shall be final and binding upon the parties and shall be enforceable in the United States district court. All such arbitrations shall be held in the New York City office of the AAA and shall be governed by New York State Law to the extent not superceded by ERISA. Any actions to stay, to confirm, to set aside, or to modify an award hereunder shall be brought in the State of New York, County of New York. ‘The failure by a claimant to seek arbitration within the time period prescribed by ERISA shall not affect the Trust Fund‘s right to bring an action in State or Federal court under Section 4221(b)(1) of ERISA for any amount demanded.

clauses.text: Economic or Business Reasons 3-D. 1. The right of the Publisher at any time to lay off men for economic or business reasons is. hereby recognized. Each Publisher shall have the right from time to time to increase or reduce the number of routes, carriers or deliveries, and to _ combine, amalgamate, condense, alter, discontinue or otherwise rearrange routes or deliveries as such Publisher may find necessary or desirable, provided, however, that if any such change results in the layoff of any employee then employed by the Publisher as a regular situation holder the layoff may be reviewed by the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board to ascertain whether it was for economic or business reasons.

The words “economic or business reasons” are used herein in their usual and ordinary | sense and their meaning shall not be confined by any claim of prior practice or interpretation to any particular economic or business reasons, but they are meant to include all reasons of an economic or business character.

clauses.text: 4-A, 8. No man may hold a regular situation in more than one (1) shop.

clauses.head: 4-A. 4, No man shall be employed or promoted unless he is qualified and competent for the work or the job in question.
clauses.name: 4-A. 4. Competence
clauses.text: 4-A. 4, No man shall be employed or promoted unless he is qualified and competent for the work or the job in question.

clauses.head: 4-A. & Should the application of the foregoing
clauses.name: 4-A. 5. Legal conformity
clauses.tail: against whom such order, judgment, or decree shall run and for the effective term thereof solely.
clauses.text: 4-A. & Should the application of the foregoing procedure for hiring and promotion be in conflict with any order, decree, or judgment directed against any signatory Publisher or the Union by the National Labor Relations Board or any Court of competent jurisdiction the procedure shall be changed to conform with such order, judgment, or decree, with respect to the parties against whom such order, judgment, or decree shall run and for the effective term thereof solely.

clauses.head: Vacant Situations 4-B. In the event a regular
clauses.name: 4-B. Vacant Situations
clauses.tail: moved up in accord with Section 4-A. 2. (c) as aforesaid.
clauses.text: Vacant Situations 4-B. In the event a regular situation becomes vacant or jis newly created, it shall be filled immediately in accord with Section 4-A. 2. (c) of this agreement but on a temporary basis. It shall be . filled permanently on the basis of qualification and competence from among the regular situation holders In accord with their senjority standing; provided, however, that when any such vacancy occurs or a new regular situation is created, it shall be posted by the Publisher within one (1) week and for four (4) weeks thereafter and shall be filled immediately at the end of that four (4) week period. Such job and the subsequent vacancies not in excess of five created by filling it shall 26 be filled by regular situation holders provided that the last such subsequent vacancy shall be filled only by a relayman, relief man, bulldog routeman or floorman. The last vacancy thus created shall be filled by the employee moved up in accord with Section 4-A. 2. (c) as aforesaid.

clauses.head: 4-C. If any unemployed extra is offered a situa-
clauses.name: 4-C. Refusal of situations
clauses.tail: promotional priority NHst or for purposes of layoff.
clauses.text: 4-C. If any unemployed extra is offered a situation in accordance with the above provisions for which he is qualified and competent and refuses to accept the same, he is to be placed at the top of the Group 3 regular extra list. If a regular extra is offered a situation in accordance with the above provisions for which he is qualified and competent and refuses to accept the same, he shall be placed at the end of the Group 3 regular extra list. A regular situation holder, however, may refuse a situation offered in accordance with the above provisions without losing his seniority standing on either the promotional priority NHst or for purposes of layoff.

clauses.head: 4-D. If a regular situation holder or an extra
clauses.name: 4-D. Incompetence after promotion
clauses.tail: but he shall retain his former seniority position for purposes of layoff.
clauses.text: 4-D. If a regular situation holder or an extra accept a new situation in aecordance with the preceding provision and then be found te be unqualified for the work of such new situation, he shall be placed in the first vacancy for which he is qualified and competent which occurs in the course of filling the situation just vacated by him, and he shall be placed at the bottom of the promotional priority Hst,- but he shall retain his former seniority position for purposes of layoff.

clauses.head: Procedure for Lay-Off 4-E. In the event of
clauses.name: 4-E. Procedure for Lay-Off
clauses.tail: weeks’ notice to the Union and to the em- ployee affected.
clauses.text: Procedure for Lay-Off 4-E. In the event of a reduction in the number of regular situations, the layoff shall be in reverse 27 FUNDO000938 >. gee order of seniority standing, and the employees so laid off because of such reduction shall be placed at the head of the unemployed extra list taking places thereon in accordance with their seniority standing. There shall be no layoff except on two (2) weeks’ notice to the Union and to the employee affected.

clauses.head: 4-F, 1. (a) Commencing February 1, 1982 an
clauses.name: 4-F. 1. (a) Absence from situation
clauses.tail: behalf of the Union; or 4, A leave of absence from the industry.
clauses.text: 4-F, 1. (a) Commencing February 1, 1982 an employee holding a regular situation who is absent from work in such regular situation for a continuous period of ninety (90) regular working days or more, or who is absent from work in such repular situation for a period aggregating more than one hundred and twenty (120) working days during a calendar year shall be considered to have vacated his regular situation subject to Subsection (c) hereof. This provision, however, shall not apply, nor shall seniority be lost by any employee because of absence due to any of the following reasons, provided notice in writing has been given to the Publisher: 1. Illness, disability or partial incapacitation by reason of advanced age, during which time the man has no employment elsewhere; or 2. Service in the Armed Forces of the United States; or 3. Work performed in behalf of the Union; or 4, A leave of absence from the industry.

clauses.head: (b) Employees may request, from the employer, a
clauses.name: 4-F. 1. (b) Leave of absence
clauses.tail: of the Union. Consent to such extension shall not be unreasonably withheld.
clauses.text: (b) Employees may request, from the employer, a leave of absence from the industry. Consent 28 to such a leave shall not be unreasonably withheld by the Employer. Such leaves may be extended by agreement of the Employer and employee with the consent of the Union. Consent to such extension shall not be unreasonably withheld.

clauses.head: (c) In the event an employee has been
clauses.name: 4-F. 1. (c) Vacancy notice
clauses.tail: from the date of mailing unless an explana- tion for the absence is received.
clauses.text: (c) In the event an employee has been absent for the periods set forth in paragraph (a) hereof, the Employer shall send a certified letter to the employee’s last known address with a copy to the Union. The letter shall state that the employee’s situation shall be deemed vacant thirty days from the date of mailing unless an explanation for the absence is received.

clauses.head: 4-F, 2, Employees absent for the foregoing reasons,
clauses.name: 4-F. 2. Restoration after absence
clauses.tail: the same promotional priority and seniority standing held by them prior to such absence. .
clauses.text: 4-F, 2, Employees absent for the foregoing reasons, shall, upon return to work, be restored to their regular positions on the regular situation holders list with the same promotional priority and seniority standing held by them prior to such absence.

clauses.head: 4-G. The Lists herein provided for shall be
clauses.name: 4-G. Posting lists
clauses.tail: changes therein from time to time, shall be fur- nished by the Adjustment Board.
clauses.text: 4-G. The Lists herein provided for shall be kept permanently posted within each plant and in garages, and copies thereof, together with any changes therein from time to time, shall be furnished by the Adjustment Board.

clauses.head: 4-H. Any question which may arise with re-
clauses.name: 4-H. Qualification disputes
clauses.tail: submitted to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board.
clauses.text: 4-H. Any question which may arise with respect to the qualifications or competency of employees or otherwise with respect to the interpretation or application of these provisions shall, if not satisfactorily adjusted between the Union and the particular Publisher involved, be submitted to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board.

clauses.head: SECTION 5 Shifts and Regular Working Time 6-A.
clauses.name: 5-A. Day shift
clauses.tail: period shall be known as the day shift.
clauses.text: SECTION 5 Shifts and Regular Working Time 6-A. A regular day’s work shall consist of 7 hours and 54 minutes or less consecutively between the period of 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., which period shall be known as the day shift.

clauses.head: §-B. A regular night’s work shall consist of
clauses.name: 5-B. Night shift
clauses.tail: begin at 4:00 p.m. These periods shall be known as the night shift.
clauses.text: §-B. A regular night’s work shall consist of seven (7) or fewer consecutive hours of work on short nights and eight (8) or fewer consecutive hours of work on one long night between the period of 6:00 p.m. and 10:00 am. A regular night’s work on Saturday shall consist of seven and one-half (74%) or fewer consecutive hours of work when the period shall begin at 4:00 p.m. These periods shall be known as the night shift.

clauses.head: 5-C, A regular work week for employees work- ing
clauses.name: 5-C. Day work week
clauses.tail: per week, exclusive of overtime, divided over not more than a five-day period.
clauses.text: 5-C, A regular work week for employees working during day shifts shall consist of no more than 8915 hours per week, exclusive of overtime, divided over not more than a five-day period.

clauses.head: §-D. A regular work week for employees work- ing
clauses.name: 5-D. Night work week
clauses.tail: Saturday night except with the consent of the Publisher involved.
clauses.text: §-D. A regular work week for employees working during night shifts shall consist of no more than thirty-six and one-half (8644) hours per week, exclusive of overtime, divided over three (3) nights of no more than seven (7) hours each and one (1) night of no more than eight (8) hours and Saturday night of no more than seven and one-half (7%) hours. Each Publisher may determine which is to be the one long night, and no night off shall be allowed on such long night or Saturday night except with the consent of the Publisher involved.

clauses.head: 5-E. Employees shall receive a full day’s or a
clauses.name: 5-E. Full shift pay
clauses.tail: for each regular day’s work or for each regular night’s work.
clauses.text: 5-E. Employees shall receive a full day’s or a 30 “oe Cl dla Riel Ne SC full night’s wage, at the rates herein specified, for each regular day’s work or for each regular night’s work.

clauses.head: Overtime Defined - 5-F. Work performed in excess
clauses.name: 5-F. Overtime Defined
clauses.tail: overtime and shall be compensated for at the overtime rates fixed herein.
clauses.text: Overtime Defined - 5-F. Work performed in excess of the hours constituting a regular day’s work or a regular night’s work, or performed in excess of the fiveday or five-night period over which the employee's regular work week is distributed, or performed before or after the hour at which the shift during which the employee regularly works begins or _ terminates as herein provided, shall be deemed overtime and shall be compensated for at the overtime rates fixed herein.

clauses.head: 5-G. In arranging the regular work week for
clauses.name: 5-G. Work-week arrangement
clauses.tail: so that as many regular situations as possible may be created and maintained.
clauses.text: 5-G. In arranging the regular work week for regular situation holders, the five-day or five night periods, respectively, shall be staggered and distributed through the calendar week so that as many regular situations as possible may be created and maintained.

clauses.head: 5-H. All work performed in the handling, dis-
clauses.name: 5-H. Sunday issue work
clauses.tail: shall be paid for at double the week-day regular and overtime rates.
clauses.text: 5-H. All work performed in the handling, distribution and delivery of the issue of any evening newspaper of which the full printing. and circulation does not begin until after 12:01 a.m., Sunday, shall be paid for at double the week-day regular and overtime rates.

clauses.head: 5-I. Double the week-day regular and overtime rates
clauses.name: 5-I. Sunday advance sections
clauses.tail: advance sections on Sundays between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
clauses.text: 5-I. Double the week-day regular and overtime rates shall be paid for any work done on advance sections on Sundays between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.

clauses.head: Notice of Change §-J. Thirty (80) days after
clauses.name: 5-J. Notice of Change
clauses.tail: from the time of notice for four (4) days, shall be paid for at time and one-half.
clauses.text: Notice of Change §-J. Thirty (80) days after the signing of this 31 FUNDOO000940 tenant Agreement, the Publisher shall furnish the chapel chairman a list of the starting time and days off of regular situation holders. If the Publisher plans to change the time at which a regular situation holder reports for work or to change days off, four (4) days’ notice of such changes shall be given to the man or men involved and to the chapel chairman. If the Publisher fails to give four (4) days’ notice, then the time involved in the change from the time of notice for four (4) days, shall be paid for at time and one-half.

clauses.head: _ 5-K. Work performed on Sunday between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. shall be paid for at the rate of time and one-half.
clauses.name: 5-K. Sunday work
clauses.text: 5-K. Work performed on Sunday between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. shall be paid for at the rate of time and one-half.

clauses.head: 5-L. An employee required to finish his job at
clauses.name: 5-L. Travel time
clauses.tail: submitted to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board.
clauses.text: 5-L. An employee required to finish his job at a point sufficiently far from where it began to involve substantial travel time shall be compensated therefor. The parties are directed to negotate such an arrangement and if they are unable to agree within thirty (30) days after the signing of this Agreement the matter shall be submitted to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board.

clauses.head: 5-M. Overtime before and after a day or night
clauses.name: 5-M. Overtime assignment
clauses.tail: Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board for settlement.
clauses.text: 5-M. Overtime before and after a day or night shift shall be worked as required by the employer. . Any charge that vvertime is being required or distributed unfairiv may be taken to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board for settlement.

clauses.head: Paid Lunch 5-N. An inside employee on duty
clauses.name: 5-N. Paid Lunch
clauses.tail: shall prevail as to an outside employee on duty away from the plant.
clauses.text: Paid Lunch 5-N. An inside employee on duty within the plant shall be sent out on paid lunc): during the period after the end of the second hour from the 82 time he started work and before the end of the fifth hour from the time he started work. In the event an inside employee on duty within the plant is ordered by a foreman or assistant foreman to work through such paid lunch, such employee shall be paid one-half hour at the rate of time-and-onehalf. Present practice regarding the paid lunch period shall prevail as to an outside employee on duty away from the plant.

clauses.head: SECTION 6 Foremen 6-A. 1. Authority and control
clauses.name: 6-A. 1. Foreman authority
clauses.tail: absence of the foreman, the assistant foreman-in-charge shall so function,
clauses.text: SECTION 6 Foremen 6-A. 1. Authority and control over all employees shall be vested exclusively in the office through its representative, the foreman, who shall be a member of the Union. In the absence of the foreman, the assistant foreman-in-charge shall so function,

clauses.head: 6-A. 2. Foremen or assistant foremen shall not
clauses.name: 6-A. 2. Orders and discipline
clauses.tail: instructions of the Publisher or his representatives in accordance with this agreement.
clauses.text: 6-A. 2. Foremen or assistant foremen shall not give orders or exercise authority contrary to contract provisions or the law. The Union shall not discipline the foremen or assistant foremen for carrying out the instructions of the Publisher or his representatives in accordance with this agreement.

clauses.head: 6-B. Each Publisher shall have the right to- appoint
clauses.name: 6-B. Appointment and duties
clauses.tail: regular days or regular nights of work in such week.
clauses.text: 6-B. Each Publisher shall have the right toappoint as many foremen and assistant foremen as he may see fit. and shall have the right of removal. The terms of a foreman’s or assistant foreman’s employment, including hours, wages and other conditions of work, shall be a matter of agreement between the Publisher and such fore- 338 FUNDO000941 + wy. "tel man or assistant foreman, except that no foreman or assistant foreman is to be permitted to perform any of the operations specified in Section 2 hereof during any time in excess of the hours constitut. ing a regular day’s work or a regular night's work, as defined herein, nor during any part of a calendar week aftcr such foreman or assistant foreman has had five (5) regular days or regular nights of work in such week.

clauses.head: Shift Foremen 6-C, Whenever a morning newspaper employs
clauses.name: 6-C. Shift Foremen
clauses.tail: shall be under the supervision of a fore man or an assistant foreman.
clauses.text: Shift Foremen 6-C, Whenever a morning newspaper employs employees on a day shift or an evening newspaper employs employees on a night shift, such employees shall be under the supervision of a fore man or an assistant foreman.

clauses.head: 6-D, Whenever a Publisher has more than one plant there shall be a foreman or assistant fore- man in each plant.
clauses.name: 6-D. Multiple plants
clauses.text: 6-D, Whenever a Publisher has more than one plant there shall be a foreman or assistant foreman in each plant.

clauses.head: 6-E. Only the foreman or the assistant fore- man-in-charge
clauses.name: 6-E. Foreman powers
clauses.tail: directions. to issue orders and make changes in operatir« procedures.
clauses.text: 6-E. Only the foreman or the assistant foreman-in-charge shall be empowered to execute the provisions, terms and conditions hereof pursuant to the directions of the Publisher, to issue orders, to hire or to discharge, and no one except-the fore- man or assistant-in-charge shall have the right, in. accordance with such directions. to issue orders and make changes in operatir« procedures.

clauses.head: 6-F. Any employee having a complaint to make
clauses.name: 6-F. Employee complaints
clauses.tail: submitted to the Joint Standing Com- mittee and/or Appeals Board,
clauses.text: 6-F. Any employee having a complaint to make with respect to the conduct or orders of a foreman or an assistant foreman or with respect to alleged discrimination or other unfair treatment by a4 foreman or assistant foreman, may take up such complaint with the person duly designated by the 84 i ela le dt te ee a ee ee Tk Ii ak Ailend - Publisher for such purpose through the shop chairman or other Union representative; and if such complaint is not satisfactorily disposed of, it may be submitted to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board,

clauses.head: 6-G. A Publisher may make complaint that the
clauses.name: 6-G. Publisher complaints
clauses.tail: submitted te the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board.
clauses.text: 6-G. A Publisher may make complaint that the Union has improperly imposed penalties upon a foreman or an assistant foreman for earrying out the specific orders or instructions of the Publisher; and if the complaint be not satisfactorily adjusted, the same may be submitted te the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board.

clauses.head: SECTION 7 Holidays . 7-A. All regular situation
clauses.name: 7-A. Holidays
clauses.tail: and obtains employment else- where in the industry on the same holiday.
clauses.text: SECTION 7 Holidays . 7-A. All regular situation holders who are not required to work shall receive the following holidays, or days observed as such, off with pay: New Year’s Day, Lincoln's Birthday, Washington’s Birthday, Memorial Day, Independence _ Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas. In the event a regular situation holder is called upon to work on any of the named holidays, or days observed as such, he shall be paid in accordance with Section 7-C hereof. No holiday payment of any kind shall be made to an employee who trips, ie, an employee who, scheduled to work on a holiday shift, does not report for work and obtains employment elsewhere in the industry on the same holiday.

clauses.head: 7-B. Holidays shall extend from the beginning of
clauses.name: 7-B. Holiday period
clauses.tail: after a holiday-rate shift shall be at time and one-half the holiday rate.
clauses.text: 7-B. Holidays shall extend from the beginning of the night shift on the night before the holiday 35 FUNDO000942 to the end of the day shift of the holiday itself, Overtime performed before or after a holiday-rate shift shall be at time and one-half the holiday rate.

clauses.head: Holiday Rate 7-C. Any employee required to work
clauses.name: 7-C. Holiday Rate
clauses.tail: sick leave has been in excess of two (2) years,
clauses.text: Holiday Rate 7-C. Any employee required to work on any of the aforementioned holidays or days observed as such shall receive not less than two (2) days’ pay for the regular shift worked and thereafter price and one-half of the holiday rate. There shall be ho rearrangements of the days or nights constituting the regular work weeks of employees in the office or plant of any Publisher within any calendar week in which a holiday oceurs. Regular Situation holders not required to work shall receive a full day’s pay or a full night’s pay, in accordance as they ordinarily work during the day or night shift, for every holiday falling on a day or night of their regular work week, irrespective of whether the newspaper on which they are employed js issued on such holiday or not. However, nothing in this section shall require an employer to make holiday payments to an employee on sick leave as defined in Section 18-B. 2. when such sick leave has been in excess of two (2) years,

clauses.head: “-D. Extras who have had at least four (4)
clauses.name: 7-D. Extra holiday pay
clauses.tail: whether such Publisher’s newspaper js issued on such holiday or not.
clauses.text: “-D. Extras who have had at least four (4) days’ work with a PubNsher during each of the three (3) payroll weeks immediately preceding the payroll week in which a holiday occurs and during such week as well shal] receive a full day’s pay for such holiday irrespective of whether such Publisher’s newspaper js issued on such holiday or not.

clauses.head: 7-E. Work performed by employees on a holi- day
clauses.name: 7-E. Holiday work when not issued
clauses.tail: shall be paid for at double the regular and overtime rates.
clauses.text: 7-E. Work performed by employees on a holiday for a Publisher whose newspaper is not issued on such holiday shall be paid for at double the regular and overtime rates.

clauses.head: 7-F. An employee covered by this Agreement who
clauses.name: 7-F. Holiday and compensation benefits
clauses.tail: both the pay provided by this Section and the benefit payable under the law.
clauses.text: 7-F. An employee covered by this Agreement who is eligible for benefits under the Worker's Compensation Law, including the Disability Benefits Law, and who, on the same day, is eligible for holiday pay under this Section 7, will be paid on such a holiday both the pay provided by this Section and the benefit payable under the law.

clauses.head: SECTION 8 Chapel Chairman 8-A. The Union may
clauses.name: 8-A. Chapel Chairman
clauses.tail: the attempt to adjust the same satisfactorily shall not be deemed such an inter- ference,
clauses.text: SECTION 8 Chapel Chairman 8-A. The Union may have a chapel chairman in each office or plant who shall perform his regular duties as an employee of the particular Publisher, and who may act on behalf of employees covered by the contract employed by such Publisher and who may report toe the Union any claims, complaints or alleged violations of the terms and conditions hereof which cannot be settled satisfactorily with such Publisher through the foreman or assistant foreman-in-charge. Chapel chairmen shall not be discriminated against on account of their activities on behalf of the Union or the employees provided these activities do not interfere with the performance of their duties, but the presentation of -claims or complaints and the attempt to adjust the same satisfactorily shall not be deemed such an interference,

clauses.head: 8-B. The Chapel Chairman shall have the right
clauses.name: 8-B. Inspection rights
clauses.tail: written demand. No chapel meeting shall be held during working hours.
clauses.text: 8-B. The Chapel Chairman shall have the right to inspect the circulation reports, and the time and/or work sheets of persons employed in the bargaining unit. The Publisher is required to make available for inspection within forty-eight (48) hours, upon request, overtime recorded on daily time sheets for the preceding fiscal week. In the event that at any time the Chapel Chairman is refused the right of inspection, he may make demand therefor in writing, provided, however, that the Publisher shall not at any time be required to produce for the inspection of the Chapel Chairman circulation reports, or time and work sheets for a period greater than three (8) weeks prior to the date of such written demand. No chapel meeting shall be held during working hours.

clauses.head: 8-C. Employees holding the position of Chapel Chairman
clauses.name: 8-C. Overtime discrimination
clauses.tail: because of their exercise of the duties and responsibilities of such office.
clauses.text: 8-C. Employees holding the position of Chapel Chairman will not be discriminated against insofar as the distribution of overtime because of their exercise of the duties and responsibilities of such office.

clauses.head: SECTION 9 All parts or sections of a
clauses.name: 9-A. Outside-printed sections
clauses.tail: shall then be handled by employees represented by the Union.
clauses.text: SECTION 9 All parts or sections of a newspaper destined for delivery within the Metropolitan Area, printed in a plant not owned or controlled by the Publisher of such newspaper shall be delivered in bulk from the place of printing to the plant or plants operated by the Publisher? and after such parts or sections reach the platform or plat- 88 . ° . « . - #, . 3 an ae » eo, See . ’ ay . clauses.head: 9-B. In the event a Publisher has parts or
clauses.name: 9-B. Bulk delivery
clauses.tail: opportunity to procure such bulk deliveries for employees in the unit.
clauses.text: 9-B. In the event a Publisher has parts or sections of his newspaper printed in a plant not owned or controlled by the Publisher and located in the Metropolitan Area, as herein defined, such Publisher shall endeavor to have the bulk delivery of such parts or sections from the place of printing to the Publisher's plant or plants made by employees: in the unit, providing doing so does not involve the Publisher in increased cost or a jurisdictional conflict with some other union. In advance of making arrangements for such outside printing or renewing existing arrangements, the Publisher shall notify the Union and give it an opportunity to procure such bulk deliveries for employees in the unit.

clauses.head: SECTION 10 Half-Day Boys 10-A. In accordance with
clauses.name: 10-A. Half-Day Boys
clauses.tail: upon such terms as may be agreed upon between such boys and the Publishers,
clauses.text: SECTION 10 Half-Day Boys 10-A. In accordance with and subject to the provisions herein contained, half-day boys may be employed who are not members of the Union upon such terms as may be agreed upon between such boys and the Publishers,

clauses.head: 10-B. A “half-day boy” means an employee of
clauses.name: 10-B. Half-day boy defined
clauses.tail: hours herein- after specified in aid of and under the direction of a route man.
clauses.text: 10-B. A “half-day boy” means an employee of the Fublisher working within the hours hereinafter specified in aid of and under the direction of a route man.

clauses.head: 10-C, No Publisher of a morning newspaper may employ any half-day boys.
clauses.name: 10-C. Morning newspapers
clauses.text: 10-C, No Publisher of a morning newspaper may employ any half-day boys.

clauses.head: 10-D. Publishers of afternoon papers may em- ploy half-day
clauses.name: 10-D. Afternoon newspapers
clauses.tail: except on Saturdays when they may begin at 12:00 o’clock noon. ' ‘
clauses.text: 10-D. Publishers of afternoon papers may employ half-day boys to work only between the hours of three o'clock and eight o’clock jin the afternoon, except on Saturdays when they may begin at 12:00 o’clock noon.

clauses.head: 10-E. No half-day boy may be employed to draw newspapers directly from a Publisher's plant.
clauses.name: 10-E. Plant pickup
clauses.text: 10-E. No half-day boy may be employed to draw newspapers directly from a Publisher's plant.

clauses.head: 10-F. Publishers employing half-day boys shall prepare a
clauses.name: 10-F. Half-day-boy lists
clauses.tail: Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board, the Publishers’ Association, and the Union.
clauses.text: 10-F. Publishers employing half-day boys shall prepare a list of all such boys now in their employ and the particular routes or points at which they are employed, and shall furnish copies of such lists together with written notice of all subsequent changes therein to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board, the Publishers’ Association, and the Union.

clauses.head: 10-G. Except as hereinafter provided, each Pub- lisher
clauses.name: 10-G. Number limitation
clauses.tail: route or at any given point on which none is being employed at this time,
clauses.text: 10-G. Except as hereinafter provided, each Publisher shall be limited to the number of half-day boys now employed by him, nor shall he increase such number, nor shall he increase the number of half-day boys now employed by him on any given route or at any given point, nor shall he employ any half-day boys on a route or at any given point on which none is being employed at this time,

clauses.head: 10-H. In the event of the discontinuance of a
clauses.name: 10-H. Discontinued routes
clauses.tail: total number of half-day boys permitted to such Publisher shall be reduced accordingly.
clauses.text: 10-H. In the event of the discontinuance of a route on which a half-day boy or boys are now employed, such boy or boys shall be eliminated, and the positions so vacated shall not be filled, and the total number of half-day boys permitted to such Publisher shall be reduced accordingly.

clauses.head: 10-I, In the event of the merger or consolida-

clauses.head: 18-A. 4. Cost of Living Allowance: On each
clauses.name: 13-A. 4. Cost of Living Allowance
clauses.tail: unable to agree, then the same shall be referred to arbitration.
clauses.text: 18-A. 4. Cost of Living Allowance: On each anniversary date of the contract, March 81, 1982, and March 31, 1983, employees covered hereunder shall receive a cost of living adjustment to the scheduled wage increases in accordance with the following formula: The Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index (C.P.1.-W; 1967=100) for New York City, hereafter called the Index, shali be used for all measurements of the change in cost of living. Effective March 831, 1982, the amount of any cost of living adjustment shall be the percentage increase in excess of 6% in the Index for May 1982 over May 1981 (as reported in June each year) multipled by the day scales and the resultant amount shall be added to the day scales. Effective March 31, 1988, the amount of any cost of living adjustment shall be the percentage increase in excess of 6¢¢ in the Index for May 47 EIN AN tare nn AE ON UN Ee FUNDOO000948 1988 over May 1982 (as reported in June each year) multiplied by the day scales and the resultant amount shall be added to the day scales. The amount of any cost of living adjustment shall be included in computing all premiums and fringes such as pension and welfare contributions, overtime premium, night shift premium, vacation payments, holiday payment, death leave pay, paid leave, ete. In no event will a decline in the Index cause a reduction in the scale of wages or in any adjustment thereto. ; In the event that the Bureau of Labor Statistics shall fail to publish the Index or shall change its base period, the parties shall meet to discuss and apply any such new Index and its application to the cost of living allowance. If the parties are unable to agree, then the same shall be referred to arbitration.

clauses.name: 13-B. 2. (a) Vacation credits
clauses.tail: during vacation period shall not be entitled to vacation pay.
clauses.text: 13-B. 2. (a) Such vacation credit shall be earned when an employee is working on a situation as a regular or extra employee. The spirit and purpose of this provision is to disallow the duplication of vacation credits on the same situation. Days during sick leave shall be included in the schedule of days worked for which vacations are allowed. The words “sick leave” as used herein shall include time lost by reason of any illness or 49 FUNDOO00949 accident subject to the provisions of either the Workers Compensation Act or the Publishers’— Newspaper and Mail Deliverers’ Welfare Fund; and such waiting periods as contained therein shall be counted as days worked, but in no event shall such period of disability in excess of thirty (30) weeks in the case of sickness or fifty-three (58) weeks in the case of accident, both periods including the waiting period, be counted as time worked for the purpose of vacation credits, Time spent on duty with the National Guard or on Reserve Duty shall be included in the days worked for which vacations are allowed, to a maximum of two weeks. Holidays shall be included in the days worked for which vacations are allowed. Days of vacation are not to be counted as work days. The vacation schedule shall be arranged at the convenience of the employer, but on the basis of seniority. The days of the vacation period shall be consecutive. The Union offers, if called upon, to supply men to the employers to cover the period for which vacations are allowed, who may be employed at straight-time rates. Employees receiving vacations will not be allowed to work during ‘the vacation periods; and an employee who works during vacation period shall not be entitled to vacation pay.

clauses.text: 18-K. 2. During the years 1981 and 1982 and 1983, an employee may elect to accumulate any or all of his unused leave days. To elect this option, the employee must notify in writing the office of the employer by November 1 of each of the above years that he is accumulating such leave. Annually, on or before November 1, at the request of an employee, the office shall provide a signed statement of paid leave days which have been accumulated by that employee. Such accumulated Jeave can be taken at any time during the term of this Agreement and will be paid at the then prevailing rate. Accumulated leave not taken during the term of this Agreement shall be liquidated and payment, at the prevailing rate, made within 80 days following the expiration of the Agreement, unless there is mutual agreement to continue accumulated leave for a later date. If leave days are not accumulated, the employee shall receive, on the pay day of the first pay period in December of that year, the cash payment for any such days he has not taken in that calendar year. The Union recognizes the need for sufficient manpower for the efficient operation of the publishers in connection with the use of accumulated leave time in excess of ten days, The Union agrees that such accumulated leave shall not be taken in such a manner as to interfere with adequate staffing.

Where physical incapacity is the cause of discharge, the Publisher concerned shall make every effort to place such discharged employee at some other operation for which such employee may be qualified and to that extent the provisions herein contained with respect to priority and seniority shall be modified.
