clauses.head: I. Executive Summary MORTGAGE FUND °08 LLC (the
clauses.name: I. Executive Summary — Offering and Security
clauses.tail: THE NOTES WILL BE SECURED BY THE ASSETS OF THE COMPANY.
clauses.text: I. Executive Summary MORTGAGE FUND °08 LLC (the “Company”), sponsored by the principals of R.E. Loans, LLC, offers a new and attractive opportunity for qualified investors to achieve superior returns with a conservative risk profile through the purchase of promissory notes (the “Notes”) issued by the Company. The Company is targeting to return approximately 8.00% or more per year on the Noteholders investments. The Notes will be secured by the assets of the Company.

clauses.head: The Company will be formed as a Delaware
clauses.name: Company Formation and Purpose
clauses.tail: LIENS AGAINST REAL PROPERTY AND ASSOCIATED PERSONAL PROPERTY.
clauses.text: The Company will be formed as a Delaware limited liability company for the purpose of lending capital raised by the sale of Notes to borrowers (the “Portfolio Borrowers”) to finance the ownership, entitlement, development or rehabilitation of commercial real estate or for other real estate related purposes throughout the United States (the “Portfolic Loans”), The Portfolio Loans will be secured by liens against real property and associated personal property.

clauses.head: The Company will be managed by its manager,
clauses.name: Management and Servicer
clauses.tail: WERE SPONSORS OF PRIOR INVESTMENT FUNDS TO R.E. Loans, LLC.
clauses.text: The Company will be managed by its manager, The Mortgage Fund LLC, a California limited liability company formed for this purpose (the “Manager” or “The Mortgage Fund LLC’). The Manager is owned and led by Walter Ng and Kelly Ng (the “Managing Directors” or “Principals”), who together bring to the Company more than 81 years of experience in mortgage lending and investing among them. The Manager expects to hire Bar-K, Inc. to provide Portfolio Loan origination, brokerage and administration services to the Company (“Loan Services”) as “Servicer”, comparable to the services that Bar-K, Inc. provides to R.E. Loans, LLC and that it provided to its predecessor investment funds. Bar-K Inc, is managed by Barney Ng, and owned by Bamey and Kelly Ng. Walter Ng, Kelly Ng and Barney Ng also manage and own, with Bruce Horwitz, M.D., B-4 Partners, LLC, the sponsor of R.E. Loans LLC, and were sponsors of prior investment funds to R.E. Loans, LLC.

clauses.head: In order to participate in this opportunity, each
clauses.name: Subscriptions and Closings
clauses.tail: THE SAME TERMS AS THE NOTES PURCHASED BY INVESTORS.
clauses.text: In order to participate in this opportunity, each prospective investor will subscribe to purchase Notes pursuant to a Note Purchase Agreement with the Company by “loaning” their investment capital to the Company (their “Loan Amounts”). Notes will be issued to investors whose subscriptions are accepted by the Company (“Nofeholders”), in its discretion, at the next closing held by the Company, The initial closing is expected to be on or before December 3, 2007, and the Company expects to hold closings on the first day of each calendar month thereafter through May 1, 2009, although there is no assurance that there will be a subsequent closing or that a closing will be held each month, The Company has not targeted a minimum or maximum amount of capital to be raised by a sale of Notes. The Manager, the Principals, their family members, and their affiliates may also purchase Notes on the same terms as the Notes purchased by investors.

clauses.head: The Notes will bear simple interest at a
clauses.name: Interest, Maturity and Payment Terms
clauses.tail: ALTHOUGH PRINCIPAL MAY BE PREPAID AT ANY TIME WITHOUT PENALTY.
clauses.text: The Notes will bear simple interest at a rate determined quarterly by the Managing Directors, subject to a minimum average rate of eight percent (8%) annualized, The Notes will be secured by the assets of the Company. Regardless of when purchased, each Note will have a term ending December 31, 2014, subject, in the discretion of the Company, to a six month extension that would be applicable to all outstanding Notes. Interest will be payable quarterly, but payment of principal will be deferred, at the discretion of the Company, until the maturity of the Note, although principal may be prepaid at any time without penalty.

clauses.head: The Notes are an illiquid and long-term investment.
clauses.name: Illiquidity, Prepayment and Transfer Restrictions
clauses.tail: FOR SALE OF THE NOTES AND NONE IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP.
clauses.text: The Notes are an illiquid and long-term investment. No investor should subscribe to purchase a Note unless it is prepared to hold the Note until its maturity. Although the Company may, in its discretion, prepay a Note at any time, a Noteholder may not request prepayment of a Note until it has held the Note for a minimum of one year from the date of its issue, and the granting of such request is within the sole discretion of the Company. The Notes will not be transferable except under very limited circumstances and then only in the discretion of the Manager. There is no secondary market for sale of the Notes and none is expected to develop.

clauses.head: By virtue of their ownership of the Notes,
clauses.name: Status of Noteholders
clauses.tail: ISSUED BY THE COMPANY WITH RESPECT TO THEIR INVESTMENTS,
clauses.text: By virtue of their ownership of the Notes, the Noteholders will be secured creditors of the Company. The Noteholders will not own a membership interest, profit sharing or other direct or indirect equity interest in the Company. The Noteholders should expect to receive IRS Form 1099's issued by the Company with respect to their investments,

clauses.head: In addition to raising capital for Portfolio Loans,
clauses.name: Use of Capital and Senior Borrowings
clauses.tail: THE LIEN SECURING THE NOTES.
clauses.text: In addition to raising capital for Portfolio Loans, the Company may raise capital from the sale of Notes to pay its expenses, including organizational expenses, to reimburse the Manager for other Company related expenses, and to pay compensation, as more particularly described in the Summary of Principal Terms in this Offering Memorandum, although the Managing Directors expect that such expenses and compensation will generally be covered by the revenues of the Company. The Company may also raise capital for Portfolio Loans or for Company operating and other expenses by borrowings from institutional or other lenders, and such borrowings may be secured by liens on the Company’s assets that are senior to the lien securing the Notes.

clauses.head: II. Private Mortgage Lending The Company intends to
clauses.name: II. Private Mortgage Lending — Investment Policy
clauses.tail: BY QUALITY REAL ESTATE FOR GENERATION OF INCOME TO THE COMPANY.
clauses.text: II. Private Mortgage Lending The Company intends to invest in conservatively underwritten real estate mortgage loans with borrowers who are experienced in real estate operations and finance by directly controlling the sourcing, funding and administration of such loans based upon criteria the Principals have found to be successful in the past. The Company will not operate in the sub-prime mortgage market and will not source loans for the purpose of resale. Instead, it will focus the portfolio on loans secured by quality real estate for generation of income to the Company.

clauses.head: To date, the Principais and their affiliates have
clauses.name: Past-Performance Disclaimer
clauses.tail: GENERATE COMPARABLE OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE COMPANY AND ITS NOTEHOLDERS.
clauses.text: To date, the Principais and their affiliates have a proven lending record of sponsoring investments in welldiversified performing loans that produce solid returns to their investors. To date, no investor has experienced a loss of investment principal through investment vehicles sponsored by the Principals or their affiliates. Although there is no assurance that investors in the Company will experience similar results, the Manager believes that the past real estate lending success of the Principals and their affiliates will generate comparable opportunities for the Company and its Noteholders.

clauses.head: NO FIDUCIARY RESPONSIBILITY OF MANAGER TO NOTEHOLDERS Under
clauses.name: No Fiduciary Responsibility to Noteholders
clauses.tail: OPERATING AGREEMENT INDEPENDENT OF ITS OWN INTERESTS IN THE COMPANY.
clauses.text: NO FIDUCIARY RESPONSIBILITY OF MANAGER TO NOTEHOLDERS Under Delaware law, a manager is accountable to a limited liability company’s members as a fiduciary, which means that a manager is required to exercise good faith and integrity with respect to company affairs. This fiduciary duty is in addition to those other duties and obligations of, and limitations on, the Manager which are set forth in the Operating Agreement. At the time of this offering, the Manager is also the sole member of the Company. The Noteholders do not have a member’s interest in the Company, but are solely creditors of the Company. Accordingly, the Manager does not have a direct fiduciary obligation to the Noteholders nor, at the time of this offering, does it have a fiduciary obligation to the Company’s members or contractual obligation under the Operating Agreement independent of its own interests in the Company.

clauses.head: The Company, however, will enter into certain contractual
clauses.name: Contractual Covenants to Noteholders
clauses.tail: WHICH WOULD BE ADVERSE TO THE MANAGER’S INTEREST IN THE COMPANY.
clauses.text: The Company, however, will enter into certain contractual operating covenants and commitments to the Noteholders pursuant to the Note Purchase Agreement, the Notes and the Security Agreement, the breach of which by the Company may give the Noteholders a cause of action against the Company, which would be adverse to the Manager’s interest in the Company.

clauses.head: The Operating Agreement provides that the Manager shall
clauses.name: Manager Exculpation
clauses.tail: THE MANAGER IS GUILTY OF FRAUD, BAD FAITH OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT.
clauses.text: The Operating Agreement provides that the Manager shall have no liability to the Company for losses resulting from errors in judgment or other acts or omissions, unless the Manager is guilty of fraud, bad faith or willful misconduct.

clauses.head: The Operating Agreement also provides that the Company
clauses.name: Manager and Servicer Indemnification
clauses.tail: WOULD HAVE ABSENT THESE PROVISIONS IN THE OPERATING AGREEMENT.
clauses.text: The Operating Agreement also provides that the Company shall indemnify the Manager and Servicer against liability and related expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs) incurred in dealing with the Company, Noteholders or third parties, so long as no fraud, bad faith or willful misconduct on the part of the Manager or Servicer is involved. A successful indemnification of the Manager or Servicer or any litigation that may arise in connection with their indemnification could deplete the assets of the Company, thereby reducing the assets available to pay the Notes. Therefore, Noteholders may have a more limited opportunity of recovery then they would have absent these provisions in the Operating Agreement.

clauses.head: In addition to its contracted obligations to the
clauses.name: Securities-Law and Creditor Obligations
clauses.tail: THE RIGHTS AND REMEDIES OF A CREDITOR AGAINST ITS OBLIGOR.
clauses.text: In addition to its contracted obligations to the Noteholders under the Note Purchase Agreement, the Notes and the Security Agreement, the Company has certain obligations under federal securities laws in connection with the offering and sale of the Notes, the preparation of this Memorandum, and representations to prospective investors and communications to Noteholders regarding the condition of the Company, certain conflicts of interest, and the terms of this offering. There are also certain state and federal laws that govern the respective rights and obligations of the Company with respect to its creditors, and the rights and remedies of a creditor against its obligor.

clauses.head: CONFLICTS OF INTEREST There are potential conflicts of
clauses.name: Conflicts of Interest

clauses.text: CONFLICTS OF INTEREST There are potential conflicts of interest between the Company and the Manager with respect to the activities undertaken by the Manager on the Company’s behalf that benefit the Manager or its affiliates. These conflicts of interest are unlikely to be resolved. The Company has not been separately represented ~8- CONFIDENTIAL of 48 Case3:14-cv-00993-SI Documenti7-1 Filed08/05/14 Page1ii7 of 268 by independent legal counsel in its formation or in its dealings with the Manager and Servicer, and Noteholders must rely on the good faith and integrity of the Manager and Servicer to act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this offering. As noted above, the Manager owes no direct fiduciary obligations to the Noteholders. Any members or managers who may be admitted to the Company in the future may be affiliated with the Manager and may have interests that align more completely with the Manager than with the Noteholders in connection with the Company’s operations. (See “Fiduciary Responsibility of the Managing Member.”’) The following is a list of the important areas in which the interests of the Manager and Servicer will conflict with those of the Noteholders. Except as may arise in the normal course of the relationship, there are no transactions presently contemplated between the Company and the Manager (or its affiliates) other than those listed below:

clauses.head: Loan Brokerage Commissions, Renewal and Forbearance Fees None
clauses.name: Loan Brokerage Commissions, Renewal and Forbearance Fees
clauses.tail: TO COMPARABLE BORROWERS OF SIMILAR SIZE, DURATION AND SECURITY,
clauses.text: Loan Brokerage Commissions, Renewal and Forbearance Fees None of the compensation set forth under “Compensation to Management” was determined by arms’ length negotiations. It is anticipated that the loan brokerage commissions, renewal fees and forbearance fees charged to Portfolio Borrowers by the Servicer for most Portfolio Loans will be in the amount set forth herein (see “J/I. Management - Compensation to Management” above), but may be higher or lower depending upon market conditions. Any increase in such charges will have a direct, adverse effect upon the interest rates that Portfolio Borrowers will be willing to pay the Company, thus reducing the overall rate of return to the Company and the Company’s ability to pay the Notes. Conversely, if the Manager or Servicer reduced the commissions and fees charged by it, a higher rate of return on Portfolio Loans might be obtained for the Company, thereby increasing its ability to repay the Notes. This conflict of interest will exist in connection with every Portfolio Loan transaction, and Noteholders must rely upon the terms of the Note Purchase Agreement to the Company, the Notes and the Security Agreement to protect their interests. The Company will generally charge Portfolio Borrowers interest at the rate generally prevailing in the geographical areas where the security property is located for loans to comparable borrowers of similar size, duration and security,

clauses.name: Right to Retain Other Firms

clauses.text: The Manager has the right to retain the services of other firms, in addition to or in lieu of the Servicer, to perform brokerage services, loan servicing and other activities in connection with the Company’s Portfolio Loans that are described in this Memorandum.

clauses.head: Loans to Related Parties The Company may make
clauses.name: Related Party Loans
clauses.tail: FOLLOWING STANDARDS AND LIMITATIONS TO SUCH RELATED PARTY LOANS:
clauses.text: Loans to Related Parties The Company may make or invest in loans to persons or entities that are affiliated with the Manager, the Members, or the Servicer, such as a loan under which the borrower is owned by one or more of the members of the Manager, the Members, the Servicer or their family members (“Related Party Loans’). In cases of such Related Party Loans, conflicts of interest will exist between such Manager, Member, Servicer or its affiliated persons, on the one hand, and the Company, on the other, in connection with setting the terms of the loan and in connection with any enforcement action or renegotiation that may occur in the future. The Manager has undertaken to address these conflicts by applying the following standards and limitations to such Related Party Loans:

clauses.head: (a) The aggregate principal amount of all Related Party Loans at any time shall not exceed 20% of total Company assets at such time;
clauses.name: Related Party Loan Limit
clauses.text: (a) The aggregate principal amount of all Related Party Loans at any time shall not exceed 20% of total Company assets at such time;

clauses.head: (b)} The terms and conditions of any Related
clauses.name: Related Party Loan Terms

clauses.text: (b)} The terms and conditions of any Related Party Loans shall be consistent with the lending standards and policies set forth above and with loan terms typically offered by the Company on similar loans to unaffiliated borrowers; and

clauses.name: Purchase of Defaulted Related Party Loans
clauses.tail: DEFAULT HAS OCCURRED AND IS CONTINUING FOR NINETY (90) CONSECUTIVE DAYS.

clauses.tail: RELATIVE AMOUNT OF UNCOMNNITTED CAPITAL AVAILABLE FOR OPERATIONS AND LENDING.
clauses.text: Other Funds or Businesses; Allocations of Portfolio Loan Opportunities B-4 Partners LLC, an affiliate of the Manager owned and managed by Walter Ng and Dr. Bruce Horwitz, currently owns and manages R.E. Loans, LLC (‘R.E. Leans”), a licensed California finance lender with a business purpose similar to the Company’s. As of November 2007, R.E. Loans owns a loan portfolio of approximately 60 loans with aggregate principal value of $750 million. R.E. Loans is not anticipated to make additional portfolio loans, but it may take four to six years for its current portfolio to mature or be liquidated. Additionally, in the future, the Manager may also sponsor other funds formed to conduct business similar to that of the Company (together with R.E. Loans, the “Other Sponsored Investment Funds”). If Other Sponsored Investment Funds have capital to loan at the same time as the Company, there will then exist conflicts of interest on the part of the Manager as to whether to offer a particular loan opportunity to the Company or to these other funds. The Manager will decide which loans are appropriate for funding by the Company or by Other Sponsored Funds after consideration of all relevant factors, including the size of the loan, portfolio diversification, remaining term of the Company and the relative amount of uncomnnitted capital available for operations and lending.

clauses.head: Also, the Manager may engage for its own

clauses.text: Also, the Manager may engage for its own account, or for the account of others, in other business ventures, similar to that of the Company or otherwise, and neither the Company nor any Noteholder shall be entitled to any interest therein.

clauses.head: The compensation structure applicable to the Manager in
clauses.name: Compensation for Outside Activities
clauses.tail: PRIVATE INVESTORS OUTSIDE THE COMPANY OR FOR OTHER SPONSORED FUNDS.
clauses.text: The compensation structure applicable to the Manager in connection with loans that are arranged or originated for investors other than the Company or Other Sponsored Investment Funds may be different than the compensation payable by the Company to the Manager for comparable services provided to the Company. Depending on the circumstances at a given point in time, devoting time or effort to provide such services to others than the Company may be more lucrative to the Manager than the compensation payable to the Manager in connection with the Company. As a result, there may exist a financial incentive for the Manager to arrange or originate loans for private investors outside the Company or for Other Sponsored Funds.

clauses.tail: TO THE NOTEHOLDERS UNDER THE TERMS OF THE NOTES AND THE NOTE PURCHASE AGREEMENT.
clauses.text: Accordingly, the Noteholders must rely on the Manager to act in good faith to cause the Company to meet its obligations to the Noteholders under the terms of the Notes and the Note Purchase Agreement.

clauses.head: Allocation of Management Time The Company will not
clauses.name: Allocation of Management Time
clauses.tail: AVAILABLE TO BE FULLY CAPABLE OF DISCHARGING ITS RESPONSIBILITIES TO ALL SUCH ENTITIES.
clauses.text: Allocation of Management Time The Company will not have independent management and it will rely on the Manager for the operation of the Company. The Manager and its Principals will devote only so much time to the business of the Company as is reasonably required. The Manager and its Principals will have conflicts of interest in allocating management time, services and functions among the Company, existing business interests other than the Company and Other Sponsored Funds which it may organize or other business ventures in which it may be involved. The Manager believes it has sufficient staff available to be fully capable of discharging its responsibilities to all such entities.

The use by the Manager, Servicer and the Company of the same counsel in the preparation of this Memorandum and the organization of the Company may result in the lack of independent review. Prospective investors must rely on their own legal counsel for legal advice in connection with this investment.

clauses.head: Sale of Defaulted Loans or Real Estate Owned
clauses.name: Sale of Defaulted Loans or Real Estate to Affiliates
clauses.tail: THE MANAGER’S DECISION WILL NOT BE SUBJECT TO REVIEW BY ANY OUTSIDE PARTIES.
clauses.text: Sale of Defaulted Loans or Real Estate Owned to Affiliates In the event a Portfolio Loan goes into default or the Company becomes the owner of any real property by reason of foreclosure on a Portfolio Loan, the Manager’s first priority will usually be to arrange the sale of the loan or property for a price that will permit the Company to recover the full amount of its invested capital plus accrued but unpaid interest and other charges, or so much thereof as can reasonably be obtained in light of current market conditions. In order to facilitate such a sale, the Manager may arrange a sale to persons or entities controlled by or affiliated with the Manager or the Servicer (e.g., to another entity formed by the Manager or its affiliates), for the express purpose of acquiring defaulted loans or foreclosure properties from lenders such as the Company. The Manager will be subject to conflicts of interest in arranging such sales since it will represent both parties to the transaction. For example, the Company and the potential buyer will have conflicting interests in determining the purchase price and other terms and conditions of sale. The Manager’s decision will not be subject to review by any outside parties.

clauses.head: The Manager shail undertake to resolve these conflicts
clauses.name: Affiliate Sale Price and Financing
clauses.tail: FINANCING PROVIDED BY THE COMPANY WILL NOT BE DEEMED A RELATED PARTY LOAN.
clauses.text: The Manager shail undertake to resolve these conflicts by setting a purchase price for each defaulted loan or property which is not less than any of the following: (i) the independently appraised value of such loan or property, if any, at the time of sale; (ii) the amount of any third party offer already received, if any; or (i1i) the total amount of the Company’s investment in the property. The Company’s investment is deemed to include without limitation the following: the unpaid principal amount of the loan upon which the Company foreclosed, all unpaid interest accrued to the date of foreclosure, expenditures made to protect the Company’s interest in the property such as payments to senior lienholders and for insurance and taxes, all costs of foreclosure (including attorneys fees actually incurred to prosecute the foreclosure or to obtain relief from stays in bankruptcy), and any advances made by or on behalf of the Company for any of the foregoing. A portion of the purchase price may be paid by the affiliate executing a promissory, note in favor of the Company, secured by a deed of trust on the property being sold. Such seller financing provided by the Company will not be deemed a Related Party Loan.

clauses.head: Transactions between the Company and Other Sponsored Funds,
clauses.name: Transactions with Other Sponsored Funds and Private Investors
clauses.tail: WITH LENDING CRITERIA FOR SUCH LOANS ESTABLISHED BY THE NOTE PURCHASE AGREEMENT.
clauses.text: Transactions between the Company and Other Sponsored Funds, Private Investors The Company may purchase or sell, from time to time, loans for its portfolio from or to Other Sponsored Funds or private investors or lenders doing business with the Manager or its affiliates. Without limiting the foregoing, the Company expects to purchase mortgage loans from, or later into co-investment agreements with, R.E. Loans as may be determined by the Manager, on behalf of the Company, and B-4 Partners LLC, on behalf of R.E. Loans. In order to mitigate conflicts of interest that arise in connection with the Ioan purchase from, sale to, or co-investment with Sponsored Investment Funds or Private Clients, such transactions will be made in compliance with lending criteria for such loans established by the Note Purchase Agreement.

clauses.head: IV. Portfolio Loan Criteria and Policies General Standards
clauses.name: IV. Portfolio Loan Criteria — General Standards
clauses.tail: WILL NOT BE INSURED OR GUARANTEED BY ANY GOVERNMENTAL AGENCY OR PRIVATE ENTITY.
clauses.text: IV. Portfolio Loan Criteria and Policies General Standards for Mortgage Loans The Company will engage in the business of making loans secured by deeds of trust that encumber real estate located primarily in the United States, its territories and possessions. The Company may also invest indirectly in a loan by acquiring an ownership interest in an entity formed for the sole purpose of holding a qualifying loan. To the extent the Manager believes it to be in the best interests of the Company, the Company may also make or invest in construction loans for the purpose of constructing various types of residential and/or commercial properties, which construction loans would be secured by such properties. The Company may also make occasional loans to individuals and entities collateralized by loans that are secured by deeds of trust. The Company’s loans will not be insured or guaranteed by any governmental agency or private entity.

clauses.head: The Company expects to select loans for investment
clauses.name: Loan-to-Value Guidelines
clauses.tail: Improved Property (whether residential, commercial or industrial) 70% Land 50%
clauses.text: The Company expects to select loans for investment pursuant to a strict set of guidelines set forth below, which guidelines are designed to set standards for the quality of the real property security given for the loans. ‘Type of Property/Loan Loan to Value Ratio Improved Property (whether residential, commercial or industrial) 70% Land 50%

clauses.head: Priority of Mortgages Most Company loans are expected
clauses.name: Priority of Mortgages
clauses.tail: TWENTY PERCENT (20%) OF THE COMPANY’S ENTIRE LOAN PORTFOLIO.
clauses.text: Priority of Mortgages Most Company loans are expected to be secured by a first deed of trust on the real property (the “Security Property”) which is to be used as security for the loan. The Company’s investment in loans that are secured by a junior deed of trust will not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the Company’s entire Loan Portfolio.

clauses.head: Geographic Area of Lending Activity The Company will
clauses.name: Geographic Area of Lending Activity
clauses.tail: LOANS SECURED BY NON-U.S. PROPERTIES IF THE LOAN MEETS THE COMPANY’S LENDING CRITERIA.
clauses.text: Geographic Area of Lending Activity The Company will limit its lending activity primarily to deeds of trust on properties located in the United States, its territories and possessions (“U.S. Praperties”), but may invest up to 20% of total Company Capital in loans secured by non-U.S. Properties if the loan meets the Company’s lending criteria.

clauses.head: Loan-to-Value Ratios The amount of the Company’s loan
clauses.name: Loan-to-Value Ratios
clauses.tail: LOAN FUNDS MAY BE WITHHELD TO BE PAID OUT UPON INSPECTION AS IMPROVEMENTS ARE MADE.
clauses.text: Loan-to-Value Ratios The amount of the Company’s loan combined with the outstanding debt secured by any senior deed of trust on the security property generally will not exceed the percentages stated above, based a valuation of the security property as determined by either the Manager or an independent written appraisal. Appraisals and loan-to-value ratios may be determined on an as-completed basis with respect to construction or home improvement loans, however, loan funds may be withheld to be paid out upon inspection as improvements are made.

clauses.head: Finally, the foregoing loan-to-value ratio will not apply

clauses.tail: OR THEIR RESPECTIVE MEMBERS OR PRINCIPALS, SHALL CONSTITUTE A RELATED PARTY LOAN,

In such cases, the Manager shall be free to accept any reasonable financing terms that it deems to be in the best interests of the Company, in its sole discretion. clauses.head: Terms of Loans The term of Company loans
clauses.name: Terms of Loans
clauses.tail: WITH A “BALLOON PAYMENT” DUE AT THE END OF THE TERM.
clauses.text: Terms of Loans The term of Company loans will vary at the discretion of the Manager. Company loans will generally have a term of between one (1) and six (6) years. Loans may be amortizing (i.e., the original principal amount of the loan will be partially or fully repaid in equal monthly installments of principal and interest over the term), or may provide for monthly payments of interest only during the term with a “balloon payment” due at the end of the term.

clauses.head: Credit Evaluations The Manager may consider the income
clauses.name: Credit Evaluations
clauses.tail: TO QUALIFY FOR LOANS FROM OTHER LENDERS SUCH AS BANKS OR SAVINGS AND LOAN ASSOCIATIONS.
clauses.text: Credit Evaluations The Manager may consider the income level and general creditworthiness of a borrower, and any guarantor, to determine a borrower’s ability to repay the Company loan according to its terms, but such considerations are subordinate to a determination that a borrower has sufficient equity in the security property to satisfy the loan-to-value ratios described above. Therefore, the Company may make loans to borrowers who are in default under other of their obligations (e.g., to consolidate their debts) or who do not have sources of income that would be sufficient to qualify for loans from other lenders such as banks or savings and loan associations.

clauses.name: Escrow Condition (a) — Title Insurance
clauses.tail: VALUE OF THE SECURITY PROPERTY, OVER-APPRAISALS, BORROWER’S DEFAULTS, ETC.
clauses.text: Escrow Conditions Company loans will be funded through an escrow account handled by the Manager or a qualified title insurance or escrow company, The escrow agent will be instructed not to disburse any funds until the following conditions are met: (a) Satisfactory title insurance coverage will be obtained for all ioans, with the title insurance policy naming the Company as the insured and providing title insurance in an amount equal to the principal amount of the loan. Title insurance insures only the validity and priority of the Company’s deed of trust, and does not insure the Company against loss by reason of other causes, such as diminution in the value of the security property, over-appraisals, borrower’s defaults, etc.

clauses.head: (b) Satisfactory fire and casualty insurance has been
clauses.name: Escrow Condition (b) — Casualty Insurance
clauses.tail: OF THE COMPANY’S LOAN. (SEE “VII. RISK FACTORS ~ UNINSURED LOSSES,”)
clauses.text: (b) Satisfactory fire and casualty insurance has been obtained for all loans, or only casualty insurance in the event of a Loan secured by unimproved land, which insurance shall name the Company as loss payee in an amount equal to the principal amount of the Company’s loan. (See “VII. Risk Factors ~ Uninsured Losses,”)

clauses.head: (c) The Manager does not intend to arrange
clauses.name: Escrow Condition (c) — Mortgage Insurance
clauses.tail: THERE WERE INSUFFICIENT EQUITY IN THE SECURITY PROPERTY TO REPAY ALL SUMS OWED.
clauses.text: (c) The Manager does not intend to arrange for mortgage insurance, which would afford some protection against loss if the Company foreclosed on a loan and there were insufficient equity in the security property to repay all sums owed.

clauses.head: (d) All loan documents (notes, deeds of trust,
clauses.name: Escrow Condition (d) — Loan Documents and Assignments
clauses.tail: HELD IN THE NAME OF THE MANAGER OR ANY OTHER NOMINEE.
clauses.text: (d) All loan documents (notes, deeds of trust, etc.) and insurance policies will name the Company as payee and beneficiary or additional loss insured, as applicable. In the event the Company purchases loans, the Company shall receive assignments of all beneficial interest in any documents related to each Loan so purchased. Company investments in Loans will not be held in the name of the Manager or any other nominee.

clauses.head: Loan Servicing It is anticipated that ail Company
clauses.name: Loan Servicing
clauses.tail: LOAN SERVICING ACTIVITIES. (SEE “II. MANAGEMENT - COMPENSATION TO MANAGEMENT.”)
clauses.text: Loan Servicing It is anticipated that ail Company loans will be “serviced” (i.c., loan payments will be collected and other administrative services performed) by the Servicer, which is expected also to act as either the initial lender or loan broker in connection with the origination of most or all Company loans. The Servicer will be compensated for such loan servicing activities. (See “iI. Management - Compensation to Management.”)

clauses.head: Portfolio Borrowers will make loan payments monthly in
clauses.name: Portfolio Borrower Payments

clauses.head: Leveraging the Portfolio If the Manager deems it
clauses.name: Leveraging the Portfolio
clauses.tail: (SEE “RISKS AND OTHER IMPORTANT FACTORS - RISKS OF LEVERAGE.”)
clauses.text: Leveraging the Portfolio If the Manager deems it to be in the best interest of the Company, the Company may borrow funds from a third party lender (which may but is not required to be a bank or other financial institution) in order to fund additional mortgage loans. By leveraging the Company’s loan portfolio, the Company can increase the yield to the Company. This increased yield will result if the interest earned by the Company on its leveraged loans exceeds the interest that must be paid by the Company on the funds borrowed from a third party lender. This “spread” between the interest eared on a leveraged loan and the interest paid on the borrowed funds used to make the loan will accrue to the Company. However, leveraging a Portfolio Loan entails certain risks to the Company that would not otherwise be present if the Company funded all ~15- CONFIDENTIAL of 48 Case3:14-cv-00993-SI Documenti7-1 Filed08/05/14 Pagei24 of 268 of its Portfolio Loans from its own funds. For example, to the extent the Company makes Portfolio Loans at long-term fixed interest rates while it borrows funds at short-term variable interest rates, the Company will be subject to the risk that prevailing interest rates (and the Company’s associated borrowing costs) will rise above the levels earned by the Company on the fixed rate portion of its loan portfolio, causing losses to the Company. (See “Risks and Other Important Factors - Risks of Leverage.”)

clauses.head: VI. Tax and Legal Considerations CERTAIN UNITED STATES
clauses.name: VI. Tax and Legal Considerations — Scope and Advice Disclaimer
clauses.tail: INCOME AND OTHER TAX CONSIDERATIONS RELATING TO AN INVESTMENT IN THE NOTES.
clauses.text: VI. Tax and Legal Considerations CERTAIN UNITED STATES FEDERAL INCOME TAX CONSIDERATIONS The following summary discusses material U.S. federal income tax consequences relating to the ownership and disposition of an investment interest in Notes. This summary is based upon existing U.S. federal income tax law, which is subject to change or differing interpretations, possibly with retroactive effect. This summary does not discuss all aspects of U.S. federal income taxation which may be important to particular investors in light of their individual investment circumstances, including investors subject to special tax rules (e.g., financial institutions, insurance companies, broker-dealers, non-United States investors, and domestic and foreign tax-exempt organizations (including private foundations)) or to investors that will hold the Notes as part of a straddle, hedge, conversion, constructive sale, or other integrated transaction for U.S. federal income tax purposes or holders that have a functional currency other than the U.S. dollar, all of whom may be subject to tax rules that differ significantly from those summarized below. This summary applies only to “U.S. Holders” (as defined below) that hold the Notes as “capital assets” (generally, for investment purposes). Each prospective investor is urged to consult its tax advisor regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and foreign income and other tax considerations relating to an investment in the Notes.

clauses.head: For this purpose, a “U.S. Holder” is a
clauses.name: Definition of U.S. Holder
clauses.tail: ELECTED TO BE TREATED AS A UNITED STATES PERSON UNDER THE CODE.
clauses.text: For this purpose, a “U.S. Holder” is a beneficial owner of the Notes that is, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, (i) an individual who is a citizen or resident of the United States, (ii) a corporation, or other entity taxable as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes, created in, or organized under the law of, the United States or any State thereof, (iii) an estate the income of which is includible in gross income for U.S. federal income tax purposes regardless of its source, or (iv) a trust (A) the administration of which is subject to the primary supervision of a United States court and which has one or more United States persons who have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust or (B) that has otherwise elected to be treated as a United States person under the Code.

United States and non-United States partnerships and their partners are urged to consult their tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and foreign income and other tax considerations relating to an investment in notes.

clauses.head: Ownership of Notes Original Issue Discount The Company
clauses.name: Original Issue Discount — Contingent Debt Treatment
clauses.tail: ORDINARY INCOME, IN WHOLE OR IN PART. SEE “GAIN OR LOSS ON DISPOSITION".
clauses.text: Ownership of Notes Original Issue Discount The Company may be deemed for tax purposes to pay to the holders of Notes “additional interest”, as such concept is described in the following discussion, Consequently, the Company will treat the Notes as contingent debt instruments subject to the "non-contingent bond method" of reporting interest as set forth in applicable Treasury Regulations. As a result of the classification of the Notes as contingent debt instruments, any gain realized on the sale or exchange of the Notes may be treated as ordinary income, in whole or in part. See “Gain or Loss on Disposition".

clauses.head: Under the non-contingent bond method, the issuer of
clauses.name: Comparable Yield
clauses.tail: EARNED EACH YEAR, EVEN THOUGH THERE ARE NO PAYMENTS OF CONTINGENT INTEREST IN SUCH YEAR.
clauses.text: Under the non-contingent bond method, the issuer of a contingent debt instrument must first determine the Comparable Yield. The Comparable Yield is the yield at which the Company could issue a debt instrument with terms and conditions similar to those of the contingent payment debt instrument. The Company has selected 8% as its Comparable Yield, and this rate will be used by the Company for purposes of determining its own taxable income and for any required information reporting. Since there is no direct authority in this area, it is uncertain whether the Internal Revenue Service will agree with this determination and may require a higher or lower Comparative Yield. If the Internal Revenue Service determines that the Comparable Yield should be higher, a Noteholder will be required to accrue the difference between the Comparable Yield selected by the Company and such higher Yield as additional interest income earned each year, even though there are no payments of contingent interest in such year.

clauses.head: Under the non-contingent bond method, if the interest
clauses.name: Contingent Payment Adjustments
clauses.tail: TREATED BY A HOLDER AS ADDITIONAL INTEREST INCOME.
clauses.text: Under the non-contingent bond method, if the interest payable for any period is greater or less than the amount projected, the amount of income included for that period would be either increased or decreased accordingly. Any net increase in the projected contingent payments for a taxable year (e.g., a determination of the amount due pursuant to the additional interest) is treated by a holder as additional interest income.

clauses.head: Please note that the Comparable Yield is supplied
clauses.name: Comparable Yield Disclaimer
clauses.tail: THAT NOTEHOLDERS WILL ACTUALLY RECEIVE WITH RESPECT TO THEIR NOTES.
clauses.text: Please note that the Comparable Yield is supplied by the Company solely for computing income under the non-contingent bond method for federal income tax purposes, and does not constitute a projection or representation as to the amounts that Noteholders will actually receive with respect to their Notes.

clauses.head: Gain or Loss on Disposition If a Note
clauses.name: Gain or Loss on Disposition
clauses.tail: LOSS WILL BE ORDINARY TO THE EXTENT OF PRIOR ORDINARY INCOME INCLUSION.
clauses.text: Gain or Loss on Disposition If a Note is sold, redeemed or otherwise disposed of, the selling Noteholder will recognize gain or loss equal to the difference between the amount realized from the disposition and the selling Noteholder's adjusted basis in such Note. The adjusted basis generally will equal the cost of such Note to the seller, increased by any original issue discount on such Note included in the seller's income and reduced (but not below zero) by any non-contingent payments on the Note. Because the Notes are characterized as contingent debt instruments under the Treasury Regulations, any gain recognized upon a sale, exchange, retirement, or other disposition of a Note will generally be ordinary income and any loss will be ordinary to the extent of prior ordinary income inclusion.

clauses.head: Tax-Exempt Entities The income earned by qualified pension,
clauses.name: Tax-Exempt Entities
clauses.tail: TO THE EXTENT OF “UNRELATED BUSINESS TAXABLE INCOME” (UBT) IN EXCESS OF $1,000 IN ANY YEAR.
clauses.text: Tax-Exempt Entities The income earned by qualified pension, profit-sharing and stock bonus plans, and IRA’s or other taxexempt entities generally is exempt from federal income taxation, except to the extent of “unrelated business taxable income” (UBT) in excess of $1,000 in any year.

clauses.head: As noted above, it is intended that the
clauses.name: Intended UBTI Treatment
clauses.tail: THE NOTES WILL NOT CONSTITUTE UBTI TO THE NOTEHOLDERS.
clauses.text: As noted above, it is intended that the interest payable with respect to the Notes will be characterized as interest for federal income tax purposes and the Notes will not constitute an equity investment in the Fund, with the result that amounts received with respect to the Notes will not constitute UBTI to the Noteholders.

clauses.head: If the IRS were successfully to characterize the
clauses.name: Equity Recharacterization and UBTI
clauses.tail: PURPOSES OF ATTRIBUTING UBTI TO INVESTORS WHO ARE DEEMED PARTNERS,
clauses.text: If the IRS were successfully to characterize the Noteholders as members in the Company, due to the nature of the source of the Fund’s revenues as portfolio interest income, amounts received with respect to the Notes would not be treated as UBTI to the Noteholders. Income to equity investors with respect to Portfolio Loans funded partially by Company Borrowings would constitute “debt financed property” and generate UBTI to the investor. Similarly, income to investors deemed partners with respect to profits to the Company earned from resale or lease of properties acquired by the Company through foreclosure that are encumbered by senior mortgages would also generate UBTI. However, in the past, it has been the practice, although not the obligation, of investment funds sponsored by the Manager’s affiliates to sell defaulting portfolio loans to the Servicer or its affiliates in order to avoid generation of UBTI in connection with possible foreclosures. The Company may continue such practice, although it is not obligated to do so. However, if the Company does continue the practice, it is possible that the IRS will consider the affiliated nature of the Servicer and disregard such sale for purposes of attributing UBTI to investors who are deemed partners,

clauses.head: In addition, the IRS has concluded in a
clauses.name: Guaranteed Payments
clauses.tail: NOTES WOULD CONSTITUTE DEDUCTIBLE GUARANTEED PAYMENT(S).
clauses.text: In addition, the IRS has concluded in a General Counsel Memorandum that guaranteed payments, such as the fixed payments provided for in the Notes, should be treated as interest for tax purposes if paid to a member and not as income from the Company’s investments. However, a general counsel memorandum may not be cited as authority. No assurances can be given that if the Notes are treated as equity, "interest" payments made with respect to the Notes would constitute deductible guaranteed payment(s).

In making such a determination, a fiduciary of a Plan Investor should be sure that the investment is in accordance with the governing instruments and the overall policies of the plan, and that the investment will comply with the diversification and prudence requirements of ERISA. clauses.name: Status of Noteholders and Company as Lenders
clauses.tail: TO WHICH NOTEHOLDERS MAY NOT BE ACCUSTOMED AS A RESULT OF OTHER INVESTMENT ACTIVITIES.
clauses.text: CONSIDERATIONS RELATING TO STATUS OF NOTEHOLDERS AND COMPANY AS LENDERS The Company is a lender with respect to its Portfolio Loans, and, for certain purposes, the Company may be deemed a borrower and the Noteholders may be deemed lenders with respect to the Notes. California and other states have numerous laws and regulations which apply to the activities of lenders and the rights of borrowers. The applicability of these laws and regulations, and their exemptions and exclusions, are frequently complex and highly fact-specific, and they vary by jurisdiction and are subject to change. In addition, litigation in a number of states has imposed liability upon lenders, or otherwise adversely impacted lenders, in ways to which Noteholders may not be accustomed as a result of other investment activities.

clauses.head: Usury A number of states have adopted usury
clauses.name: Usury
clauses.tail: A COURT IMPOSING TREBLE DAMAGES OR OTHER PENALTIES AND FINES, INCLUDING CRIMINAL PENALTIES.
clauses.text: Usury A number of states have adopted usury laws, which generally prohibit the charging of interest in certain circumstances in excess of a statutorily-defined rate. The rates of interest to be paid to the Noteholders by the Company, and the rates of interest to be paid by the Company’s Portfolio Borrowers to the Company, may exceed the applicable statutorily-defined usury rates. As of November 2007, charging interest at a rate greater than ten percent (10%) per annum is usurious in California unless an exemption or exclusion therefrom exists, but such threshold rate may change in the future in California or rates in other jurisdictions may be applicable. As a result, were any of the capital loans made by the Noteholders to the Company or by the Company to the Portfolio Borrowers to be challenged, as usurious, in certain circumstances, such as in a bankruptcy, it is possible other creditors, a bankruptcy trustee or receiver or another interested party (an “Interested Party”) would be able to successfully invalidate all or a portion of the interest due to the Noteholders or to the Company. This could result in a court imposing treble damages or other penalties and fines, including criminal penalties.

clauses.head: The Company intends to rely on qualified advisors
clauses.name: Compliance with Lending Laws
clauses.tail: TO MEET THE INVESTMENT OBJECTIVES OF THE COMPANY AND THIS OFFERING,
clauses.text: The Company intends to rely on qualified advisors and use commercially reasonable efforts to comply with laws and regulations applying to lenders and borrowers, and to seek exemptions and exclusions as advisable from such laws where appropriate to meet the investment objectives of the Company and this offering,

clauses.head: Lending Laws The California Finance Lenders Law and
clauses.name: Lending Laws and Licensing Risk
clauses.tail: SUBJECT TO SUCH RISK IN CONNECTION WITH ITS LOANS TO THE PORTFOLIO BORROWERS.
clauses.text: Lending Laws The California Finance Lenders Law and similar statues in other states may permit a borrower or a person acting on behalf of a borrower to avoid paying principal and interest on any loan made by a person required to be licensed under such a statute who does not become so registered. Any Noteholder that is not properly licensed as a finance lender in a jurisdiction which requires such licensing in connection with its loans to the Company may risk having its ability to collect principal and interest from the Company challenged by an Interested Party in any adversarial proceeding relating to the Company, such as bankruptcy. In addition, the Company itself may be subject to such risk in connection with its Loans to the Portfolio Borrowers.

clauses.head: The Company expects to make its Portfolio Loans
clauses.name: Finance-Lender Licensing and Compliance
clauses.tail: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE REGULATIONS BY THE COMPANY OR A NOTEHOLDER COULD RESULT IN CIVIL OR CRIMINAL PENALTIES.
clauses.text: The Company expects to make its Portfolio Loans pursuant to a finance lender’s license issued by California and other jurisdictions as applicable. The Company also intends to rely on qualified advisors and use commercially reasonable efforts to comply with laws and regulations applying to lenders and borrowers, and to seek exemptions and exclusions as advisable from such laws where appropriate to meet the investment objectives of the Company and this offering. The Manager anticipates that such efforts -3l- CONFIDENTIAL Case: 12-04137 Doc# 75-2 Filed: 09/16/13 Entered: 09/16/13 15:56:26 Page 3/ of 48 should be sufficient to avoid issues of noncompliance. However, Noteholders should be aware, that, under certain circumstances, a failure to comply with applicable regulations by the Company or a Noteholder could result in civil or criminal penalties.

clauses.head: Lender Liability As an additional consideration, legal decisions
clauses.name: Lender Liability
clauses.tail: THE COMPANY’S LOANS TO ITS PORTFOLIO BORROWERS.
clauses.text: Lender Liability As an additional consideration, legal decisions in many jurisdictions, including California, have imposed liability upon lenders for actions such as declaring defaults with respect to loans and refusing to meet Company loan commitments under certain circumstances. In addition, some courts have permitted litigants to pursue claims against lenders for environmental torts of a borrower and other liability as a result of their association with a borrower. Such so-called “lender liability” is a developing and uncertain area of the law, and there can be no assurance that such a claim could not be brought against the Company or, by extension, a Noteholder. In addition, in some cases, courts have recharacterized loans or debt securities as equity instruments, such that lenders or debt security holders have been subject to “equitable subordination” and thus not entitled to the preferred status of a creditor in a bankruptcy or other adversarial proceeding. Such decisions have been highly fact specific, and there can be no assurance that a court would not follow a similar approach with respect to the Noteholders’ loans to the Company, or the Company’s loans to its Portfolio Borrowers.
