clauses.text: Noteholders are encouraged to consult with their legal counsel regarding the lender-related issues discussed above.

clauses.head: VII. Risk Factors The purchase of Notes will
clauses.name: VII. Risk Factors — General Warning
clauses.tail: FACTORS, PROSPECTIVE NOTEHOLDERS ARE URGED TO CONSIDER THE FOLLOWING:
clauses.text: VII. Risk Factors The purchase of Notes will involve a high degree of risk. By its nature a summary of all possible risks is incomplete. However, among other factors, prospective Noteholders are urged to consider the following:

clauses.head: Risk Inherent in Relying on Management by Portfolio
clauses.name: Reliance on Portfolio Borrower Management
clauses.tail: MANAGED EXCLUSIVELY BY THE PRINCIPALS OF THE PORTFOLIO BORROWER OR ITS CO-INVESTORS OR AFFILIATES.
clauses.text: Risk Inherent in Relying on Management by Portfolio Borrower: Typically a Portfolio Borrower will be structured as a single purpose entity or venture for the purpose of acquiring, developing or holding the real property (a “Projecf’) collateralizing a Portfolio Loan. The Portfolio Borrower and the Project will be managed exclusively by the principals of the Portfolio Borrower or its co-investors or affiliates.

clauses.head: « No Voice in Portfolio Borrower Management, Noteholders
clauses.name: No Voice in Portfolio Borrower Management
clauses.tail: VALUE OF THE LOAN COLLATERAL IS LIKELY TO BE IMPAIRED.
clauses.text: No Voice in Portfolio Borrower Management, Noteholders will have no opportunity to directly affect the management of the Portfolio Borrower or of the Project. The Company is also likely to have little opportunity to influence the management of the Portfolio Borrower or Project, except to the limited extent of imposing conditions to the draw of funds under a Portfolio Loan. Therefore, the successful operation of the Portfolio Borrower, the choice and terms of any senior Project financing, the success of the Project, the repayment of a Portfolio Loan, and the ability of the Portfolio Borrower to repay the Portfolio Loan will depend greatly upon the skill, experience and efforts of the Portfolio Borrower in the acquisition, development, management, improvement and sale of the Project and in the management of the Portfolio Borrower. In the event the Project is not successfully completed, in addition to the inability of the Portfolio Manager to repay such Loan, the value of the Loan collateral is likely to be impaired.

clauses.head: ¢ No Prior History. Although a Portfolio Borrower
clauses.name: No Prior History
clauses.tail: COMPARABLE SUCCESS WITH RESPECT TO THE PROJECT COLLATERALIZING THE PORTFOLIO LOAN.
clauses.text: No Prior History. Although a Portfolio Borrower or its principals may be experienced real estate investors, the Project may have no operating or financial history. The prior successes of the principals of the Portfolio Borrower in connection with previous real estate investments are no assurance that the Portfolio Borrower will enjoy comparable success with respect to the Project collateralizing the Portfolio Loan.

clauses.head: if a Portfolio Loan or Project collateral is impaired by the poor performance of a Portfolio Borrower, the Company’s ability to repay the Notes may be impaired.
clauses.name: Effect of Portfolio Borrower Performance
clauses.text: if a Portfolio Loan or Project collateral is impaired by the poor performance of a Portfolio Borrower, the Company’s ability to repay the Notes may be impaired.

clauses.head: Risk Inherent in the Portfolio Borrower’s Investment in
clauses.name: Risks in Portfolio Borrower’s Real-Property Investment
clauses.tail: LOSS TO THE PROJECT OCCASIONED BY THE FOLLOWING:
clauses.text: Risk Inherent in the Portfolio Borrower’s Investment in Real Property: As noted, the Company’s ability to repay the Principal and Interest on the Notes will depend upon the Portfolio Borrower’s ability to manage the Project and to repay the Portfolio Loan, which ultimately depends upon the successful acquisition, management, operation and disposition by the Portfolio Borrower of the Project. In addition to the risks of poor management noted above, certain risks inherent in the operation of real property in general, or of a Project in particular, may adversely affect the ability of the Portfolio Borrower to repay the Portfolio Loan or may impair the value of the Project as collateral for the repayment of the Portfolio Loan. Such risks include, among others, a loss to the Project occasioned by the following:

clauses.head: e Changes in Economic Conditions. The Portfolio Borrower’s
clauses.name: Changes in Economic Conditions
clauses.tail: GENERAL CONDITIONS AND THE ECONOMY IN THE MARKET AREA OF THE PROJECT.
clauses.text: e Changes in Economic Conditions. The Portfolio Borrower’s investment in the Project will be subject to the risks generally incident to the ownership of real property, such as adverse changes in regional or local economic conditions, including local employment, interest rates, inflation, availability of funds, governmental rules and fiscal policies, existing competition and potential competition generated out of competing projects being built, leased or operated in the same general area as the Project. Additionally, national economic changes and international events may adversely impact general conditions and the economy in the market area of the Project.

clauses.head: e Increased Costs of Development or Operations. The
clauses.name: Increased Costs of Development or Operations
clauses.tail: THEN-EXISTING LAWS, ORDINANCES, REGULATIONS AND BUILDING CODES.
clauses.text: e Increased Costs of Development or Operations. The cost of planned development or operations of the Project may exceed estimates, or may not be permissible under then-existing laws, ordinances, regulations and building codes.

clauses.head: * Environmental Concerns. Under various federal, state and
clauses.name: Environmental Concerns
clauses.tail: WAS RESPONSIBLE FOR, THE PRESENCE OF HAZARDOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS.
clauses.text: Environmental Concerns. Under various federal, state and local laws, ordinances and regulations, an owner of real estate may be liable for the costs of clean-up of certain conditions relating to the presence of hazardous or toxic materials on, in or emanating from the Project, and any related damages to natural resources. Such laws often impose liability without regard to whether the owner knew of, or was responsible for, the presence of hazardous or toxic materials.

clauses.head: « Terms of Senior Financing. While leveraged investments
clauses.name: Terms of Senior Financing
clauses.tail: ITS ABILITY TO REPAY THE PORTFOLIO LOAN.
clauses.text: Terms of Senior Financing. While leveraged investments offer the opportunity for capital appreciation, such investments also involve a higher degree of risk. The Portfolio Borrower's financing of a Project may involve varying degrees of leverage in order to provide greater financial return to the Portfolio Borrower, as a result of which recessions, operating problems and other general business and economic risks may have a more pronounced effect on the profitability or survival of such investments than if leverage were not employed. The Portfolio Borrower may also have to make debt service payments, including interest, which will most likely fluctuate based on a spread above an underlying base rate. By its very nature, a variable interest rate will move up or down based on changes in the economy and other factors, all of which are beyond the control of the Portfolio Borrower. Accordingly, there can be no assurance that such rates will not rise significantly and, consequently, that a Portfolio Borrower would be required to pay more interest than is anticipated with respect to its senior financing on the Project, thereby impairing its ability to repay the Portfolio Loan.

clauses.head: e Foreclosure by Senior Lender. The Company may
clauses.name: Foreclosure by Senior Lender
clauses.tail: IN FULL BOTH THE SENIOR LOAN AND THE PORTFOLIO LOAN.
clauses.text: e Foreclosure by Senior Lender. The Company may suffer a loss of its Portfolio Loan upon a foreclosure of the Project by a senior Iender. The loans made to the Portfolio Borrower in connection with the acquisition and development of the Project may be secured by first and second mortgages on the Project. Incurring mortgage indebtedness increases the risk of loss to the Portfolio Borrower because the debt service must be paid. If there is a payment or other default on these senior loans, the lender may foreclose on the Project and the Project Owner will not have the capacity to repay all or a portion of the Portfolio Loans. The value of the Project in foreciosure may be insufficient collateral to repay in full both the senior loan and the Portfolio Loan.

clauses.head: * Mechanics Liens. The Project may be subject
clauses.name: Mechanics Liens
clauses.tail: FORECLOSE ON THE PROJECT IN ORDER TO SATISFY THE AMOUNT DUE UNDER THE HIEN.
clauses.text: Mechanics Liens. The Project may be subject to a mechanic’s lien which entitles the holder of such lien to foreclose on the Project. State law provides any person who supplies services or materials to a real estate project may impose a lien against the project securing any amounts owed to such person. Although the Portfolio Borrower may be required by the terms of the Portfolio Loan to utilize procedures to prevent the occurrence of mechanics’ liens (such as requiring mechanic lien releases prior to payment and issuing joint-party checks) no assurance can be given that mechanics’ liens will not appear against the Project. If a mechanic’s lien does appear, then it must be negotiated by the Portfolio Borrower in order to obtain its release or the person holding such lien will have the right to bring an action to foreclose on the Project in order to satisfy the amount due under the Hien.

clauses.head: s Eminent Domain. The Project or a portion
clauses.name: Eminent Domain
clauses.tail: REMAINING VALUE TO REPAY ACCRUED INTEREST AND PRINCIPAL ON FORECLOSURE.
clauses.text: s Eminent Domain. The Project or a portion of the Project could become subject to an eminent domain or inverse condemnation action. Such an action could have a material adverse effect on the operations or marketability of the Project, and, as a consequence, adversely affect the ability of the Portfolio Borrower to repay the Loan. In addition, the value of the Project as coilateral would be impaired and the Project may have insufficient remaining value to repay accrued Interest and Principal on foreclosure.

clauses.head: Risks Inherent in the Company’s Investment in Debt
clauses.name: Risks in Company Debt Investments
clauses.tail: BY THE TERMS OF ITS LOAN AGREEMENT, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION WITH RESPECT TO THE FOLLOWING:
clauses.text: Risks Inherent in the Company’s Investment in Debt Instruments. The Company’s funding of Portfolio Loans presents substantial risk to its capital that may affect its ability to repay Principal and Interest of the Notes, including risks that are inherent in the business of real estate lending. The CONFIDENTIAL of 48 Company, for instance, may be limited by law or by the terms of its loan agreement, including without limitation with respect to the following:

clauses.head: Effect on Risk of Portfolio Diversification. The financial
clauses.name: Effect of Portfolio Diversification
clauses.tail: A SUBSTANTIAL EFFECT ON THE LOAN PORTFOLIO’S RISK PROFILE.
clauses.text: Effect on Risk of Portfolio Diversification. The financial failure of a Portfolio Borrower and default on a Portfolio Loan could result in a significant reduction in the Company’s income. The Company will be relying solely on the value of the underlying collateral as security for the Portfolio Loan in such event. With respect to the collateral, the Company will be subject to general economic risks with respect to its debt investments similar to those experienced by the Portfolio Borrower with respect to the Project. Accordingly, the diversification of the Company’s Portfolio Loans with respect to borrowers, principal amounts, location and nature of collateral, and loan seniority will have a substantial effect on the Loan Portfolio’s risk profile.

clauses.head: Lender Remedies. Portfolio Loans will generally not be
clauses.name: Lender Remedies
clauses.tail: FROM PURSUING BOTH FORECLOSURE AND AN ACTION ON A NOTE SIMULTANEOUSLY.
clauses.text: Lender Remedies. Portfolio Loans will generally not be personal obligations of the applicable borrowers. In the event of a borrower default under a Portfolio Loan, the Company may be entitled to foreclose upon the property securing the Portfolio Loan. A foreclosure action or other lender remedies may be subject to delays and additional expenses if defenses or counterclaims are interposed, and may require several years to complete. Moreover, a non-collusive, regularly conducted foreclosure sale may be challenged as a fraudulent conveyance, regardless of the parties’ intent, if a court determines that the sale was for less than fair consideration and such sale occurred when the borrower was insolvent and within one year (or within the applicable state statute of limitations if the trustee in bankruptcy elects to proceed under state fraudulent conveyance laws) of the filing of bankruptcy. Similarly, a suit against a borrower on a note may take several years, and generally is a remedy alternative to foreclosure so that the Company may be precluded from pursuing both foreclosure and an action on a note simultaneously.

clauses.head: Cross-Collateralization of Loans. The repayment of one or
clauses.name: Cross-Collateralization of Loans
clauses.tail: PROVIDE PROTECTION IN THE EVENT THAT THE PORTFOLIO LOAN CEASES TO PERFORM.
clauses.text: Cross-Collateralization of Loans. The repayment of one or more of the Portfolio Loans may be cross-coliateralized by a direct or indirect interest in more than one Project. A Project will be released as collateral as it is sold and the payment is made on the Portfolio Loan. However, there is no assurance that Projects will be sold in the order of their coilateral value, or that the passage of time or changes in market conditions will preserve the value of remaining collateral. Therefore, the remaining Project may be insufficient collateral to provide protection in the event that the Portfolio Loan ceases to perform.

clauses.head: Inadequate Preservation of Collateral. Although the Company intends
clauses.name: Inadequate Preservation of Collateral
clauses.tail: THE APPLICABLE PORTFOLIO LOAN DOES NOT PERFORM COULD BE SUBSTANTIAL.
clauses.text: Inadequate Preservation of Collateral. Although the Company intends to require its Portfolio Borrowers to maintain adequate insurance coverage against liability for personal injury and property damage, such insurance may prove insufficient to cover any liabilities or casualty losses incurred by a Portfolio Borrower. Also certain risks may be uninsurable or may become uninsurable, or may become insurable only at prohibitive cost, such as the risk of property damage and general liability from earthquakes, floods, damage from terrorist activities, and/or certain environmental hazards. In addition, such risks may be insurable only in amounts that are less than the full market value or replacement cost of the relevant collateral. In addition to the unintentional loss of the collateral, the Portfolio Borrower may permit uninsured waste or other damage to the collateral by tenants, licensees or invitees. In the event of the occurrence of such risk or waste, the collateral may be substantially impaired or destroyed, and the potential loss to the Company in the event the applicable Portfolio Loan does not perform could be substantial.

clauses.head: Subordinated Loan Positions. The Company’s Portfolio Loans may
clauses.name: Subordinated Loan Positions
clauses.tail: THROUGH THIRD-PARTY FINANCING, WHICH MAY NOT BE AVAILABLE.
clauses.text: Subordinated Loan Positions. The Company’s Portfolio Loans may carry additional risks typical of subordinate loan positions, including subordinate positions to entities affiliated with the Manager, Other Sponsored Funds or other private investors working with the Manager or its affiliates. Where a Portfolio Borrower defaults under a mezzanine investment comprising a subordinate note in a loan evidenced by both a senior note and a subordinate note and secured by CONFIDENTIAL -35-~ Case: 12-04137 Doc#75-2 Filed: 09/16/13 Entered: 09/16/13 15:56:26” Page 41 of 48 a single mortgage lien encumbering the Portfolio Borrower’s real property, the Company may seek an inter-creditor agreement to provide the Company with the right to cure the Portfolio Borrower's defaults. Should such an inter-creditor agreement be in place, the Company would expect (a) to realize the value of any remaining equity in the collateral once the senior lender has completed foreclosure, or (b) provided sufficient funds are then available, to cure the Portfolio Borrower’s default with respect to the senior notes, buy the senior notes and/or foreclose the mortgage lien. In either case, the Company’s remedies will be subject to the rights of the senior lenders. Additionally, in order to purchase senior notes, the Company may need to obtain financing, either through capital raised from Noteholders or new investors, Company Borrowings, or through third-party financing, which may not be available.

clauses.head: Subordinated Loan with Equity Position Collateral. Should a
clauses.name: Subordinated Loan with Equity Position Collateral
clauses.tail: THE BASIS OF ITS EQUITY INTERESTS IN THE PORTFOLIO BORROWER.
clauses.text: Subordinated Loan with Equity Position Collateral. Should a Portfolio Loan be secured by a pledge of equity interests in a Portfolio Borrower, but be subordinate to a third party mortgage loan made simultaneously to such Borrower, the Company may be able to exercise its remedies independently of the senior lender’s remedies. However, if the Company forecloses on its equity pledge, the Company will then own the Portfolio Borrower, and become obligated for mortgage liabilities to the senior lender and other liabilities of a failing borrower. Additionally, the Company may be subject to equitable defenses to foreclosure on its loan collateral on the basis of its equity interests in the Portfolio Borrower.

clauses.head: Laws Regulating Lenders. In connection with the Portfolio
clauses.name: Laws Regulating Lenders
clauses.tail: PRINCIPAL OR INTEREST ON THE NOTES MAY BE MATERIALLY IMPAIRED.
clauses.text: Laws Regulating Lenders. In connection with the Portfolio Loans, the Company intends to use commercially reasonable efforts in reliance on qualified advisors, including its affiliate Bar-K, Inc., to comply with laws and regulations applying to lenders in the relevant jurisdictions. However, such laws are not always clearly applicable to a particular foan transaction or investment structure, or they may change. In such event, the Company’s interest in a Portfolio Loan may be materially impaired, with the consequence that the Company’s ability to repay Principal or Interest on the Notes may be materially impaired.

clauses.head: Usury. The structure of the Company’s Portfolio Loans
clauses.name: Usury Risk for Portfolio Loans
clauses.tail: PENALTIES AND FACE THE POTENTIAL LOSS OF ITS PORTFOLIO LOAN INVESTMENT.
clauses.text: Usury. The structure of the Company’s Portfolio Loans is expected to comply with California usury laws and the laws of other relevant jurisdictions. However, usury laws and their exemptions are complex and may change. If, despite the Company’s reasonable efforts in reliance on qualified advisors to avoid such a result, a Portfolio Loan made by the Company does not comply with applicable state usury laws, the Company may be responsible for payment of penalties and face the potential loss of its Portfolio Loan investment.

clauses.head: Risks Resulting from Conflicts of Interest between the
clauses.name: Conflicts between Company and Manager
clauses.tail: INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO, THE FOLLOWING:
clauses.text: Risks Resulting from Conflicts of Interest between the Company and the Manager and its Principals and Affiliates: The Manager, its affiliates and their principals, including the Principals, may have direct and indirect equity and compensation interests with respect to the Portfolio Loans, as well as in co-investors and in co-lenders with the Company, that are likely to create a conflict of interest between the investment interests of the Company and the investment interests of the Manager, its affiliates and principals. Risks and other considerations inherent in this context that may affect the Company’s ability to pay the Notes when due include, but are not limited to, the following:

clauses.head: Time Demands. The Manager or the Principals will
clauses.name: Time Demands
clauses.tail: WITH SUCH OTHER INVESTMENTS MAY CREATE A CONFLICT WITH THE COMPANY’S INTERESTS.
clauses.text: Time Demands. The Manager or the Principals will also pursue investment and lending activities with R.E. Loans and Other Sponsored Funds, as well as for private investors with whom they may choose to do business. In addition, Principals may have commitments in connection with the management of affiliates of the Company or Manager. Although the Manager anticipates that they will have sufficient resources and time to commit to the management of the Company for the CONFIDENTIAL Case: 12-04137 Doc# 75-2 Filed: o9/i6/13 Entered: 09/16/13 15:56:26 Page 42 of 48 benefit of the Noteholders, their interests and activities in connection with such other investments may create a conflict with the Company’s interests.

clauses.head: Proportionally Disproportionate Interest of Manager. The Company’s Manager
clauses.name: Proportionally Disproportionate Interest of Manager
clauses.tail: WITH RESPECT TO THE USE OF THE COMPANY’S CAPITAL MAY DIVERGE FROM THAT OF A NOTEHOLDER.
clauses.text: Proportionally Disproportionate Interest of Manager. The Company’s Manager and its members will receive Company gains and certain other income that, relative to their capital contribution to the Company, are proportionally greater than the Interest payable to Noteholders on account of their investment in the Notes, Accordingly, the Manager’s risk profile with respect to the use of the Company’s capital may diverge from that of a Noteholder.

clauses.head: Potential Conflicts of Interest. The Manager may encounter
clauses.name: Potential Conflicts of Interest
clauses.tail: CO-INVEST WITH THE COMPANY OR PURCHASE OR SELL LOANS FROM OR TO THE COMPANY.
clauses.text: Potential Conflicts of Interest. The Manager may encounter various potential and actual conflicts of interest between itself and the Company as a function of various activities including, but not limited to, the provision by its affiliates or Principals of certain management or other real estate related services to the Portfolio Borrower or its affiliates. Also, the Manager, its Principals or affiliates may encounter various conflicts of interest with the Company in the event that they or an Other Sponsored Fund or private investor with whom they are doing business co-invest with the Company or purchase or sell loans from or to the Company.

clauses.head: Accordingly, no person should purchase Notes from the
clauses.name: Entrustment of Management
clauses.tail: VALUATION OF THE PROJECTS AND THE TERMS OF THE PORTFOLIO LOANS TO THE MANAGER.
clauses.text: Accordingly, no person should purchase Notes from the Company unless he is willing to entrust all aspects of the management, financing, and development of a Project to the Portfolio Borrower, and management of the Company, valuation of the Projects and the terms of the Portfolio Loans to the Manager.

clauses.head: Risks Inherent in Private Equity Investments: In addition
clauses.name: Private Equity Investment Risks
clauses.tail: PARTICULAR TO THE COMPANY, INCLUDING THE FOLLOWING:
clauses.text: Risks Inherent in Private Equity Investments: In addition to risks associated with investments in real property related assets, the purchase of Notes from the Company will also be subject to certain risks that are typical of investments in private equity funds, as well as risks which are more particular to the Company, including the following:

clauses.head: No Operating History. The Company will begin operations
clauses.name: No Operating History
clauses.tail: CANNOT BE RELIED UPON TO PREDICT THE COMPANY’S SUCCESS.
clauses.text: No Operating History. The Company will begin operations upon closing. It has no operating history and has not identified all of its portfolio loans. Although the Principals and affiliates of the Manager and their sponsored investment vehicles may have achieved favorable returns with some of their previous loan investments, the performance of past investments cannot be relied upon to predict the Company’s success.

clauses.head: Concentration af Loan Investments. Depending upon the amount
clauses.name: Concentration of Loan Investments
clauses.tail: DIVERSIFIED IN THE NUMBER AND LOCATION OF PORTFOLIO LOANS AND PORTFOLIO BORROWERS.
clauses.text: Concentration af Loan Investments. Depending upon the amount of capital committed by prospective Noteholders, the Company’s portfolio may become concentrated in a limited number of portfolio loans, increasing the vulnerability of the portfolio as compared with a portfolio that is more diversified in the number and location of portfolio loans and Portfolio Borrowers.

clauses.head: Unspecified Investments. A Notehoider must rely upon the
clauses.name: Unspecified Investments
clauses.tail: IF SUFFICIENTLY ATTRACTIVE LOAN OPPORTUNITIES ARE NOT IDENTIFIED.
clauses.text: Unspecified Investments. A Notehoider must rely upon the ability of the Manager to identify, structure and implement portfolio loans consistent with the Company’s investment objective. There can be no assurance that loans of a suitable nature will be available on the market. It is possible that the Company will never be fully invested if sufficiently attractive loan opportunities are not identified.

clauses.head: Failure of Security. Although the Company’s repayment of
clauses.name: Failure of Security
clauses.tail: SUFFICIENT TO REPAY ALL OUTSTANDING PRINCIPAL AND INTEREST ON THE NOTES.
clauses.text: Failure of Security. Although the Company’s repayment of the Notes will be secured by an interest in the assets of the Company, such security interest may be subordinated to senior security interests in connection with possible Company Borrowings, as well as to statutorily protected interests, such as liens in connection with unpaid taxes. The terms of Company CONFIDENTIAL ~ 37 - of 48 Borrowings may also impose certain conditions on subordinate lenders with respect to the exercise of remedies in the event the Company is in default under the Company Borrowing, Therefore, there is no assurance that the Noteholders’ security interest will be perfected in seniority over the interests of other creditors of the Company in such assets, that its remedies will be enforceable, or if such collateral is foreclosed upon, that it will be sufficient to repay all outstanding Principal and Interest on the Notes.

clauses.head: e Restrictions on Transferability. The transferability of the
clauses.name: Restrictions on Transferability
clauses.tail: NOTE AND BY FEDERAL AND STATE SECURITIES LAWS.
clauses.text: e Restrictions on Transferability. The transferability of the Notes will be severely restricted by the Note Purchase Agreement, the terms of the Note and by federal and state securities laws.

clauses.head: ¢ No Market; illiquidity of Notes, An investment
clauses.name: No Market; Illiquidity of Notes
clauses.tail: FOR INVESTMENT ONLY AND NOT WITH A VIEW TO THE RESALE OR DISTRIBUTION THEREOF.
clauses.text: No Market; illiquidity of Notes, An investment in the Notes will be illiquid and involves a high degree of risk. There is no public market for the Notes, and it is not expected that a public market will develop. Consequently, Noteholders will bear the economic risks of their investment until the Notes are paid in full. Prospective Noteholders will be required to represent and agree that they are purchasing the Notes for their own account for investment only and not with a view to the resale or distribution thereof.

clauses.head: « Passive investment. The structure of a Noteholder’s
clauses.name: Passive Investment
clauses.tail: THAT WILL BE USED BY THE MANAGER IN MAKING DECISIONS.
clauses.text: Passive investment. The structure of a Noteholder’s investment in the Notes precludes the Noteholders from active participation in the Company’s investment lending decisions or from voting on Company operating matters. Moreover, the Noteholders will not be permitted to evaluate Portfolio Loan opportunities or relevant business, economic, financial or other information that will be used by the Manager in making decisions.

clauses.head: * Dependence on Management Team. Decisions with respect
clauses.name: Dependence on Management Team
clauses.tail: FROM BEING ADMITTED TO THE MANAGER’S MANAGEMENT TEAM FOR THE COMPANY.
clauses.text: Dependence on Management Team. Decisions with respect to the management of the Company will be made by the Principals. The success of the Company will depend on the ability of the Principals to identify and consummate suitable Portfolio Loans, and to improve the performance of such Portfolio Loans. The loss of the services of one or more of the Principals could have a material adverse impact on the Company’s ability to realize its investment objectives. Further, certain of such Principals may have significant business commitments to other companies or activities, including to R.E. Loans and Other Sponsored Investment Funds, that will occupy some portion of his business time. Additional persons may be admitted as principals of the Manager following the Company’s initial closing, and the Noteholders will have no power to prevent any specific person from being admitted to the Manager’s management team for the Company.

clauses.head: * Tax, ERISA and Other Legal Matters. There
clauses.name: Tax, ERISA and Other Legal Matters
clauses.tail: ITS OWN LEGAL, TAX AND ERISA ADVISORS BEFORE PURCHASING NOTES.
clauses.text: Tax, ERISA and Other Legal Matters. There are risks associated with the tax aspects of an investment in the Notes and of the Company’s Loans that are complex and will not be the same for all prospective Notehoiders. Also, some Notehoiders, depending upon their state of residence, may be subject to certain laws and regulations governing the lending of money. Similarly, payment of the Notes to Noteholders who are not California residents may, depending upon their state of residence, be subject to certain defenses by the Company or interested persons claiming through the Company under applicable usury laws. In addition, there may be special concerns for investors subject to ERISA and any rules or regulations promulgated thereunder. Please review Section VI Tax and Legal Considerations of this Memorandum, Each proposed investor is advised to consult its own legal, tax and ERISA advisors before purchasing Notes.

clauses.text: 3. Trade Terms. The Debtors shall pay for the Goods delivered by MGF in full no later than fourteen (14) calendar days after delivery; provided that the Debtors shall pay for Goods to be delivered by MGF in full on a cash in advance basis (with respect to each specific individual delivery of Goods, no later than two business days prior to the delivery of any such Goods) after an Event of Default (as defined in the DIP Financing) has occurred under the Debtors’ current Secured Superpriority Debtor in Possession Loan, Security and Guaranty Agreement, the Interim Order Pursuant to 11 U.S.C. §§105, 361, 362, 363 and 364 and Rules 2002, 4001 and 9014 of the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure (i) Authorizing Incurrence by the Debtors of Postpetition Secured Indebtedness, (ii) Granting Liens, (iii) Authorizing Use of Cash Collateral by the Debtors and Providing for Adequate Protection, (iv) Modifying the Automatic Stay, and (v) Scheduling a Final Hearing, entered on May 6, 2016, or any final order referenced therein (collectively, the “DIP Financing”), unless such Event of Default was (a) caused by or related to any breach by MGF of the terms of this Agreement and/or the Sourcing Agreement, as modified by this Agreement; (b) cured by the Debtors in accordance with the terms of the DIP Financing or waived by the administrative agent under the DIP Financing within ten (10) calendar days of the occurrence of such Event of Default; or (c) caused by MGF’s acceleration of the Detailed Delivery Schedule (other than at the request of the Debtors). All payments referenced herein shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by MGF in writing on or prior to the date hereof unless and until MGF changes such account designation in writing.

clauses.head: 4. Run-Off License. In the event of a
clauses.name: 4. Run-Off License

clauses.text: 4. Run-Off License. In the event of a liquidation of all or substantially all of the Debtors’ retail stores and/or the merchandise held for sale therein (a “Full Chain Liquidation”) approved by the Bankruptcy Court, beginning as of the commencement date of such Full Chain Liquidation as set forth in an agency agreement governing such Full Chain Liquidation (such date, the “Commencement Date”) and ending on the later of (x) December 31, 2017 and (y) one year after the commencement of such Full Chain Liquidation, the Debtors hereby grant MGF a worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid up, irrevocable run-off license to all of the Debtors’ trademarks and other intellectual property of any kind sufficient to permit MGF to sell Goods not yet delivered to the Debtors (but only to the extent that title to such Goods has not passed to the Debtors), subject to the following: (a) the run-off license shall not permit MGF (or its agents or representatives) to sell Goods in the United States during the sixty (60) day period immediately following the Commencement Date (it being agreed that in the event any such Full Chain Liquidation is stayed by the Bankruptcy Court for any reason, such sixty (60) day period shall be extended day-for-day concurrently with the period of such stay), and (b) if MGF wants to sell Goods to a third party in any country (other than the United States) in which the Debtors currently (as of the date hereof) authorize the sale of Aéropostale products to any licensee, then in such country MGF may only sell such Goods to such licensee. Subject to the foregoing limitations, the run-off license shall provide that, effective as of the commencement of such license as described above, MGF shall be entitled to complete the manufacture of, sell or otherwise dispose of all or any of the Goods not yet delivered to the Debtors (but only to the extent that title to such Goods has not passed to the Debtors) and make any advertisement or other promotion in furtherance thereof on a worldwide basis through one or more sales channels as MGF deems appropriate in it sole discretion (it being agreed and understood that no such advertisement or promotion shall be commenced until such run-off license becomes effective; for the avoidance of doubt, there shall be no advertising or promotion in the United States (or relating to sales of Goods to occur in the United States) prior to the date on which MGF is permitted to sell such Goods in the United States as set forth in clause (a) of the preceding sentence); provided that the run-off license shall be expressly limited to the foregoing and shall be valid for no other purpose. Notwithstanding the foregoing, MGF shall not be entitled to such license if the Court denies the proposed DIP Financing on a final basis based on the objection of Aero Investors LLC, MGF Sourcing Holdings, Limited (f/k/a TSAM Holdings, Limited) or Sycamore Partners or any of its affiliates.

clauses.text: 6. Sourcing Agreement Termination. The Debtors shall not submit any new orders to MGF under the Sourcing Agreement, and the Debtors shall notify their international licensees that they will not be permitted to submit any new orders to MGF. After MGF makes the last delivery of Goods set forth on the Detailed Delivery Schedule and the Debtors make the final payment for Goods delivered by MGF, in each case as contemplated by this Agreement, the Sourcing Agreement shall automatically terminate and be of no further force or effect. The parties hereto each acknowledge and agree that the termination fee, the shortfall payment, and the rebate provisions of the Sourcing Agreement shall be of no further force or effect as of the date that the Settlement Order (as defined hereinafter) becomes a final order. MGF further agrees not to make any claim related to the termination fee and the shortfall payment under the Sourcing Agreement and the Debtors agree to waive any claim for any rebate under the Sourcing Agreement.

clauses.text: 7. Bankruptcy Court Approval/Effectiveness of Agreement. The parties to this Agreement shall comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement pending approval of this Agreement by the Bankruptcy Court, and MGF shall continue to take all actions necessary to comply with its production and delivery obligations for all of the Goods. The Debtors shall file a revised version of Exhibit A to the motion to approve this Agreement pursuant to Rule 9019 of the Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure (the “Settlement Motion”) on May 20, 2016, and shall seek the Settlement Motion’s approval by the Bankruptcy Court on May 23, 2016. If the Debtors do not file the Settlement Motion and seek Bankruptcy Court approval thereof in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, or if the Bankruptcy Court either denies the Settlement Motion or fails to enter an order approving the Settlement Motion in form and substance reasonably acceptable to MGF (the “Settlement Order”) on or before May 30, 2016, then this Agreement shall be of no further force or effect; provided that the Debtors’ obligation to pay for any Goods delivered prior thereto and MGF’s obligation to provide 14 day payment terms for any such Goods delivered prior thereto shall survive until fully performed.

The parties acknowledge that the pricing information contained in the Detailed Delivery Schedule is confidential and proprietary information and they each agree to keep such pricing information confidential and not disclose it to any person or entity without the prior written consent of the other party. If such pricing information is required to be disclosed under applicable law, regulation or legal process, or if necessary to enforce a party’s rights under this Agreement, the disclosing party must take all reasonable actions necessary to obtain a protective order or file the information under seal so as to protect the pricing information from disclosure, to the extent possible, consistent with the applicable law, regulation or legal process that made disclosure necessary. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Debtors may disclose the pricing information to the agent and lenders under the DIP Financing, the Debtors’ term loan lenders and, on a “professionals-eyes-only” basis, to the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors appointed in the Debtors’ chapter 11 cases, in each case so long as the recipient agrees to keep such information confidential in accordance with this paragraph.

Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, to the extent that either the Debtors or MGF need assistance to comply with the delivery or acceptance of Goods, the other shall use reasonable business efforts, whenever possible, and the party seeking such assistance shall, whenever possible, provide the other party with reasonable advance notice of such need for assistance. clauses.head: "Additional Indebtedness Holder's Pro Rata Interest" means with
clauses.name: 1.01 “Additional Indebtedness Holder's Pro Rata Interest”
clauses.tail: same terms as the required by the Loans.
clauses.text: "Additional Indebtedness Holder's Pro Rata Interest" means with respect to each holder of Additional Indebtedness, on the date that the Boffower is required to make a mandatory prepayment (and not an optional prepayment) of the Additional Indebtedness in accordance with Section 2.11 (f) hereof, the percentage detennined by the quotient of (a) the principal amount of the then Additional Indebtedness outstanding owed to such holder of Additional Indebtedness divided by (b) the sum of (i) the principal amount of the Loans outstanding on such date to all Lenders, (ii) the principal amount of the Supplier Financing outstanding on such date, and (iii) the principal amount of any Additional Indebtedness, outstanding on such date, under which the creditors thereof share on a pari passu basis the security interest of the Lenders in the relevant Collateral affected by such mandatory prepayment, on such date, if and to the extent the Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors or the creditors under any Additional Indebtedness on such date require a mandatory prepayment (and not an optional prepayment) on the same terms as the required by the Loans.

clauses.head: "Additional Obligations" means, with respect to the Borrower,
clauses.name: 1.01 “Additional Obligations”
clauses.tail: extent arising in connection with the Additional Obligations.
clauses.text: "Additional Obligations" means, with respect to the Borrower, the obligations under the Supplier Financing, including, without limitation, (a) the due and punctual payment by the Boffower of (i) the principal of and interest (including interest accruing during the pendency of any bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership or similar proceeding, regardless of whether allowed or allowable in such proceeding) on the loans, when and as due, whether at maturity, by acceleration, upon one or more dates set for prepayment or otherwise, and (ii) all other monetary obligations of the Boffower under the Supplier Financing and the loan documents in connection therewith, including in respect of fees, costs, expenses and indemnities (including any monetary obligations incuffed during the pendency of any bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership or similar proceeding, regardless of whether allowed or allowable in such proceeding), in each case to the Credit Agreement -2- extent arising in connection with the Additional Obligations, and (b) the due and punctual performance of all other obligations of the Borrower under or pursuant to the Supplier Financing and the loan documents in connection therewith, in each case to the extent arising in connection with the Additional Obligations.

clauses.head: "Additional Security Documents" means any additional or supplemental
clauses.name: 1.01 “Additional Security Documents”
clauses.tail: to the reasonable satisfaction of the Security Agent.

clauses.head: "Adjusted Net Income" means, for any period, the
clauses.name: 1.01 “Adjusted Net Income”
clauses.tail: the Transactions, in each case, for such period.
clauses.text: "Adjusted Net Income" means, for any period, the net income of Borrower for such period detennined in accordance with GAAP; provided, however, that there shall not be included in the calculation of such Adjusted Net Income: (1) any net income of any Person (other than Borrower), except that: (A) subject to the limitations contained in clause ( 4) below, Borrower's equity in the net income of any such person for such period shall be included in such Adjusted Net Income up to the aggregate amount of cash actually distributed by such Person during such period to Borrower as a dividend or other distribution; and (B) Borrower's equity in a net loss of any such Person for such period shall be included in determining such Adjusted Net Income; (2) any nel income (or loss) of any Person at:y_ uireu by Burrower in a pooling of interests transaction (or any transaction accounted for in a manner similar to a pooling of interests) for any period prior to the date of such acquisition; (3) any gain (or loss) realized upon the sale or other disposition of any asset of Borrower (including pursuant to any sale and leaseback transaction) that is not sold or otherwise disposed of in the ordinary course of business and any gain (or loss) realized upon the sale brother disposition of any Equity Interest in any Person; (4) any extraordinary, unusual or nonrecurring gain or loss; (5) the cumulative effect of a change in accounting principles; (6) any noncash gain or loss attributable to any Hedging Agreement relating to commodity prices until such time as it is settled, at which time the net gain or loss shall be included; (7) accruals and reserves that are established within twelve (12) months after the Effective Date and that are so required to be established as a result of the Transactions in accordance with GAAP, and any accrual or reserve that is established in the event of the filing of any action, suit or proceeding by or before any arbitrator or Governrnental Authority against or affecting Borrower that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect that occurs prior to the Commercial Operations Date, with respect to which a contribution to the Borrower's Equity Interests or other capital contribution, or an advance of an Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans, has been Credit Agreement -3- made with respect to such accrual or to fund such reserve in respect of any liability or Indebtedness (or the creation of any reserve) arising as a result of such action, suit or proceeding; (8) any increase in amortization, depletion, depreciation and depletion, cost of goods sold attributable to metal inventories or any one-time noncash charges resulting from purchase accounting in connection with the Transactions or any acquisition that is consummated after the Effective Date; (9) any noncash impairment charges resulting from the application of Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 142 and No. 144 and any amortization of intangibles pursuant to Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 141; (10) any net after-tax income or loss from discontinued operations and any net after-tax gain or loss on disposal of discontinued operations; (11) any noncash compensation expense recognized from grants of stock appreciation or similar rights, stock options, restricted stock, restricted stock units or other rights to officers, governors and employees of the Borrower; and (12) any premiums, fees and expenses (and any amortization thereof) paid in connection with the Transactions, in each case, for such period.

clauses.head: "Adjusted Tangible Net Worth" means, in each case
clauses.name: 1.01 “Adjusted Tangible Net Worth”
clauses.tail: a result of such action, suit or proceeding.
clauses.text: "Adjusted Tangible Net Worth" means, in each case and without double counting, (a) amounts paid up as issued ordinary share capital (or equivalent for limited liability companies); plus (b) amounts standing to the credit of the reserves, including any amount credited to the share premium account (or equivalent for limited liability companies); minus (c) any debit balance on the profit and loss account; plus (d) any credit balance on the profit and loss account; minus ( e) any amount shown in respect of goodwill or other intangible assets, such as patents; minus (f) bad or doubtful expenses not provided for; minus (g) any provision for defen-ed Taxes; plus (h) any deferred Tax refund or other Tax asset; minus (i) any amounts arising from an upward revaluation of assets made; minus (j) any amount in respect of any dividend or distribution declared, recommended or made and to the extent such distribution is not provided for in the most recent financial statements; minus (k) any investments or loans or advances provided to any Affiliate; plus (1) amounts in respect of the principal amount of Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans; minus (m) in the event of the filing of any action, suit or proceeding by or before any arbitrator or Governmental Authority against or affecting Borrower that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect that occurs prior to the Commercial Operations Date, any contribution to the Borrower's Equity Interests or other capital contribution, or advance of an Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans, in respect of any liability or Indebtedness (or the creation of any reserve) arising as a result of such action, suit or proceeding.

clauses.name: 1.01 “Affiliate”
clauses.tail: is under common Control with the Person specified.
clauses.text: "Affiliate" means, with respect to a specified Person, another Person that directly, or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, Controls or is Controlled by or is under common Control with the Person specified.

For the avoidance of doubt, the term "Attributable Debt" excludes operating leases entered into the ordinary course of business that are not required under GAAP to be treated as a Capital Lease Obligation.

clauses.head: "Cash" means at any time with respect to
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash”
clauses.tail: or prepayment of the Borrowings under this Agreement.
clauses.text: "Cash" means at any time with respect to the Borrower, cash on hand or cash at reputable banks or financial institutions, acceptable to the Lenders, credited to an account in the name of the Borrower and to which the Borrower is alone beneficially entitled and for so long as (a) that cash is repayable on demand, (b) repayment of that cash is not contingent on the prior discharge of any other Indebtedness of the Borrower or any other Person whatsoever or on the satisfaction of any other condition, (c) there is no Lien over that cash (other than pursuant to the Security Documents, and (d) such cash is freely and immediately available to be applied in repayment or prepayment of the Borrowings under this Agreement.

clauses.head: "Cash Available" means for any period, as applicable
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Available”
clauses.tail: (d) Net Finance Charges, plus (e) noncash write-offs.
clauses.text: "Cash Available" means for any period, as applicable to the Borrower, (a) standalone net profits after taxation, plus (b) amounts attributable to amortization or goodwill, plus (c) amounts attributable to depreciation and depletion of tangible assets, plus (d) Net Finance Charges, plus (e) noncash write-offs.

clauses.head: "Cash Equivalent Investments" means Investments that are marketable
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Equivalent Investments”
clauses.tail: Cash without incurring any significant premium or penalty.
clauses.text: "Cash Equivalent Investments" means Investments that are marketable securities with a maturity ofless than twelve (12) months from the date of their acquisition by the Borrower, issued or fully guaranteed by the government of the United States of America or by any member state of the European Union and certificates of deposit or time deposits with a maturity ofless than six (6) months, issued by a commercial bank, in each case, in freely conve1iible currency, which is not issued by the Borrower or Affiliate of the B01rnwer, and which are readily convertible into Cash without incurring any significant premium or penalty.

clauses.head: "Cash Sweep Cash Available" means, without double counting,
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep Cash Available”
clauses.tail: if such amount would otherwise be included therein.
clauses.text: "Cash Sweep Cash Available" means, without double counting, for any period, as applicable to the Bo1rnwer, (a) standalone net profits after taxation, plus (b) amounts attributable to amortization or goodwill, plus (c) amounts attributable to depreciation and depletion of tangible assets, plus (d) Net Finance Charges, plus (e) noncash write-offs, and minus (f) the lesser of actual maintenance capital expenditures and US$12,500,000, provided, however, as a clarification of the foregoing, to the extent an amount has been or is to be paid as a mandatory prepayment in accordance with Section 2.11 (c), such amount shall not be included in Cash Sweep Cash Available for purposes of determining the Cash Sweep DSCR, if such amount would otherwise be included therein, but any amount arising from an event or receipt referred to in Section 2.11( c) that is not so applied as a mandatory prepayment will be included in Cash Sweep Cash Available, if such amount would otherwise be included therein.

clauses.head: "Cash Sweep Debt Service" means, for any period,
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep Debt Service”
clauses.tail: scheduled repayments of any Permitted Capex Additional Indebtedness.
clauses.text: "Cash Sweep Debt Service" means, for any period, (a) Cash Sweep Net Finance Charges, plus (b) all scheduled repayments of Loans to Project Lenders pursuant to Section 2.09 hereof, corresponding scheduled repayments of any Supplier Financing, and scheduled repayments of any Permitted Capex Additional Indebtedness.

clauses.head: "Cash Sweep DSCR" means the amount of Cash
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep DSCR”
clauses.tail: Cash Available divided by Cash Sweep Debt Service.
clauses.text: "Cash Sweep DSCR" means the amount of Cash Sweep Cash Available divided by Cash Sweep Debt Service.

clauses.head: "Cash Sweep Mechanism" means: (i) for the First
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep Mechanism” (i)
clauses.tail: the amount of Reference Cash Sweep Debt Service;
clauses.text: "Cash Sweep Mechanism" means: (i) for the First Sweep Period, on each Sweep Payment Date for each Sweep Date occurring in such period, if the Reference Cash Sweep DSCR for the Sweep Date immediately preceding such Sweep Payment Date results in an amount in excess of 1.25, the Lenders and the Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors shall have the right to receive an aggregate amount (a "First Sweep Period Sweep Amount") equal to fifty percent (50%) of (x) Reference Cash Sweep DSCR minus 1.25, multiplied by (y) the amount of Reference Cash Sweep Debt Service;

clauses.head: (ii) for the Second Sweep Period, on each
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep Mechanism” (ii)
clauses.tail: the amount of Reference Cash Sweep Debt Service;
clauses.text: (ii) for the Second Sweep Period, on each Sweep Payment Date for each Sweep Date occurring in such period, if the Reference Cash Sweep DSCR for the Sweep Date immediately preceding such Sweep Payment Date results in an amount (a "Second Sweep Period Sweep Amount") in excess of 1.15, the Lenders and the Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors shall have the right to receive an aggregate amount equal to fifty percent (50%) of (x) Reference Cash Sweep DSCR minus 1.15, multiplied by (y) the amount of Reference Cash Sweep Debt Service;

clauses.head: (iii) the Lenders and Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep Mechanism” (iii)
clauses.tail: Interest in accordance with Section 2.1 l(f); and
clauses.text: (iii) the Lenders and Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors shall have the right to receive on each Sweep Payment Date the Sweep Amount for such Sweep Payment Date, first out of cash available in the Escrow Account for such payment, and then, to the extent of any deficiency in cash available in the Escrow Account on a Sweep Payment Date to fully pay the Sweep Amount, out of cash in the DSRA. The Sweep Amount shall be applied for prepayment of the Loans then outstanding pro rata Lo each Lemler in accordance with its Lender's Pro Rata Interest in accordance with Section 2.11 (c)(vii), and in repayment of the Supplier Financing then outstanding in accordance with each Upstream Supplier Financing Creditor's Pro Rata Interest in accordance with Section 2.1 l(f); and

clauses.head: (iv) calculations made with respect to unaudited results
clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep Mechanism” (iv)
clauses.tail: on the Sweep Payment Date for such period.
clauses.text: (iv) calculations made with respect to unaudited results for the fourth fiscal quarter shall be retroactively adjusted in the event the audited results for such period require a different Sweep Amount, and such adjustment shall be made in the distributions with respect to the Sweep Amount for the first fiscal quarter and paid on the Sweep Payment Date for such period.

clauses.name: 1.01 “First Sweep Period”
clauses.tail: Operations Date, to but excluding April 1, 2014.

clauses.tail: Amount or a Second Sweep Period Sweep Amount.
clauses.text: "Sweep Amount" means a First Sweep Period Sweep Amount or a Second Sweep Period Sweep Amount.

clauses.name: 1.01 “Second Sweep Period”

clauses.name: 1.01 “Sweep Payment Date”

clauses.name: 1.01 “Sweep Period”

clauses.text: "Sweep Period" means the First Sweep Period or the Second Sweep Period, as the case may be.

clauses.name: 1.01 “Cash Sweep Net Finance Charges”

clauses.text: "Cash Sweep Net Finance Charges" means, with respect to any period and without any double counting, the aggregate of interest, commission, fees, discounts, prepayment penalties or premiums and other finance payments in respect of any Loans, Supplier Financing or Pennitted Capex Additional Indebtedness, whether accrued or paid for such period and whether or not capitalized, including for such period the net amount accrued or paid, or reduced by the net amount accrued or received, by the BoITower under any interest rate Hedging Agreements entered into in respect of any of such Loans or Supplier Financing, minus the amounts received by the Borrower as interest on Permitted Investments for such period.

clauses.name: 1.01 “Indebtedness”
clauses.tail: such Indebtedness provide that such Person is not liable therefor.
clauses.text: "Indebtedness" of any Person means, without duplication, (a) all obligations of such Person for borrowed money, (b) all obligations of such Person evidenced by bonds, debentures, notes or similar instruments, (c) all obligations of such Person under conditional sale or other title retention agreements relating to property acquired by such Person, (d) all obligations of such Person in respect of the deferred purchase price of property or services (excluding trade accounts payable and other accrued expenses incurred in the ordinary course of business and deferred compensation), (e) all Indebtedness of others secured by (or for which the holder of such Indebtedness has an existing right, contingent or otherwise, to be secured by) any Lien on property owned or acquired by such Person, whether or not the Indebtedness secured thereby has been assumed, (f) all Guaranties by such Person of Indebtedness of others, and any put options, shortfall undertakings, letters of comfort or any obligation undertaken by such Person in the nature of a payment obligation, (g) all Capital Lease Obligations of such Person, (h) all obligations, contingent or otherwise, of such Person as an account party (including reimbursement obligations to the issuer) in respect ofletters of credit and letters of guaranty, which support or secure Indebtedness, (i) all obligations in respect of any Working Capital Bank Facility and all other obligations in respect of prepaid production arrangements, prepaid forward sale arrangements or derivative contracts in respect of which such Person receives upfront payments in consideration of an obligation to deliver product or commodities (or make cash payments based on the value of product or commodities) at a future time, (j) all obligations, contingent or otherwise, of such Person in respect of bankers' acceptances, and (k) all obligations of a Person under any Hedging Agreement. The Indebtedness of any Person shall include the Indebtedness of any other entity (including any partnership in which such Person is a general partner) to the extent such Person is liable therefor as a result of such Person's ownership interest in or other relationship with such entity, except to the extent the terms of such Indebtedness provide that such Person is not liable therefor.

clauses.text: "Insurance and Other Proceeds Account" means the Insurance and Other Proceeds Account established by the Borrower with the Escrow Agent and Account Bank pursuant to the Collateral Account Agreement into which the Borrower shall deposit all proceeds from any Equity Interest proceeds, insurance, expropriation the proceeds of the sale of assets and other proceeds and amounts in respect of events set forth in clauses (i) through (vi) of Section 2.11 (c) which may give rise to a mandatory prepayment. Funds deposited in the Insurance and Other Proceeds Account shall be allocated and distributed as set forth in the Collateral Account Agreement.

clauses.head: "Insurance Premium Financing" means Indebtedness owed to institutional
clauses.name: 1.01 “Insurance Premium Financing”

clauses.text: "Insurance Premium Financing" means Indebtedness owed to institutional providers (other than Affiliates of the Borrower) of financing of annual or longer premium payments required under any of the Borrower's insurance policies in the ordinary course of the Borrower's business.

clauses.head: "Intercreditor Agent" means any financial institution appointed by

clauses.head: "Interest Period" means (a) with respect to the
clauses.name: 1.01 “Interest Period”
clauses.tail: the effective date of the most recent conversion or continuation of such Borrowing.
clauses.text: "Interest Period" means (a) with respect to the initial Borrowing hereunder, the period commencing on the date of such initial Borrowing and ending on the numerically corresponding day in the calendar month that is three (3) or six (6) months thereafter, as the Borrower may elect in its Interest Election Request in accordance with Section 2.07, and (b) with respect to all subsequent Borrowings after the initial Borrowing hereunder, (i) the first Interest Pe1iod of each such subsequent Borrowing shall end on the last day of the Interest Period applicable to the initial Borrowing hereunder falling immediately after the date such subsequent Bon-owing is made, and may be for a period shorter than the three (3) or six (6) month period elected by the Borrower in order that the Interest Periods of all Borrowings hereunder shall be concurrent, and (iii) thereafter each subsequent Interest Period shall be for an Interest Period and shall end on the same day as the Interest Period with respect to the initial Borrowing hereunder; provided that (a) if any Interest Period would end on a day other than a Business Day, such Interest Period shall be extended to the next succeeding Business Day unless such next succeeding Business Day would fall in the next calendar month, in which case such Interest Period shall end on the next preceding Business Day, (b) any Interest Period that commences on the last Business Day of a calendar month (or on a day for which there is no numerically corresponding day in the last calendar month of such Interest Period) shall end on the last Business Day of the last calendar month of such Interest Period, and (c) no Interest Period shall end after the Term Loan Maturity Date. For purposes hereof, the date of a Borrowing initially shall be the date on which such Borrowing is made and thereafter shall be the effective date of the most recent conversion or continuation of such Borrowing.

clauses.head: "Investment" means purchasing, holding or acquiring (including pursuant
clauses.name: 1.01 “Investment”
clauses.tail: valued at its fair market value at the time of such transfer.
clauses.text: "Investment" means purchasing, holding or acquiring (including pursuant to any merger with any Person that was not a Wholly Owned Subsidiary prior to such merger) any Equity Interests, evidences of indebtedness or other securities (including any option, warrant or other right to acquire any of the foregoing) of, or making or permitting to exist any capital cont1ibution or loans or advances to, guaranteeing any obligations of, or making or permitting to exist any investment in, any other Person, or purchasing or otherwise acquiring (in one transaction or a series of transactions) any assets of any Person constituting a business unit. The amount, as of any date of determination, of any Investment shall be the original cost of such Investment (including any Indebtedness of a Person existing at the time such Person becomes a Subsidiary in connection with any Investment and any Indebtedness assumed in connection with any acquisition of assets), plus the cost of all additions, as of such date, thereto and minus the amount, as of such date, of any portion of such Investment repaid to the investor in cash as a repayment of principal or a return of capital, as the case may be, but without any other adjustments for increases or decreases in value, or write-ups, write-downs or write-offs with respect to such Investment. In determining the amount of any Investment involving a transfer of any property other than cash, such property shall be valued at its fair market value at the time of such transfer.

Each Issuing Bank may, in its discretion but with the consent of Borrower, arrange for one or more Letters of Credit Credit Agreement - 18 - to be issued by Affiliates of such Issuing Bank, in which case the tenn "Issuing Bank" shall include any such Affiliate with respect to Letters of Credit issued by such Affiliate.

clauses.name: 1.01 “LC Disbursement”
clauses.text: "LC Disbursement" means a payment made by an Issuing Bank pursuant to a Letter of Credit following receipt of the required documentation under the Letter of Credit.

clauses.head: "LC Exposure" means, at any time, (a) when
clauses.name: 1.01 “LC Exposure”
clauses.tail: that have not been converted to Term Loans pursuant to Section 2.06(e).
clauses.text: "LC Exposure" means, at any time, (a) when referring to all Letters of Credit, the sum of (i) the aggregate undrawn amount of all outstanding Letters of Credit at such time, plus (ii) the aggregate amount of all LC Disbursements outstanding at such time that have not been converted to Term Loans pursuant to Section 2.06(e); and (b) when referring to the LC Exposure of any Lender in respect of any Letter of Credit that is issued hereunder, the sum of (i) the aggregate undrawn amount of all outstanding Letters of Credit issued by the Issuing Bank (or its Affiliate) for which such Lender is obligated to reimburse LC Disbursements in accordance with Section 2.06(e), plus the aggregate amount of all LC Disbursements outstanding at such time that have not been converted to Term Loans pursuant to Section 2.06(e).

clauses.head: "Lender Affiliate" means (a) with respect to any

clauses.head: "Lender's Pro Rata Interest" means with respect to
clauses.name: 1.01 “Lender's Pro Rata Interest”
clauses.tail: same terms as the required by the Loans.
clauses.text: "Lender's Pro Rata Interest" means with respect to each Lender, on the date that the Borrower is required to make a mandatory prepayment of the Loans in accordance with Section 2.11 (b ), the percentage determined by the quotient of (a) the principal amount of the then Loans outstanding owed to such Lender divided by (b) the sum of (i) the principal amount of the Loans outstanding on such date to all Lenders, (ii) the principal amount of the Supplier Financing, and (iii) the principal amount of any Additional Indebtedness under which the creditors thereof share on a pari passu basis the security interest of the Lenders in the relevant Collateral affected by such mandatory prepayment, on such date, if and to the extent the Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors or the creditors under any Additional Indebtedness on such date require a mandatory prepayment (and not an optional prepayment) on the same terms as the required by the Loans.

clauses.head: "Letter of Credit" means a usance, sight or

clauses.head: "Letter of Credit Facility" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals above.

clauses.text: "Letter of Credit Facility" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals above.

clauses.head: "LIBO Rate" means, with respect to any Eurodollar
clauses.name: 1.01 “LIBO Rate”
clauses.tail: time, two (2) Business Days prior to the commencement of such Interest Period.
clauses.text: "LIBO Rate" means, with respect to any Eurodollar Rate Borrowing for any Interest Period, the rate appearing on the Reuters "LIBOROl" screen displaying British Bankers' Association Interest Settlement Rates (or on any successor or substitute page for such screen, or any successor to or substitute for such service, providing rate quotations comparable to those cmTently provided on such screen, as detern1ined by the Facility Agent, from time to time for purposes of providing quotations of interest rates applicable to dollar deposits in the London interbank market) at approximately 11 :00 a.m., London time, two (2) Business Days prior to the commencement of such Interest Period, as the rate for dollar deposits with a maturity comparable to such Interest Period. In the event that such rate is not available at the time of determination for any other Interest Period for any reason, then the "LIBO Rate" with respect to such Eurodollar Rate Borrowing for such Interest Period shall be the rate at which dollar deposits of five million Dollars (US$5,000,000) and for a maturity comparable to such Interest Period are offered by the principal London office of the Facility Agent in immediately available funds in the London interbank market at approximately 11 :00 a.m., London time, two (2) Business Days prior to the commencement of such Interest Period.

clauses.head: "Market Disruption Event" means an event that Required Lenders

clauses.text: "Market Disruption Event" means an event that Required Lenders determine: (i) by reason of circumstances affecting the London interbank market generally, adequate and fair means do not exist for ascertaining the LIBO Rate for the relevant Interest Period; or (ii) for the relevant Interest Period the Reuters "LIBOOl" screen rate is not available or such screen rate is zero or negative, and none or only one of the Reference Banks supplies a rate to detennine the LIBO Rate for Dollars for the relevant Interest Period; or (iii) for the relevant Interest Period, the cost to such Required Lenders of obtaining matching deposits in the London interbank market would be in excess of the LIBO Rate; or (iv) at any time, deposits in Dollars in the required amount are not available to such Required Lenders.

clauses.name: 1.01 “Material Adverse Effect”
clauses.tail: the rights of or remedies available to the Lenders under the Loan Documents.
clauses.text: "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, financial condition, operations or performance or properties of the Borrower since March 31, 2010, (b) the ability of the Borrower to perform its material obligations under any Loan Document, the transactions contemplated thereby, or with respect to the Project, or (c) the rights of or remedies available to the Lenders under the Loan Documents.

clauses.head: "Permitted Encumbrances" means: (a) Liens for taxes, assessments
clauses.name: 1.01 “Permitted Encumbrances”
clauses.tail: shall not include any Lien securing Indebtedness on Attributable Debt.
clauses.text: "Permitted Encumbrances" means: (a) Liens for taxes, assessments and other governmental charges or levies not at the time delinquent or which are being contested in compliance with Section 5.05 or secure amounts that are not material to the value of the properties to which such Liens attach (it being understood that for purposes of this paragraph (a) all the Mortgaged Properties covered by a single Mortgage shall be deemed to be a single real property); (b) Liens imposed by law, including landlords', carriers', warehousemen's, mechanics', mate1ialmen's, repairmen's and other like Liens imposed by law, arising in the ordinary course of business and securing obligations that are not overdue by more than thirty (30) days or are being contested in compliance with Section 5.05 or secure amounts that are not material to the value of the properties to which such Liens attach (it being understood that for purposes of this paragraph (b) all the Mortgaged Properties covered by a single Mortgage shall be deemed to be a single real property); (c) pledges, deposits or Liens under workmen's compensation laws, unemployment insurance laws, social security laws or similar legislation, or insurance related obligations (including pledges or deposits securing liability to insurance carriers Credit Agreement - 24 - under insurance or self-insurance arrangements), or in connection with bids, tenders, contracts (other than for borrowed money) or leases, or to secure utilities, licenses, public or statutory obligations, or to secure surety, indemnity, judgment, appeal or performance bonds, guaranties of government contracts (or other similar bonds, instruments or obligations), or as security for contested taxes or import or customs duties or for the payment of rent, or other obligations of like nature, in each case incurred in the ordinary coursC'. of business; (d) judgment liens in respect of judgments that do not constitute an Event of Default under clause (j) of Article VII; (e) Liens in favor of issuers of surety, perfonnance or other bonds, statutory obligations, guaranties or letters of credit or bankers' acceptances (not issued to suppo1i Indebtedness or Attributable Debt) issued pursuant to the request of and for the account of Borrower in the ordinary course of its business; (f) encumbrances, ground leases, easements (including reciprocal easement agreements), survey exceptions, or reservations of, or rights of others for, licenses, rights of way, sewers, canals, ditches, water rights, highways, roads, railroads, fences, oil and gas leases, electric lines, data communications and telephone lines and other similar purposes, or zoning, building codes or other restrictions (including minor defects or irregularities in title and similar encumbrances) as to the use of the real properties or Liens incidental to the conduct of the business of Borrower or to the ownership of its properties which do not in the aggregate materially adversely affect the value of said properties or materially adversely interfere with the operations of the business of Borrower (it being understood that for purposes of this paragraph (f) all the Mortgaged Properties covered by a single Mortgage shall be deemed to be a single.real property); (g) contractual Liens which arise in the ordinary course of business under operating agreements, joint venture agreements, partnership agreements, leases, area of mutual interest agreements, royalty agreements, marketing agreements, processing agreements, development agreements, and other agreements which are usual and customary in the mining business; (h) leases, licenses, subleases and sublicenses of assets (including real property and intellectual property rights), in each case entered into in the ordinary course of business; (i) Liens arising by virtue of any statutory or common law provisions relating to banker's Liens, rights of setoff or similar rights and remedies as to deposit accounts or other funds maintained with a depositary or financial institution; (j) Liens arising from Uniform Commercial Code financing statement filings (or similar filings in other applicable jurisdictions) regarding operating leases entered into by Borrower in the ordinary course of business; (k) any interest or title of a lessor under any operating lease; Credit Agreement - 25 - (1) (i) mortgages, liens, security interests, restrictions, encumbrances or any other matters of record that have been placed by any government, statutory or regulatory authority, developer, landlord or other third party on property over which Borrower has easement rights or on any leased property and subordination or similar arrangements relating thereto and (ii) any condemnation or eminent domain proceedings affecting any real property; (m) any encumbrance or restriction (including put and call arrangements) with respect to Equity Interests of any joint venture or similar arrangement pursuant to any joint venture or similar agreement that does not violate the provisions of the LLC Pledge Agreement; (n) Liens on property or assets under construction (and related rights) in favor of a contractor or developer or arising from progress or partial payments by a third paiiy relating to such property or assets; (o) Liens securing or mising by reason of any netting or setoff arrangement entered into in the ordinary course of banking or other trading activities or Liens over cash accounts securing cash pooling arrangements; (p) Liens arising out of conditional sale, title retention, hire purchase, consignment or similar arrangements for the sale of goods entered into in the ordinary course of business; (q) Liens created under the Minnesota State Loan (but not any change in any collateral thereunder or any increase in the amount of Indebtedness in respect of such Lien, other than the capitalization of interest accruing thereunder); and (r) to the extent not included in any of the foregoing clauses, Liens in existence on the date hereof as set forth in Schedule 6.02; provided that, except for Pennitted Encumbrances referred to in clause ( e), (h), U) or (p) above, the term "Permitted Encumbrances" shall not include any Lien securing Indebtedness on Attributable Debt.
